title: Bienfaisance roumaine
text: Bienfaisance roumaine (Satu Mare - 1945) Claude Wainstain, France Article extrait du dossier publié dans L'Arche n° 524-525, octobre-novembre 2001 La suite, pour EFIRO 2008 (mise en page par V. Manta. Merci, M. Wainstain !) Certains naïfs croient encore que la philatélie se résume à collectionner les timbres-poste destinés à affranchir le courrier. Quelle erreur! Feuilletez les catalogues: vous y trouverez une foule de vignettes non postales allant des timbres de prévoyance aux timbres-téléphone, des timbres pour coffres-forts flottants aux timbres de connaissement et des timbres fiscaux aux timbres de bienfaisance, toute une thématique qui peut se révéler riche en histoires et en anecdotes Judaïca. Car on tombe parfois sur des objets étonnants, comme ces timbres de bienfaisance vendus à la fin de la guerre en Transylvanie du Nord, avec la légende "Au profit des déportés" et le nom des villes, Satu-Mare (Szatmar) ou Carei, où ils furent utilisés. Une campagne de charité, en Roumanie, pour aider les Juifs! Ce fait unique en son genre mérite vraiment qu'on s'y attarde. Petit rappel historique: la Transylvanie du Nord, province frontalière éternellement disputée entre la Roumanie et la Hongrie, fut annexée par cette dernière en septembre 1940, ce qui scella le destin des deux cent mille Juifs qui s'y trouvaient. Comme dans le reste de la Hongrie, ils furent massacrés par les "Croix fléchées" hongroises; les survivants furent regroupés dans des ghettos et déportés en quasi-totalité à Auschwitz entre mai et juin 1944. Par contraste, en Transylvanie du Sud, région restée roumaine et pourtant alliée de l'Allemagne, il n'y eut pas de Solution finale. Le dictateur Antonescu qui, au début de la guerre, avait permis à son armée de participer aux massacres de Jassy et d'Odessa, et qui avait livré les Juifs de Bessarabie et de Bucovine, se montra très prudent dès que la situation militaire se dégrada. Grâce notamment aux interventions du Nonce apostolique, du Métropolite de Sibiu et du grand rabbin Safran, les déportations prévues furent plusieurs fois ajournées puis finalement annulées, et les Juifs fuyant la Transylvanie du Nord à travers les Carpates trouvèrent refuge dans les villes roumaines frontalières comme Turda, où des Roumains les aidèrent au péril de leur vie bien avant que la Roumanie ne change de camp. Mais revenons à nos timbres, qui ont été réimprimés à l'occasion d'une exposition philatélique tenue à Cluj en avril 2000. On ne sait pas grand-chose d'eux, sinon qu'il en existe deux sortes, avec et sans Maguen David, qu'on les découpait suivant leur perforation horizontale pour en coller une moitié sur le registre de la mairie et l'autre sur le reçu de l'acheteur, et qu'ils ont aussi servi à l'affranchissement du courrier. Mais on ignore qui a décidé de leur diffusion, combien d'exemplaires ont été vendus et qui les a achetés. Quoi qu'il en soit, ces timbres sont rares et chers, et cette manne qui dort dans les archives de Satu-Mare et de Carei devrait inciter les fonctionnaires municipaux à mieux explorer leurs rayonnages. Pourtant, nul ne le fait. À vrai dire, qui, en Transylvanie du Nord, a envie de se replonger dans le passé? Remerciements à Dan Cosma, Cluj. Le timbre originale. A gauche le timbre réimprimés à l'occasion d'une exposition philatélique tenue à Cluj en avril 2000. Il y a quelques années, dans l'avion pour Budapest, je me suis trouvé assis à côté d'une dame, et la discussion nous a amenés à parler de Satu Mare, dont elle était originaire. Au retour, je lui ai adressé mon article. Quelques mois plus tard, elle m'a envoyé un livre écrit par son mari, ancien déporté, dont la quatrième de couverture reprend en partie mon article. (C. W.) Language

title: THE ROMANIAN POSTAL-HISTORY WEB PAGE
text: THE ROMANIAN POSTAL-HISTORY WEB PAGE ( http://membres.lycos.fr/dgrecu/) Dan Grecu, Romania The primary intention is for this website to be an on-line "magazine" of research and study of Romanian postal history. As a beginning, I list a number of the articles written by me and published by different philatelic publications in Romania, USA, Great Britain and Germany. In addition, I propose to post significant and important articles, written by other contributors . Also, it is intended to provide visitors with a source for other Romanian postal history information including: a short presentation of each magazine or bulletin that had published Romanian postal history articles (when possible, tables of contents will be also provided); a short presentation & review of the books, monographs & catalogues which deals with Romanian postal history matters; bibliographical lists of (hopefully) all books & articles written in the world-wide philatelic press about Romanian traditional philately and Romanian postal history; I think this would be maybe the most useful feature for researchers - when you start to write something on a topic, you HAVE to know what was already written about ! the chronology of the history & postal services in all Romanian territories; some links to Websites which deal with Romanian history and postal history matters; But the main focus will be maintained on a NEW SECTION, the Research Materials , which will provide reference materials (based on expanded aticles or never published materials), online listings and catalogues as a basis for further Postal History studies !!!. It is hoped that this wide presentation of information will attract visitors and stimulate them to become involved in a beautiful and captivating field, namely Romanian postal history. Postal History Articles: Grecu Dan Other Contributors Thematic Index Publications: Stamps Books & Catalogues: Romanian Stamps Catalogues; Foreign Stamp Catalogues ; Postal History Books, Monographs & Catalogue; Romanian Books & Monographs; Foreign Books&Monographs. Magazines & Bulletins: Romanian Philatelic Periodicals 1881-1950. Romanian Philatelic Periodicals 1950- to date. Foreign Philatelic Periodicals Bibliography: Romanian Traditional Philately & Postal History. Or you can go directly to The Foreign Presence in Romanian Postal History Research Materials: Postal History Reference Studies. What's new: 10 March 2008 Language

title: ROMANIAN FREE MILITARY POSTAL STATIONERY
text: ROMANIAN FREE MILITARY POSTAL STATIONERY (1941-1945). A research material based on the article initially published in 'Romanian Postal History Bulletin' No. 13, June 1994. Dan Grecu, România There are two categories of Romanian postal stationery. The one where the rates for mailing were reduced for soldiers quartered in barracks during peacetime, and behind the lines in garrisons and other situations during the war. The other where the cards were free and used by soldiers in front line situations and war zones. In this study only the free stationeries will be discussed as the others are discussed in the existing Romanian catalogues. It is important to appreciate that only about half the mail coming from war zones was written on free stationery items. The other half were written on regular full-postage civilian postcards or used full-postage letters. Until definitive free military stationery (FMS) was issued in June - August of 1941 provisional stationery was used. These were the reduced rate postcards that were overprinted using a mechanical roll or hand impression which read "Gratuit" (Free). P.1 Provisional GRATUIT stationery The definitive FMS for the Romanian army consisted of free military postcards (FMPC) and Campaign / Field Letters (FL). 3.3 In addition to the features of Type 3.1 this card has on the right half of the front an 89 x 15 mm blue rectangular band over the address lines. The black drawing show two children singing Christmas carols on a snow-bound village street. Above this there are two protecting soldiers, one Romanian and one German. Below the text reads, "Romania and Germany, comrades for today and for ever" The color of the card is light cream or dirty white. 3.5. This card provides a dramatic historical reversal to that of 3.3 above. It was issued after September 1944 and has a different front. It has the Kingdoms' arms, printed stamp, title and seal without other features. The multicolored drawing showing Romanian and Russian soldiers stepping across the northern Transylvanian border and attacking a German soldier. The text reads "Long live Romanian-Soviet brotherhood in arms" and "The Romanian army together with the glorious Red army fight to annihilate the invading Hitlerites" Language

title: Penitenciarul Pitest
text: CENZURA PENITENCIARULUI PITESTI CENSORSHIP OF THE PENITENTIARY PITESTI Article published in 'Filatelia', no.3-4 / March-April 1991. Dan Grecu, România În România comunistă, la mare pret s-au situat în colectii si exponate misivele diversilor 'luptători antifascisti' trimise din închisori cu mari semnificatii pentru guvernanti (Târgu Jiu, Doftana, etc). A sosit însă timpul să întregim tabloul universului concentrationar politic românesc cu marele fragment lipsă - 'Gulagul românesc', locuri de detentie si exterminare a zeci de mii de opozanti adevărati si închipuiti ai regimurilor comuniste din tara noastră. Facem o invitatie la cercetarea si publicarea documentelor postale referitoare la acestea prin semnalarea următoarei piese. Este vorba de un întreg-carte postală din 1948, cu marcă fixă tip Stema RPR albastru, nominal 6 lei, carton crem, având aplicată si o marcă IOVR, 1 leu rosu. Este scrisă cu creionul la data de 23 sept. 1948 (după cum rezultă din text). Plecarea din Pitesti, la data de 28 sept. ora 8.00, fapt atestat de stampilele de zi aplicate. Între timp, cartea postală este cenzurată, cu stampila ovală de culoare rosie, cu dimensiunile exterioare de 28 x 19 mm si cu textul: ' Penitenciarul Corectional / CENSURAT / * Pitesti * ', neînsotită de semnătura cenzorului. De mentionat cuvântul 'cenzurat', care în 1948, în timp de 'pace', spune multe... Sosirea la destinatie are loc peste exact o zi, cu stampila de zi Bucuresti 2, 29 sept.1948, ora 8.00. S i o ultimă mentiune: cartea postală prezentată este legată de locul unde, între 1949-1952, se va desfăsura sinistrul 'experiment Pitesti', episod aparte în cadrul terorii nou-instalate în estul european. La data scrierii acesteia însă, abia urma să înceapă strângerea 'cobailor' spre Pitesti. R epublica Populară făcea primii ei pasi hotărâti spre democratia lui Stalin.. . In the communist Romania the documents of the different "antifascist fighters" who were imprisoned (at Târgu Jiu, Doftana, etc.) were especially appreciated in collections and exhibits. The time came to complete the image of the Romanian repressive universe with the big missing piece - "The Romanian Gulag" - the place of detention and extermination of tens of thousands of real or imagined opponents of the communist regimes in our country. We make an invitation toward the research and the publication of the postal documents that refer to this, by presenting the stationary shown above. It is about a postal stationary of 1948, with an imprinted stamp type "Coat of Arms" RRR, blue, face value 6 lei, yellow cardboard, with also a stamp IOVR, 1 leu red. It is written with a pencil on Sept. 23, 1948, as shown by the text. Left Pitesti on Sept. 28, 8:00 AM, as shown by the cancels. Meanwhile the card is censored, and marked by an oval red cancel 'Penitenciarul Corectional / CENSURAT / * Pitesti *', without the censor's signature. Please pay attention to the usage of the word "censored" during peace time... The card arrived a day later in Bucharest, on Sept. 29, 8:00. And a last note: this stationary is related to the place where, between 1949-1952, will take place the horrible "Pitesti experiment", a special moment of the terror that started to be applied. But when this card was sent, the gathering of the future 'guinea pigs' just started. The Popular Republic did her first decided steps toward Stalin's democracy. (Free translation by Victor Manta) Language

title: MULTIPLE AND MIXED CENSORING IN THE BANAT AND TRANSYLVANIA
text: MULTIPLE AND MIXED CENSORING IN THE BANAT AND TRANSYLVANIA -1919 This version was then published in German, in the 'AG Zensurpost Rundbrief' Bulletin no. 87 / 1997. Here an excerpt in English Dan Grecu, România Following WW1, three of the former Austro-Hungarian territories became part of Romania (Bucovina, Transylvania and the Banat). The Romanian administrations were quickly established in each of these areas giving rise to its own local postal history. In all these new provinces civilian mail censorship was established. Romania had complete control of this in Bucovina and Transylvania but in the Banat, two military forces allied to the Romanians, namely the French and Serbs, were interposed between the Hungarian and Romanian troops. The French and Serbs set up censorship offices prior to the arrival of the Romanians. The brief war between Romania and the Hungarian Soviet Republic (April - July 1919) led to the temporary occupation of Hungary and a few censorship offices were set up there. A.1. Romanian double censor markings Double censoring (by both sending and arrival offices). As far as I know, there are no regulations for the re-censoring of the mail in 1919-1920, this apparently happened because of irregular circumstances. Examples of double censoring in OR or MZ are unknown to me, if they exist they are extremely rare. One can usually see double censoring from 'TB' zone, for an example: postmarks from Blaj + Odorhei (July 1920), Zalău + Oradea (July 1920) or Lugoj + Buzias-Băi. A.2. Serbian double censoring There is only one possibility involving censoring offices from today's Romania: TIMIŞOARA and SÂNNICOLAUL MARE B.1.1. Serbian-French Censoring (S-F/ F-S) . Here (below) one finds a combination between a Serb office in BW and a French one in Arad. These covers occur in the following ways. Mail that circulated between BE or BW and Arad (after May 25 censored according to General Tournadre's decree as described above, see #2.3). The mail sent from BE (an area whithout permanent censoring offices) went to one of the BW Serbian censorship offices prior to being forwarded to Arad; this happened particularly during the period December 1918 to January 1919. Some of the BW censorship towns such as Nagy Kikinda / Kikinda, Versecz / Vrsac (see Fig. 1), Nagy Becskerek / Vel.Betschkerek (today Zrenjanin), Pancsevo / Pancevo are outside of present day Romania; however, because of the sending office in BE, such covers are fully interesting for Romanian Postal Historians. B.1.2. French-Romanian censoring (F-R or R-F). This can be found on mail circulated between Arad (French censoring) to the Romanian occupied territories (T, MZ): After May 25 th and until July 10, 1919 the combination should not be found because of the clear delineation of responsibilities between the French and Romanians in Arad (the French were not allowed to censor mail from or to Romanian territories, see #2.3). However, one does find such covers from the first days of July 1919. This was towards the end of the French occupation in Arad, when the decree was not followed. B.1.3. Serbian-Romanian censoring (S-R or R-S). Combinations between Serb markings from BW and Romanian ones from T are quite unlikely during the "a" period and possible during the "b" period (see an example here). Combinations between Serb markings from BW and Romanian ones from OR are unlikely during the ‘a’ period, and possible, but not yet seen during the ‘b’ period (they have to be very rare). Combinations between Serb markings from BW and Romanian ones from MZ are possible too, but we know up to now only the mixture Timisoara + Măru Rosu (Măru Rosu functioned until July 1919 (?) in Mezöhegyes – MZ1, then it was moved to Arad). See an example here. Combinations between Serb markings from BW and Romanian from Lugoj (BE) were possible only for 2-3 months (June-July 1919). We know until now only the combination Timisoara + Lugoj. Not shown here. Language

title: Philatelic Webmastering Event at EFIRO 2008
text: Philatelic Webmasters Event at EFIRO 2008 The Philatelic Webmasters Organization (PWO) is an international philatelic organization that is based in Switzerland and that was created in 2001 by its current president Mr. Victor Manta. Its goal is to encourage the use of advanced information technologies for the promotion and development of philately. Among its over 350 members there are many collectors with a large experience in philatelic webmastering and who are driven by their passion of sharing with others their knowledge of and love for philately. Some of them are also collectors with important philatelic experience, members of prestigious philatelic organizations who are well-known for their competence and have been rewarded with prestigious awards at different philatelic exhibitions. In the year 2008, the most important philatelic event of the last 50 years for the Romania philately, the international philatelic exhibition EFIRO 2008, takes place in Bucharest, the capital of Romania. In collaboration with the Association Internationale des Journalistes Philatélique (AIJP) and the OK of the EFIRO 2008, PWO presents on the following pages an excerpt of many pages published on the WWW, that are dedicated to Romanian philately . Un eveniment al creatorilor de saituri filatelice la EFIRO 2008 Philatelic Webmasters Organization (PWO) este o organizaţie filatelică internaţională bazată în Elveţia, care a fost creată în anul 2001 de preşedintele ei în funcţiune, Dl. Victor Manta. Scopul lui PWO este să încurajeze folosirea tehnologiilor informatice avansate pentru promovarea şi dezvoltarea filateliei. Printre cei peste 350 de membrii ai lui PWO se numără filatelişti cu o vastă experienţă în crearea de saituri filatelice, colecţionari care sunt mânaţi de pasiunea lor de a împărtăşi cu alţii cunoştinţele lor şi dragostea lor pentru filatelie. Unii dintre ei sunt de asemeni colecţionari cu o experienţă filatelică deosebită, fiind bine cunoscuţi pentru competenţa lor, făcând parte din organizaţii filatelice de renume şi fiind recompensaţi cu premii prestigioase la competiţiile filatelice . În anul 2008 se desfăşoară în Bucureşti cel mai important eveniment filatelic al ultimelor 50 de ani din România, expoziţia filatelică internaţională EFIRO 2008 . Î n colaborare cu AIJP şi cu CO al expoziţiei EFIRO 2008, PWO prezintă pe paginile ce urmează extrase ale multiplelor pagini publicate pe Web care sunt dedicate filateliei româneşti. Language

title: Local Issues Satu Mare 1945
text: Local Issues of Satu Mare Jay T. Carrigan, USA Satu Mare / Szatmárnémeti County Satu Mare / Szatmár Early 1945 The Jewish population of Satu Mare was 12,960 in 1941. The Horthy administration at first sent Jews to forced labor camps, but by 1944 the entire Jewish population had been sent to Auschwitz. Only a few hundred survived the war. To raise funds to aid the returning refugees, the municipal council of Satu Mare issued two revenue stamps to be used on legal documents. The stamps were perforated through the middle so that on half could be attached to the legal document and the other to a receipt. The bilingual text on the stamps translates to "For the Deported". title: Local Issues of Northern Transylvania 1944 - 1945
text: Local Issues of Northern Transylvania 1944-1945 Jay T. Carrigan, USA The territory of Transylvania, in the northwestern part of present-day Romania, was incorporated into Hungary until the Treaty of Trianon (June 4, 1920), at which time it was awarded to Romania. As a result of the 2nd Vienna Award (August 30, 1940), the northern portion of this territory was returned to Hungary. Following World War II, it was again incorporated into Romania. These facts alone give this region a rich and interesting postal history. Picture post card to Budapest, with special VISSZATÉRT ("returned") cancel of Kolozsvár (Cluj in Romanian) and separate Sept. 13, 1940 Kolozsvár datestamp. The Hungarian stamp commemorates the return of Northern Transylvania. What is little known, even among philatelists, is that Northern Transylvania achieved a degree of quasi-independence (in civil matters) under the occupation of the Red Army. Romania, one of the Axis powers, surrendered unconditionally on August 23, 1944, shortly after her borders were crossed by Soviet troops. On September 12, 1944, an armistice was concluded in which the USSR promised to return Northern Transylvania to Romania, and Romania agreed to commit its military forces to the allied cause. The 1920 frontier was formally re-established by the peace treaty of February 10, 1947.Soviet and Romanian troops first entered Northern Transylvania on September 21, 1944, and on October 25 finally succeeded in clearing the entire region from the defending Hungarian and German troops. In spite of the armistice agreement, Romanian civil officials were not allowed to assume civil control. The Red Army continued to hold the area under military occupation, granting autonomy to each district in civil matters. Permission to resume civil control over Northern Transylvania was granted on March 11, 1945, and Romanian administration resumed in fact on April 9th. Thus there existed an interregnum period of almost six months, during which Northern Transylvania was neither part of Hungary nor part of Romania, but was also not an independent state. Censored cover dated August 23, 1944 (date of the coup d'état that overthrew the Antonescu government). 8 Oct. 1944 , Romanian forces in Northern Transylvania. Post card from FPO 941 (21st Infantry Division), unit cachet with handwritten censor notation. Language

title: 01 martie 2008
text: László KÁLLAI, România Supratipar cu textul „C.M.T. Român Pocutia” pe mărcile austiece de 1.20/1 kr., 1.20/2kr, 1.20/3 kr şi 4/4 kr. Mărcile din imagine au făcut parte din colecţie regelui Carol al României. Se cunosc doar două serii complete şi atestate. Supratiparul s-a produs în timpul războiului polono-ucrainean, când forţele armate ale României au ocupat fără lupte regiunea, pe care au predat-o mai apoi autorităţilor poloneze. Pentru aprovizionarea oficiilor poştale din timpul ocupaţiei româneşti au fost folosite timbre austriece. În mai 2006 la licitaţia organizată de Cherrystone, mărcile din imagine au fost vândute cu 16.500 USD. Pocuţia (în limbile ucraineană: Покуття, poloneză: Pokucie) este o subregiune istorică a Galiţiei, cuprinsă între râurile Prut şi Ceremuş, în zilele noastre parte a Ucrainei. Din punct de vedere istoric, a fost o regiune culturală distinctă, locuită de români şi de ruteni. Centrul istoric al regiunii a fost oraşul Colomeea. Denumirea regiunii poate fi tradusă prin „lângă colţ”, după numele oraşului Kuti, care la rândul lui înseamnă „colţ”. Iniţial, Pocuţia a fost parte a Rusiei Kievene şi mai apoi a unuia dintre statele sale succesoare, Halici-Volînia. Regiunea a fost anexată în 1349 de regele polonez Cazimir al III-lea. Acesta, în căutarea de fonduri necesare continuării războaielor cu Ordinul Cavalerilor Teutoni, a folosit regiunea drept garanţie pentru împrumutul obţinut din partea domnitorului Moldovei Petru I. Regiunea a fost disputată între cele două state, deoarece sumele împrumutate de regele polonez nu au fost returnate niciodată în întregime. În 1498, regiunea a fost cucerită de Ştefan cel Mare. În 1531, după bătălia de la Obretin, Pocuţia a fost recucerită de polonezii conduşi de hatmanul Jan Tarnowski, care l-a învins pe domnitorul moldovean Petru Rareş. În urma divizării Poloniei din 1772, Pocuţia a devenit parte a Austriei, fiind încorporată în Regatul Galiţiei şi Lodomeriei. După încheierea primului război mondial şi dizolvarea Austro-Ungariei, Pocuţia a fost disputată de Polonia şi efemerul stat Naţional al Ucrainei Occidentale.În timpul războiului polono-ucrainean, forţele armate ale României au ocupat fără lupte regiunea, pe care au predat-o mai apoi autorităţilor poloneze. După războiul polono-sovietic, zona a rămas în cadrul Poloniei. Drept urmare a şi partiţiei Poloniei din 1939 între Germania Nazistă şi Uniunea Sovietică, Pocuţia a fost încorporată în RSS Ucraineană, pentru ca, mai apoi, după declanşarea Operaţiunii Barbarossa, zona să ajungă sub stăpânirea germană. După eliberarea ei de Armata Roşie, zona a rămas în cadrul RSS Ucraineene, iar, în momentul de faţă face parte din regiunea Ivano-Frankovsk, Ucraina. (Surse: Wikipedia, Cherrystone) Language

title: 07 mai 2008
text: László KÁLLAI, România Iuliu Popper, un explorator şi aventurier român, de origine evreiască, s-a născut în 1857 la Bucureşti. La nici 30 de ani, Popper a devenit „Conchistadorul Patagoniei” şi „Don Quijote al aurului Ţării de Foc”. Devine unul dintre cei mai bogaţi oameni ai acelor vremuri, deţine mine de aur, bate monezi de aur pe care îi apare numele şi tipăreşte mărci poştale locale. Tânărul Popper, după studiile din ţară, obţine diploma de inginer al Şcolii Politehnice din Paris. La începutul anului 1886 ajunge la Buenos Aires unde se angajează să facă prospecţiuni ţi studii geologice în vederea exploatării aurului în Ţara de Foc. Zona unde lucrează Popper era necartografiată în acel moment aşa că munţilor, râurilor „descoperite” de el le dă denumiri româneşti. Astfel apare pe harta geografică a lumii Rio Rosetti, Rio Ureche, Vârful Lahovary, Punta Sinaia, Sierra Carmen Sylva. Î n 1891, Iuliu Popper decide să ia în propriile mâini conducerea Ţării de Foc. În acel an el emite după monezi de aur şi mărci poştale. Macheta mărcii poştale, emisă de către Popper a fost realizată de litograful Rodolfo Soukup. Imprimarea colilor de timbre a fost realizată de Atelierul de Timbre a lui J. H. Kidd y Cia din Buenos Aires. Tot aici au fost tipărite mărcile poştale emise de Administraţia Poştala Naţională din Argentina. Grafica mărcii reprezintă simboluri ale mineritului, respectiv ciocanul şi târnacopul, peste care este desenat un soare în centrul acestuia litera „P” de la Popper. Pe laturile desenului apare inscripşia „TIERRA DEL FUEGO” respectiv „DIEZ CENTAVOS ORO LOCAL”, iar în cele patru colturi cifra „10”, reprezentând contravaloarea, adică zece centigrame de aur. Culoarea mărcii este trandafiriu aprins. Se cunosc printuri de probă de culoarea albastră. A fost pusă în circulatie pe aşezările Companiei Popper, precum El Paramo, San Sebastián, Carmen Sylva, şi Rio Grande-Colonia Popper. Timbrul Popper a fost utilizat doar şapte luni în perioada ianuarie-august 1891. Mărcile emise în urmă cu peste un secol de Popper au fost botezate cu timpul „Timbrele Popper” şi sunt râvnite de marii colecţionari. Tirajul mic şi perioada scurtă de circulaţie efectivă a făcut ca exemplarele circulate, alături de mărcile oficiale ale Argentinei, să fie extrem de rare. Probă de culoare din colecţia autorului Ş tampilografie Language

title: My Destryed Bucharest
text: A BUCHAREST, I WILL NEVER SEE AGAIN Victor Manta, a Bucharester from Switzerland I show above, in its full "Disneyland" splendor, the second biggest building in the world, one that appears in the background on the picture on the right. It is still called by the inhabitants of Bucharest "The House of the Fool", or "Dracula's House", even if its official name is today "The Palace of the Parliament." The whole complex was build in the period 1980 - 1990, in a starving country, where food and heating of houses became both luxuries. During that whole period no Western government or a big international organization has vigorously protested against this large scale cultural crime (erasing of the past) committed in Bucharest by the communist government, under the ruling of the communist party and guided by its leader Nicolae Ceausescu. The large street shown on the above picture was called only 17 years ago "The Boulevard of the Victory of Socialism". The big building in the background had the official name: "The House of People". But only twenty years ago there were no traces of these gigantic buildings in Bucharest, the capital of Romania. The area covered by the buildings shown above was a part of the so called Old Bucharest, consisting of small individual houses, several churches, an old market, monasteries and several historical buildings. Some of them are shown on the stamps below. These are two sets, labeled in Michel "Destroyed historical buildings", issued in 1993 (below, Mi. 4859-4861) and 1994 (above, Mi. 4950 - 4953). Please note that most of them are churches and monasteries, the best mean found by the communist regime to wipe out the collective history and traditions of the Romanian people. The numerous inhabitants of old houses, who lived their whole life there, were obliged to accept flats in blocks where hundreds of people lived and where it was easier for the Securitate (secret police) to permanently keep an eye on all of them. Several persons committed suicide, desperate in front of bulldozers attacking their houses, inherited from their parents and grand-parents. Language

title: By the Sea - Nicolae Grigorescu
text: By the Sea - Nicolae Grigorescu Victor Manta, Switzerland The classical Romanian painter Nicolae Grigorescu was born 1838 at Pitaru and died in the year 1907 at Campina. He is considered the founder of the modern Romanian school. He was the first Romanian painter to develop a consistent approach closely linked to a personal style. Grigorescu is renown as the fine painter of the peasants' life in Muntenia (Wallachia), a province of Romania. His canvases inspired by country life capture the national character under various guises and mark the beginning of what was to become a genuine tradition for the artists of the following generations. Probably painted on the French shore of the English Channel, this picture is one of the few sea pieces ever produced by Grigorescu. It was painted between 1880 and 1885. I have discovered it by chance in 2001, during a visit of the National Museum. It suddenly revealed to me the fact that the great classical painter was actually rather our contemporary, and not an artist from a distant past. I liked the image of these beautiful and elegant lady so much that I decided, it should absolutely be displayed on a stamp. The manner in which the atmosphere is rendered, the fluid, transparent quality of the paint, the spontaneous brushwork as well as the character's feature and stance are all reminiscent of Impressionism. Yet in Grigorescu's paintings tonus do not dissolve into the air, the fore-, middle-, and background do not blend, on the contrary, they retain their own individuality. The shore, the sea and the sky are clearly delineated, allowing the onlooker to rejoice at the ambiance. This is yet another proof of the creative war in which the painter assimilated just those features which befitted his own artistic temperament from novel contemporary trends. Meanwhile his approach never relied on the imitation of a particular formula, thereby preserving its own originality. (After Dana Herbay). The stamp, shown on the FDC, as the sheet, will be issued in 2007, in commemoration of artist's death centenary. This is the first set in the world philately that is shown long before its official appearance. The print run of the stamp will be of 300,000 pieces, and as much this stamps, as the 150,000 sheets, will be freely available at post offices. The prices of these stamps will correspond to the level of general prices in 2007, which means that a deflation of the Romanian currency will take place (at 1 Leu = 100,000 old Lei). The stamps were created by the stamp designer Victor Manta, PWO, AIJP, PASIC... Note: written in 2002.The real deflation rate was: 1 New Leu = 10,000 old Lei I had a nice surprise during my recent visit to Bucharest. As usually, I have visited the official philatelic shop, and there I have found the sheet of my dreams. It is exactly the painting that I have shown above, on a sheet, but issued in 2003 and not in 2007. Romanian post, chapeau! Just to mention that Grigorescu has created hundreds of paintings, so that the fact that the Romanian PA and myself have decided ourselves for the same work is a wonderful and remarkable coincidence. Language

title: A sad story - Brancusi
text: A sad story of a work of art Victor Manta, Switzerland Constantin Brancuşi was a Romanian sculptor who trained initially as a carpenter and stonemason. He settled in Paris in 1904 where his early influences included African as well as oriental art. Although Rodin was another early influence, Brancuşi decided he wished to make much simpler work and began an evolutionary search for pure form. While never entirely rejecting the natural world, Brancusi undoubtedly succeeds in conveying a sense of gravity by reducing his work to a few basic elements. Paradoxically, this process also tends to highlight the complexity of thought that has gone into its making. One of his early works, The Wisdom of the Earth (Cumin ţ enia pamântului, 1907) is a reflection of Brancusi's philosophy, that has its roots in a wisdom that is anterior to Christianity. The sculpture shows a woman that is very concentrated on herself, her figure releasing a mystery that transfigures her into an universal portrait. The statue expresses author's feeling of attachment toward the mother Earth but the source of inspiration of his work is actually unknown. This statue, valuing now over 15 million dollars, was confiscated by the communist regime from its owner, the architect Gheorghe Romaşcu, who bought it from Brancuşi in 1910. The heirs of Romaşcu are fighting over through the legal system with the Romanian government for over 15 years. The statue is in custody of the National Museum of Art. The daughter of Gheorghe Romaşcu, Paula Ionescu, explained that the statue was in the possession of her father during 47 years. In the year 1957 the police took the statue "for an exhibition". It was never returned. Later the state officials have invented the story that the statue was bought from Mr. Romaşcu by the state but they never could present the smallest evidence to the justice. Even if Paula Ionescu has documents that prove that she is one of the two legal owners of the work, she got so far (2006), in 15 years, only unfavorable sentences from the Romanian legal system. Now she put her hopes in the Supreme Tribunal, the highest legal instance in Romania, and she is decided to appeal to the High Justice Court in The Haag if necessary. At a certain moment the statue was mounted on a pedestal, under the supervisory of the state specialists. When this was done, the legs of the statue were broken, said Paula Ionescu. Before this accident the statue was evaluated at $ 30 millions but the accident reduced its value to a half. And even now the statue isn't assured by the National Museum of Art...On this page I show different views of the statue, in its original and then in the modified state, as well as the stamp " Cumin ţ enia pamântului ", issued in 1967 (Scott #1917) and the miniature sheet that shows Brancuşi in his atelier, issued in 1982 (Scott #3070). Eventually note that the face of the statue, on the stamp, looks somehow differently when compared with the original (was not intelligent or inspired enough for the "socialist realism"?). Language

title: Farming in the Post WWII Romania
text: Farming in the Post - W.W.II Romania Victor Manta, Switzerland After the W.W.II. Romania was practically occupied by the USSR, that imposed its own (pro-communist, then later entirely communist) government and the unique party system. To "celebrate" the new rulers of the country, Romanian post has issued many stamps with Lenin (first on Jan. 21, 1949, not shown) and even one with Stalin, as perforated and imperforated (see above on the right, Sc. 718, Stalin's 70th birth anniversary). Stalin's portrait is shown because the Romanian government will step by step implement the strategy that Stalin implemented in the Soviet Union, in order to "socialize" the agriculture of his country and to make the farmers, like all other social strata, dependent on the communist state. The first act of the communist government in the farming domain was the agrarian reform law of March 23, 1945. The big land owners (most of them fled the country) were expropriated and their land was distributed to peasantry. The reform was much less extensive that the reform of 1920, but was presented as the final solution of the agrarian problem. Above one can see on the sheet the Prime Minister Petru Groza personally distributing new property documents (sheet issued in June 1946, Mi. Block 31). This measure won for a short time sympathizers and voters for the new government. As usually after such reforms, a famine shortly followed (see the "Help to Starving" sheet). The second act started in 1949, under the ruling of the First Secretary of the Romanian Workers Party, Gheorghe Gheorghiu Dej (see below the stamp, Sc. 1822; the sheet is not shown). The communist party officials, using the forces of the Securitate (Secret Police) and of the army, started by imposing to the majority of farmers the joining of the so called collective farms (named "kolkhoz" in USSR). The farmers were practically deprived of their ground and cattle and were obliged to work together in these units. The recalcitrant who refused to join the collective farms were crudely repressed. The opposition of the peasantry was so important that the government hasn't dared to issue stamps on this subject till 1951/1952, when was issued a set dedicated to the first 5 years plan, a "planning" method overtaken from the big brother and friend, the Soviet Union. The Plan started in 1951 and it failed, like many other similar plans started in other communist countries. But not all of its actions failed, unfortunately. For example on the green 7 Lei stamp (above, the first on the row) one can read: "In 1955 the socialist sector will prevail in the agriculture." This part of the plan will succeed, thanks to the repression of the farmers by the members of the communist party, the secret police (the feared Securitate) and when necessary to the army (the soviet troops being also present on the Romanian soil). The stamp issued in 1956 and labeled "5 years from the founding of collective farms, 1951 - 1956" is one of the most interesting in the Romanian post - W.W.II philately. It was issued on July 23, 1956 and it was withdrawn after only a few days. The authors of the stamps have obviously taken the provisions of the Five Years Plan of 1951 as the starting point of collectivization, and not the earlier decision of the Communist party, that actually started the collectivization of agriculture. On October 18, 1956 the stamp was replaced by a new one, with the exactly same design (not shown, Sc. 1107), marked "7 years of collective farm, 1949 - 1956". On April 27, 1962. was issued a set of 3 stamps (many thanks to Tom from UK for the scans), celebrating the Full Collectivization of the agriculture. This was the third act, the goal of the socialization of the whole Romanian farming being thus attained. The great result of this action will be that Romania, an important exporter of cereals before the W.W.II, will be obliged to import them, in order to feed its population. A miniature sheet (not shown) was issued on June 29, 1982, Sc. 3076. Logically enough, it celebrates the 20th anniversary of the full collectivization of the farming in Romania. But it shows also the beginning of the forth and final farming act of the communist regime - the so called modernization of villages. The idea came from the ruler of the Communist Party, Nicolae Ceausescu, (not) shown together with his wife on a miniature sheet (issued 1985, Scott 3270). He started to move by force the peasantry into blocks of flats, in order to better control it, and to destroy the individual houses. The fall of the Communism in 1989, but also in a certain way the opposition that came from many villages (and less from governments) of Western Europe, the Operation Romanian Villages, that has braked a bit this last plan of the collectivization of the farmers ' life. Language

title: Introduction to Inflation in Romania
text: Victor Manta, Switzerland Introduction to Inflation Introducere la infla ţie The results of the bad politics of the former communist leaders and of some of their later followers can still be perceived also on more recent stamps. Take as an example the stamp displayed on the left (Dacilor Lodge, Brasov, Scott 4219). True, it may look better in the overprinted version of 1998 than the original of 1991, but notice the inflation rate of over 5500%, and the quite suggestive image of the archer who tries, unsuccessfully, to hide the old value. My only objection to the design of the overprint is that the archer should be pointing much higher than the roof! In the Feb. 1999 edition of Scott Stamp Monthly, the stamp above appeared with the very appropriate caption: "Stamps that need all the help they can get". (p. 107). Another example (on the right) is the stamp Abies Alba, issued in 1994 and then overprinted, where the red overprinted rabbit makes a jump from 15L to 4150L (a 27700% increase, or over 5000% per year). Here the rabbit could eventually be replaced by a hawk. I present below an interesting combination of Romanian stamps, received on a postcard. The Airbus A-310 stamp was issued in 1994 and was then overprinted with a dirigible airship, possible in the hope of slowing down the inflation. Notice that the postcard took 5 days to travel from Azuga to Bucharest (130 Km or 78 miles) and other 5 days from Bucharest to Switzerland (about 1500 Km). The first part of the travel was eventually made on the board of a really very slow airship... Rezultatele politicii nefaste a foştilor lideri comunişti şi a unora dintre urmaşii lor pot fi percepute până şi pe timbrele relativ recente. Luaţi ca exemplu Şura Dacilor, Braşov, Scott 4219, prezentat în stânga. Este adevărat, el poate că arată mai bine în versiunea sa supratipărită din 1998 decât originalul din 1999, dar notaţi rata de inflaţie de peste 5500% şi imaginea destul de sugestivă a arcaşului care încearcă, fără mult succes, să ascundă vechea valoare. Singura mea observaţie referitoare la designul supratiparului este că arcaşul ar fi trebuit să ţintească mult deasupra acoperişului. În ediţia din Februarie 1999, p.177, a catalogului american Scott Stamp Monthly, timbrul din stanga sus a aparut subtitrat "Timbre care au nevoie de tot ajutorul posibil pe care îl pot primi. Un alt exemplu este timbrul Abies Alba, apărut în 1994 şi apoi supratipărit, în care iepurele roşu al supratiparului face un salt de la 15L la 4150L (o creştere de 27700%, adică de 5000% pe an). În acest caz iepurele s-ar fi cuvenit să fie înlocuit cu un vultur. Mai jos vă prezint o combinaţie interesantă, primită pe o carte poştală. Timbrul Airbus A-310 a fost emis în 1994 şi a fost apoi supratipărit cu un dirijabil, poate în speranţa să frâneze inflaţia. Steagul european aminteşte poate că aceasta a fost o precondiţie pentru aderarea la EU. Notă: versiunea în limba română a acestei pagini a fost creată pentru EFIRO 2008. Cartea poştală a călătorit 5 zile de la Azuga la Bucureşti (120 Km) şi alte 5 zile de la Bucureşti câtre destinaţia finală Elveţia (circa 1500 Km). Prima parte a drumului a fost probabil efectuată pe un dirijabil care a avut de înfruntat în permanenţă un vânt potrivnic... http://www .marci-postale.com Language

title: MONETARY REFORMS AFTER THE W
text: MONETARY REFORMS AFTER THE W.W.II Victor Manta, Switzerland A period of a relative monetary stability has followed the monetary reform of April 15, 1947, the highest stamp value being of Lei 100, shown on the Transportation stamp, issued on November 22, 1948, Sc. C34, Mi. 1164. You can see an overprinted version of it below, on the second row, on the right. On January 28, 1952 the government has suddenly again deflated the currency, this time without bringing as excuse an earlier inflation period. All the existing money immediately lost its validity, without any transition period. This was the second and the definitive blow of the Communist party (the ruling party and the only one accepted by the Constitution) against its declared "class enemies". The result was that everybody lost his money reserves and became fully dependent of the state and of its jobs (practically the only existing ones). Just to notice that laws, already promulgated earlier, forbade and severely punished the ownership of gold, jewelry or foreign currency. See below on the right the stamp commemorating the new Constitution, that stipulated the rule of the unique party. It was issued issued on April 8, 1948 and it was surcharged together with other stamps in 1952. A limited selection of stamps that were urgently surcharged in the infamous year 1952 is presented above. Some of surcharged stamps of that period are quite scarce (like the Winter Games, the second and the third stamp on the first row, Sc. 847-848, Mi. 1340-1341), because their run was of under 100,000 pieces. The general population and the stamp collectors alike, left without money in their pockets, usually hadn't the means to buy at that time the surcharged stamps. The first not surcharged commemorative set appeared on February 16, 1952 and the first not surcharged definitive set was issued in May 1953. Starting with the surcharged issues of the year 1952, all stamps are postally valid in Romania. A new inflation period started in Romania in 1991, an year after the overthrow of the communist regime. Another page on this site shows the 23 (!) stamps surcharged only during the first 8 months of the year 2000. Language

title: ROMANIAN CURRENCY
text: ROMANIAN CURRENCY AS IT APPEARS ON ROMANIAN STAMPS In the year 1868 a new currency was introduced on stamps, that replaced the older one, from Turkish language, Parale. The name of this currency, one that survived till today, is LEU . Singular: 1 leu (literally means "one lion"). Plural: 2 or more lei The Leu was subdivided into 100 Bani , something that never changed since 1868. Singular: 1 Ban Plural: 2 or more Bani (bani means also "money") 1 leu = 100 bani On the stamps, the name of leu ( lei ) can appear either fully, or abbreviated as L . The abbreviation for ban ( bani ) is b . When Lei appears before the numeric value, it is correct to write: LEI 1 (like LEI 2). It is also correct 1 + 1 LEI for surcharged stamps. On the stamps issued in 1894 and later there are also values written as 1 BANI 1. This can be considered correct, because BANI 1 is correct (even is 1 BANI isn't, the correct form being 1 Ban ). Examples (text) Examples (stamps) Example for bani Example of abbreviation b, B (for bani) Example for 1 Leu Example for LEI Typical example for Lei and subdivisions (1.75) Example for the abbreviation L (for Lei) Example for 1 + 1 LEI The apparently strange, but correct LEI 1. Notes This page is thought as a help for stamp collectors who don't speak the Romanian language. For information about monetary reforms and inflation, as reflected by Romanian stamps, please visit the pages found on the site: www.marci-postale.com Romanian's neighbor Bulgaria, located on the South border, uses a currency with a similar name and the same significance. It was introduced on stamps in 1881 and is named Leva (also "lion"). 1 Leva = 100 Stotinki. Tne name of stotinki comes from Sto, with the meaning 100 in Slavic languages. The first Bulgarian stamps show a stylized lion. Language

title: Romania as Shown by Its Stams
text: Victor Manta, Switzerland Discover this non-commercial site, dedicated to Romania, as seen through its stamps. The site not only shows nice Romanian stamps, but tries to introduce you to this country, to its original culture, its wonderful landscapes and its friendly people. You can find here pages dedicated to Romanian history, thematic collection, postal history and to many other subjects. The author hopes that you will appreciate the quality of the images too. We show at EFIRO 2008 a short selection of multiple pages that belong to this site. Descoperiţi acest sait necomercial, dedicat României, aşa cum este ea văzută prin timbrele ei. Saitul nu numai că arată frumoase timbre româneşti, dar vă şi prezintă această ţară, cultura ei originală, peisajele ei minunate şi oamenii ei prietenoşi. Veţi găsi aici pagini dedicate istoriei României, colecţii tematice, istorie poştală, precum şi multe altele. Sperăm că veţi aprecia şi calitatea imaginilor prezentate pe sait. Prezentăm la EFIRO 2008 o scurtă selecţie a multiplelor pagini care fac parte din acest sait. This site is intended for you, a person who wishes to know more about Romania. It was created and is permanently updated by Victor Manta, a Swiss stamp collector. You can benefit from his experience, because he lived many years in Romania and has a large knowledge of country's culture, language, history, literature, and also its stamps, which he collects since childhood. A long years fan of Romanian topical stamps, he is especially interested in the relationship between the images on Romanian stamps and the tormented history of Romanian people, and by the art and culture in Romania. Unfortunately, Mr. Manta hasn't found the time to consistently translate this site into Romanian. Victor Manta is a former member of the Association of Romanian Philatelists and of the Union of Swiss Philatelic Associations. In the year 1997 Mr. Manta founded PASIC (Paintings and Arts on Stamps Internet Club), counting at time over 800 members from 81 countries, and affiliated since 1999 with the American Topical Association. This club is quite popular worldwide, and especially in Romanian philatelic circles, which is reflected by the fact that the second largest participation at PASIC comes from Romania. Mr. Victor Manta is also the founder of the Philatelic Webmasters Organization (PWO, www.pwmo.org), a site created in 2001, and counting at time over 350 members. It is PWO that organizes, together with AIJP and the OC of EFIRO 2008, the presentation of philatelic websites dedicated to Romanian philately. In the year 2002 this site was awarded the "3-Star Award" by the International Philatelic Association (FIP), at the PhilaKorea Philatelic Exhibition in Seoul. His Arts on Stamps site (www.artonstamps.org), that includes a large chapter on Romanian art (from which some pages are presented at EFIRO 2008), was was also internationally awarded, for example in 2000 by the International Philatelic Association (FIP). In 2003 Mr. Manta created the Communism on Stamps site (http://www.reds-on.postalstamps.biz/), from which he is also presenting excerpts at EFIRO 2008. Language

title: SHOT ROMANIAN PAINTINGS
text: SHOT PAINTINGS Victor Manta, Switzerland The paintings were hit by bullets in December 1989, during the popular uprising against the dictator Ceausescu and the communist regime. On the right side you can see the impact of the bullet (compare with the stamp on the left side, issued in 1968). This masterpiece was painted by Stefan Luchian and represents Old Nicholas, the Cobza-player. In the meantime the painting was restored and can be admired at the National Museum of Art.All stamps of the set mention on the top: Tablouri împuscate = Shot Paintings. The set was issued the October 15, 1990. The print run of the whole set was of 250,000. From left to the right: Ion Andreescu. Woman in White, Stefan Luchian. Safta the Florist, Jan Bruegel the Elder. Vase of Flowers, G.B.Paggi. Madonna and Child. SHOT, THEN OVERPRINTED AND SURCHARGED After about 10 years following the original issue, the first five values of the set were overprinted with a new value of 1700 Lei. It represented the cost of a simple letter sent inside Romania. The old face value was overprinted by the image of a easel, following the "tradition" of recent overprints of the Romanian PA. In order to cheer up the set, I have cancelled it in Bucharest on my birth anniversary day, the 19 of September 2000. Please note that the value of 5 Lei wasn't overprinted, probably because it was out of stock. Only 250,000 pieces were printed, which is a small quantity when compared with the print run of 800,000 to 3,000,000 for other values of the set. I show only the above part of the cover. Below there are affixed other two stamps, in order to attain the value of 12,300 Lei, the price for a letter from Romania to Switzerland. A high price for the Romanian population! Language

title: The Danube - Black Sea Canal. A penitenciary.
text: THE DANUBE - BLACK SEA CANAL Victor Manta, Switzerland The first work on this canal started at the beginning of the 1950's. The freshly installed Communist regime decided eliminating many people it declared as enemies, and silencing the rest of the population at the same time. The Canal was an immense concentration camp, with many thousands of prisoners. During those times a "political" joke was sufficient for rejoining the camps. Some of prisoners were not allowed to even use overcoats during the very cold local winters nor to receive medical aid. A lot of prisoners died of cold, inhuman working and living conditions, and lack of medical attention. In 1951 the post issued in a set dedicated to the 1951-1955 Five Year Plan (a plan that failed miserably, like all others that followed). This sinister enterprise had many points of work. We speak here only about one of them, named Peninsula. This forced work colony existed between 1951-1977, and it was named also the Extermination Camp Nr. 1. It was founded in the fall of 1950, in the North of the lake Siutghiol. on a peninsula that enters the lake, 5 Km away from the village Valea Neagra (Black Valley). Three years later the village was renamed The Light. About 8'000 people worked there (possible not only prisoners). The colony functioned also after the Canal works were closed. See above a post card, sent from the Colonia Peninsula, village Valea Neagră , cenzored by a square cancel with the number 40, passed by the distribution point Constanta the 8th of May.1952 and arrived at Calatele the 11th of May.1952.From the text: please send 4 white undershirts, 2 pairs of tennis shoes or sandals, brush, tooth paste and laundry soap. When you can, send also foodstuff (10 Kg). Stationery and info courtesy of Dan Grecu, Romania. We show its original 6 lei value and the overprinted version of 1952, dedicated to the Danube - Black Sea Canal (Scott 799-818, Michel 1276-1285). On the stamp one can read: "In the year 1955 the Danube - Black Sea canal will be put into operation". Work was stopped in 1953 and, after a parody of a trial, two state-employed engineers, who were not camp internees, were shot for allegedly sabotaging the project. Interestingly enough, for a long period (approximately 1955 - 1990) this stamp was banned from the Romanian catalogues and from the state philatelic commerce. It was a sore reminder of a never finished canal - a project that those in power felt that it should be as soon as possible forgotten, as well as the the bad memories related to it . Thirty years later, more exactly in October 1975, the Romanian President Ceausescu, a loyal follower of those criminals who preceded him as rulers, restarted this megalomaniac project and, spending billions of dollars that his starving country badly needed, succeeded in finishing the works. At the time the project was restarted, water transportation had already begun being replaced by road transport, a development that only accelerated later and made the whole investment useless. The works started on another route, south of the city of Constanta, and they were finished in 1981. Later was finished also the part Poarta Alba - Midia - Navodari, one that practically followed the route of the old Canal. The souvenir sheet presented above on a FDC (1985, Scott 3270, Michel 216) still evokes bad souvenirs to many Romanians. It shows the opening ceremony in Cernavoda, where the former President and the General Secretary of the Romanian Communist Party, Nicolae Ceausescu and his wife Elena (both shot five years later) inaugurated the new canal. Please notice on the material presented above the evolution of the name of the country, from Republica Populara Romana toward the Republica Socialista Romania. Neither translation nor further comments should be necessary but I know that any consistent socialist worldwide will claim that s/he will do it better next time, if s/he gets a new opportunity to demonstrate it. I hope that Romanian people won't ever give such an opportunity, therefore keep in mind US Founding Father, Thomas Jefferson's words: T he price of freedom is eternal vigilance Language

title: VILLAGE MUSEUM AND PEASANT HOUSES
text: VILLAGE MUSEUM AND PEASANT HOUSES (BUCHAREST) Victor Manta, Switzerland Rural life and civilization played a significant part in Romania's past history. In the first centuries AD, the Roman colonization had a rural character and, before the first half of the current century, most of Romania's population lived in a village environment. Farming and village communities were organized in order to cover all everyday demands. Clothes were home-made as well as different tools. The Village Museum is the major attraction of the cultural tourism in Bucharest, the capital of Romania. A creation of sociologist Dimitrie Gusti in 1936, the outdoors museum located in northern Bucharest, on the Herastrau lake shore, with verdure and lakes all around, displays, on the 30 hectares it covers 70 exhibits of households, churches and traditional techniques and devices (water and windmills, oil presses, etc) from all the country's provinces. The originality of the folk creation, the sensibility and care for the beauty of the rural people is shown in the objects found inside their households - carpets, pottery, rugs, icons, furniture. To build up the Village Museum, which Dimitrie Gusti used to call "the very chime of the Romanian nation's anonymous past", the houses were dismantled piece by piece, transported by cart, train, boat etc, and then restored in Bucharest on the Herastrau Lake bank. The oldest houses date from the 17th century, but most of them were built in the 19th century. Houses coming from hill and mountain regions are easy to identify by the raised groundwork (hosting the cellar) unlike plain field houses with their low foundation. Houses from frequently invaded regions are half-buried in the earth. Usually, slant roofs preventing snow stacks indicate northern or mountain areas. The three nice sets shown on this page present peasant houses from Romania. The first set was issued on Dec.25, 1963, Scott No. 1590 - 1596. For the fans: even if the set is older, the stamps are nicely engraved! The second set was issued in July 21, 1986 and commemorates the 50th anniversary of the Open Air Museum of Historic Dwellings in Bucharest, Scott No. 3387 - 3392. The third set was issued on Feb. 8, 1989 and present the architecture of Romanian peasants houses. Only three of the total of six values are shown below on the right. In der Ausstellung werden die Webseiten auf einem HDTV mit einer Diagonale von 106 cm (42") und mit einer Auflösung von 1024 par 768 Pixels vorgestellt. In den meissten Fällen wird die Präsentation ohne menschliche Hilfe laufen müssen. Gerade weil der manuelle Ablauf eher selten verwendet wird, sollten die Seiten den Bildschirm füllen, aber nicht « auslaufen ». Aus diesem Grund sollte die Grösse der Seiten nicht 950 par 550 Pixel (L x H, wie diese Seite) übersteigen. Der Bildschirm wird an einen PC der unter Windows XP läuft angehängt. Aus diesem Grund werden nur Dateien die mit dem Windows-Betriebssystem kompatibel sind akzeptiert. Die Präsentation wird im Internet Explorer 7 Browser ablaufen. Drücken Sie hier für einen kleinen Beispiel der Präsentation. Sie können testen wie Ihre Seiten auf dem grossen Bildschirm erscheinen werden. Dafür stellen Sie die Auflösung Ihres Computerbildschirmes provisorisch auf 1024 mal 768 Pixel um. Bitte berücksichtigen Sie die Tatsache, dass auf einem grossen Bildschirm die Bilder um einiges grösser als auf dem Computerbildschirm erscheinen. C liquez sur l 'affiche en bas svp., pour suivre la présentation (s'ouvre dans une nouvelle fenêtre; des consei lls d'utilisations se trouvent sous l'affiiche ). La présentation se déroule en mode automatique. Déplaces svp. le curseur en dehors de l'image pour que le menu disparaisse. Pour passer au mode manuel cliquez sur n'importe quel ligne du menu, qui s'affiche a gauche. Pour retourner à la présentation automatique, cliquez sur Play en bas du menu. Sur ma site Romania as Seen by its Stamps j'ai publié un récit de mon activité a EFIRO 2008. Elle est ici . Lien: PWO press release Created: 05/05/07. Revised: 08/22/10 . title: Prezentarea lui PWO la EFIRO 2008
text: Participa rea cu pagini Web la Expoziţia Mondială de Filatelie EFIRO 2008 English , Français Victor Manta, PWO, AIJP, Elveţia Philatelic Webmasters Organization (PWO), în colaborare cu AIJP şi cu CO, a organizat la Expoziţia Mondială de Filatelie EFIRO 2008 (Bucureşti, România, 20 - 28 iunie) o prezentare a unor extrase din saiturile filatelice dedicate filateliei româneşti. Creatorii de pagini web au fost contactaţi de către PWO şi au acceptat cu entuziasm să participe la acest eveniment important, legat de a 150-a aniversare a apariţiei primelor mărci poştale româneşti, faimoasele Capete de Bour. Prezentarea a avut loc loc la EFIRO 2008 într-un loc perfect, în proximitatea Curţii de Onoare şi a Muzeului Filatelic, pe o suprafaţă de 45 m2. PWO a oferit tuturor colecţionarilor de timbre care sunt interesaţi ocazia să participe la o expoziţie filatelică mondială, cu pagini dedicate filateliei româneşti Paginile web participante au putut aborda oricare capitol al bogatei filatelii româneşti. Ele au prezentat imagini scanate de material filatelic, precum şi texte explicative. Limbile acceptate pentru texte au fost engleza, franceza, germana şi româna. Participarea a fost gratuita . Nu s-a cerut ca participanţii să facă parte din vreo organizaţie filatelică. Dreptul de autor aparţine atât autorilor paginilor, cât şi lui PWO, care afişează de manieră permanentă prezentarea pe saitul ei. Clicaţi pe afisul de mai jos pentru a accesa prezentarea. Ea va aparea intr-o noua fereastra. Prezentarea se derulează în mod automat. Îndepartaţi c ursorul de pe imagine şi meniul din stânga va dispare. Clicând pe orice punct de pe meniu prezentarea va comuta în modul manual, ceea ce permite accesul direct la orice pagină, pentru un timp nedeterminat. Vă puteţi întoarce la prezentarea automată apăsând pe butonul Play care se află în partea de jos a meniului. Pe situl meu intitulat România vazuta prin timbrele ei am publicat o relatare despre activitatea mea la EFIRO 2008. O gasiti aici . Legături: Anunţul de presă al PWO . title: PWO-AIJP-EFIRO2008/OK Ereignis an der EFIRO 2008
text: PWO & AIJP geben ein Webmastering Ereignis an der EFIRO 2008 bekannt Română Die Briefmarkenwebmaster-Organisation (PWO) ist eine internationaler philatelistische Organisation, dessen Sitz in der Schweiz ist und welche im Jahre 2001 durch seinen gegenwärtigen Präsident Herr Victor Manta gegründet wurde. Seine Absicht ist, den Gebrauch fortgeschritten Informationstechnologien für die Promotion und die Entwicklung der Philatelie zu fördern. Unter den mehr als 350 Mitglieder befinden sich viele Sammler mit einer großen Erfahrung in philatelistischem webmastering, welche Ihre Kenntnisse und Leidenschaft für Philatelie mit anderen teilen möchten. Einige von ihnen sind auch Sammler mit grosser Briefmarkenerfahrung, Mitglieder von berühmten Briefmarkenorganisationen, welche für ihre Kompetenz wohl bekannt sind und mit verschieden Preisen belohnt wurden, einschließlich jene welche an FIP Websiten-Wettbewerben erhalten wurden. Ddie internationale Briefmarkenausstellung EFIRO 2008 wird das wichtigste Briefmarkenereignis der letzten 50 Jahre in Rumänien sein. Sie wird Bukarest, der Hauptstadt Rumäniens, stattfinden. Diese Ausstellung wird den 150. Jahrestag des ersten Moldavischen Marken, die berühmten Ochsen-Köpfe gedenken. Die PWO schlug den Beginn und die Koordination einer Ausstellung von Briefmarkenseiten am EFIRO 2008, Seiten welche der rumänischen Philatelie gewidmet sind. Diese Initiative wurde von Herrn Wolfgang Maassen, dem Präsidenten des Internationalen Verbandes Philatelistischer Journalisten (AIJP), unterstützt. AIJP und PWO sind überzeugt, dass das Interesse für das Briefmarkensammeln durch die Popularisierung von Briefmarkenseiten, welche Rumänische Briefmarken als Ziel haben, beträchtlich steigern wird und dass die Vorstellung der erwähnten Briefmarkenseiten an dieser internationalen Ausstellung einen wichtigen Einfluss sowohl auf die rumänischen Philatelie wie auch auf den philatelistischem Webmastering haben wird. Die Nachfolgende Daten illustrieren das Interesse für die Anwesenheit im Web der rumänischen Philatelie: Die PWO zählt zur Zeit fünf rumänischeMitglieder auf Die Seite des FFR (rumänische Briefmarkenföderation) präsentiert sechs Seiten, welche der rumänischen Philatelie gewidmet sind Auf den Webseite www.marci-postale.ro veröffentlicht Herr Manta 24 Verbindungen zu den rumänischen Briefmarken gewidmeten Seiten. Deren Zahl ist eigentlich höher. Im Monat April 2007 genehmigte das Organisationskomitee von EFIRO 2008 das von der PWO vorgeschlagene Projekt. Eine Sitzung zwischen Hauptmitgliedern des OC (Frau Simona Tarabasanu und Herr Cosmin Mateescu) und der PWO fand im Monat Mai 2007 in Bern am Internationalen Büro des UPU statt. Während dieser sehr wirksamen Sitzung einigten sich die Teilnehmer über ihre Absichten und auf die verschiedenen Mittel zum rechtzeitigen Erzielen des Projektes. Die nachfolgenden Schritte, welche von den Veranstaltern des Ereignisses genommen werden sollen, (PWO, AIJP, OC - EFIRO 2008) sind: diese Pressemitteilung auf ihren jeweiligen Seiten und in ihrem gedruckten Meldungen zu veröffentlichen sich in Verbindung zu der Briefmarkenpresse, newsgroups und den anderen Medien zu setzen, um das Prokekt bekannt zu machen. sich direkt mit den Autoren von verschiedenen Briefmarkenseiten in Verbindung zu setzen, welche der rumänischen Philatelie gewidmet sind, und ihnen vorzuschlagen, an der Veranstaltung teilzunehmen. Wir sind überzeugt, dass sich Webmaster solcher Seiten zur Teilnahme erfreuen werden. allen interessierten Briefmarkenwebmastern weltweit vorzuschalgen, an dieses Ereignis mit neuen, der rumänischen Philatelie gewidmeten Webseiten, teilzunehmen. Die Präsentation in EFIRO 2008, wird auf einem Computer mit einem großen Bildschirm vorgestellt, in einer außergewöhnlich für diese Tätigkeit gut passenden Lage. Ein Poster in der Nähe vom Monitor wird Basisinformationen über das vorgestellte Objekt bekanntgeben. Die Präsentation wird auf der PWO Seite am Ende der Ausstellung verfügbar bleiben. Der PWO Präsident, Herrn Victor Manta, wird die Besucher auf EFIRO 2008 persönlich begleiten, um (in Rumänisch, Deutsch, Französisch, Englisch und Russisch) die kompilierte Darstellung der rumänischen philatelistischen Seiten ihnen zu erklären. Die Besucher werden von seine Kenntnissen profitieren können, da er selber philatelistisch auf im Web seit 1996 tätig ist und diese Angelegenheit wohl sehr gut kennt. Die interessierten Briefmarkensammler sind bereits eingeladen an dieser Veranstaltung teilzunehmen und dieses e-mail zu benutzen, um sich anzumelden. Genauere Informationen über die Darstellung selber wird in Kürze auf der PWO Website veröffentlicht werden. title: Evènement commun PWO-AIJP-EFIRO2008/OK a EFIRO 2008
text: PWO & AIJP annoncent un évènement de Webmastering philatélique a EFIRO 2008 Română L'Organisation des Webmasters Philatélistes (PWO) est une organisation philatélique internationale qui est basé en Suisse et a été créé en 2001 par son président actuel M. Victor Manta. Son but est d'encourager l'utilisation de technologies avancées d'information pour la promotion et le développement de philatélie. Parmi ses plus de 350 membres il y a beaucoup de collectionneurs avec une grande expérience dans le webmastering philatélique, motivés par le partage de leurs connaissances avec d'autres philatélistes et de transmettre la passion pour la philatélie qui est leur. Certains d'entre eux sont aussi des collectionneurs avec une grande expérience philatélique, membres d'organisations philatéliques prestigieuses, célèbres pour leurs compétences et ont été récompensés avec différents prix, en incluant ceux reçus aux compétitions de sites Internet par la FIP. En 2008, l'événement philatélique le plus important des 50 ans derniers, l'exposition philatélique internationale EFIRO 2008, a eu lieu à Bucarest, la capitale de la Roumanie. Cette exposition commémorera le 150ème anniversaire des premiers timbres de Moldavie, les illustres Têtes de Boeufs. La PWO a récemment suggéré le début et la coordination d'une activité constuée par la présentation de pages de philatélistes dévouées à la philatélie roumaine à 2008 EFIRO. Cette initiative est soutenue par M. Wolfgang Maassen, le Président de l'Association Internationale des Journalistes Philatélique (AIJP), une organisation qui traite cet événement avec condescendance. AIJP et PWO sont convaincus que l'intérêt pour la collection de timbres sera considérablement augmenté par la popularisation de sites philatélistes qui ont comme sujet les timbres postaux roumains et que la présentation des sites philatélistes mentionnés à cette exposition internationale aura un impact important tant sur la philatélie roumaine que webmastering philatéliste dans le monde entier. les données suivantes illustrent l'intérêt de la philatélie roumaine pour la présence sur le Web : la PWO compte en ce moment cinq webmasters philatélistes roumains Le site du FFR (Fédération Philatélique Roumaine) présente six sites dévoués à la philatélie roumaine Sur le site de timbres www.marci-postale.com M. Manta publie 24 liens vers les sites dédiés aux timbres roumains. Leur nombre est actuellement plus élevé. Le mois d'avril 2007, le Comité d'Organisation de 2008 EFIRO a approuvé le projet proposé par la PWO. Une réunion entre de principaux membres de l'OC (Mme Simona Tarabasanu et M. Cosmin Mateescu) et la PWO est survenue dans le mois de mai de 2007 à Berne, au Bureau international de l'UPU. Pendant cette réunion très efficace, les participants ont manifesté de façon significative leur accord sur leurs buts et sur les différents moyens d'accomplissement de ceux-ci dans le temps. Les étapes suivantes à franchir par les organisateurs de l'événement (PWO, AIJP, OC - EFIRO 2008) sont: de publier ce communiqué de presse sur leurs sites respectifs et dans leurs communiqués de contacter la presse philatéliste, les newsgroups et d'autres mass-média pour vulgariser ce projet de contacter directement les auteurs de différents sites dévoués à la philatélie roumaine et leur suggérer de participer à l'évènement. Nous sommes convaincus que les webmasters de ces sites seront heureux de participer de suggérer à tout webmaster philatéliste intéressé dans le monde entier de participer à cet événement, avec de nouvelles pages Web dévouées à la philatélie roumaine La présentation surviendra à 2008 EFIRO, sur un ordinateur avec un grand écran, dans un endroit exceptionnel et convenable pour cette activité. Un poster près du moniteur fournira des renseignements de base sur ce qui est présenté. La participation sera gratuite pour tous. La présentation restera disponible sur le site PWO après la fermeture de l'exposition. Le président de la PWO, M. Victor Manta, montrera personnellement aux visiteurs à 2008 EFIRO (en roumain, allemand, français, anglais russe) la présentation compilée de pages philatéliques roumaines et discutera avec eux sur l'activité philatélique sur le Web, qu'il connait très bien puisqu'il y a participé depuis 1996. lLs collectionneurs de timbres intéressés sont déjà invités à permettre au PWO d'être au courant de leur intention de participer. Les renseignements plus spécifiques sur la présentation elle-même seront publiés bientôt sur le site PWO. . title: Eveniment de Philatelic Webmastering la EFIRO 2008
text: PWO şi AIJP anunţă un eveniment special la EFIRO 2008 English Philatelic Webmasters Organization (PWO) este o organizaţie filatelică internaţională bazată în Elveţia, care a fost creată în anul 2001 de preşedintele ei în funcţiune, Dl. Victor Manta. Scopul lui PWO este să încurajeze folosirea tehnologiilor informatice avansate pentru promovarea şi dezvoltarea filateliei. Printre cei peste 350 de membrii ai lui PWO se numără filatelişti cu o vastă experienţă în crearea de saituri filatelice, colecţionari care sunt mânaţi de pasiunea lor de a împărtăşi cu alţii cunoştinţele lor şi dragostea lor pentru filatelie. Unii dintre ei sunt de asemeni colecţionari cu o experienţă filatelică deosebită, fiind bine cunoscuţi pentru competenţa lor, făcând parte din organizaţii filatelice de renume şi fiind de asemeni recompensaţi cu premii importante la competiţii de saituri filatelice, de exemplu de cele organizate în trecut de FIP. În anul 2008 se va desfăşura în Bucureşti cel mai important eveniment filatelic al ultimelor 50 de ani din România, expoziţia filatelică internaţională EFIRO 2008 ( www.efiro2008.ro ). Această mare expoziţie va comemora aşa cum se cuvine a 150-a aniversare de la emiterea primelor mărci poştale ale Moldovei, renumitele Capete de Bour. PWO a propus recent ca ea să pornească şi să coordoneze o activitate care să fie finalizată printr-o prezentare a unor pagini filatelice Web, dedicate filateliei româneşti, la EFIRO 2008. Această iniţiativă este sprijinită de Dl. Wolfgang Maassen, preşedintele lui Association Internationale des Journalistes Philatélique (AIJP - www.aijp.org ), o organizaţie care sprijină activ EFIRO 2008. AIJP şi PWO îşi exprimă convingerea că interesul pentru colecţionarea de mărci poştale va putea fi crescut prin popularizarea saiturilor filatelice care au ca subiect mărcile poştale româneşti şi că prezentarea de pagini filatelice la această importantă expoziţie filatelică internaţională va avea un impact pozitiv atât asupra filateliei româneşti, cât şi asupra activităţii de creare de pagini filatelice pe Web. Următoarele date ilustrează interesul pentru prezenţa pe Web a filateliei româneşti: PWO numără în acest moment printre membrii ei cinci webmasteri filatelici Saitul Federaţiei Filatelice Române ( www.federatia-filatelica.ro ) prezintă şase saituri dedicate filateliei româneşti Pe saitul său dedicate filateliei româneşti, www.marci-postale.ro , dl. Manta publică nu mai puţin de 24 de linkuri către situri/pagini dedicate mărcilor poştale româneşti. Numărul acestora este desigur mai mare. În luna aprilie a anului 2007, Comitetul de Organizare (CO) a expoziţiei EFIRO 2008 a aprobat proiectul menţionat mai sus, propus de PWO. O întâlnire dintre membri cu înalte responsabilităţi ai CO (D-na Simona Tărăbăşanu şi Dl. Cosmin Mateescu) şi PWO a avut loc în luna mai a anului 2007 la Berna, la sediul Biroului Internaţional al Uniunii Poştale Universale. Pe parcursul acestei întâlniri prieteneşti şi deosebit de eficiente au fost definite scopurile urmărite şi au fost stabilite modalităţile prin care acestea vor fi atinse în perioada de timp rămasă până la deschiderea expoziţiei. Cei trei organizatori ai evenimentului (PWO, AIJP, CO - EFIRO 2008) vor întreprinde următoarele acţiuni concrete, în termen scurt şi mediu: Vor publica prezenta Informaţie de Presă pe saiturile lor filatelice şi în buletinele lor imprimate Vor contacta presa filatelică, newsgroup-urile şi alte media filatelice pentru a populariza prezentul eveniment Vor contacta direct pe autorii diferitelor saituri filatelice, dedicate filateliei româneşti, şi le vor propune să participe la eveniment. Suntem convinşi că webmasterii respectivi vor participa cu interes şi plăcere. Vor propune tuturor amatorilor de filatelie să participe la prezentare cu pagini Web dedicate filateliei româneşti Prezentarea paginilor Web reunite va avea loc în cadrul expoziţiei EFIRO 2008, pe un monitor de dimensiuni importante, conectat la un calculator, şi se va desfăşura într-un spaţiu potrivit pentru această activitate. Un poster de mari dimensiuni va furniza o informaţie de bază asupra evenimentului. Participarea la prezentare va fi gratuită pentru toţi webmasterii. Prezentarea va continua să fie accesibilă de pe saitul lui PWO şi după închiderea expoziţiei. Preşedintele lui PWO, Dl. Victor Manta, va prezenta în persoană, în cadrul lui EFIRO 2008, in limbile română, germană, franceză, engleză sau rusă, după caz, atât compilarea paginilor Web, cât şi activitatea filatelică de pe Web, pe care o cunoaşte foarte bine, deoarece participă la ea din anul 1996, cu numeroase sale saituri filatelice. Filateliştii care sunt deja interesaţi să participe, sunt invitaţi sa îi facă cunoscută lui PWO intenţia lor de a lua parte la eveniment, folosind această adresa . O informaţie detaliată, precum şi formulare de participare, vor fi publicate în curând pe saitul PWO.
