title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Morocco | PWO
text: ← UPU Circulars by Country Version française → Illegal Stamp Issues from Morocco Morocco - Illegal Issues of Postage Stamps UNIVERSAL POSTAL UNION Berne, 10 April 2000 International Bureau Circular 129 Dear Sir/Madam The postal administration of MOROCCO asks me to inform you of the following: "Our administration has been informed of the existence of postage stamps bearing the inscription 'République Arabe Sahraoui Démocratique' and various designs. "We would like to point out that this so-called republic does not exist, that all these stamps are illegal and that their circulation does harm to the international postal service and to collectors. "In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Acts of the Universal Postal Union, these stamps may not be accepted as a means of prepayment of postage for mail." Yours faithfully, M S RAMAN Assistant Director-General UNIVERSAL POSTAL UNION Berne, 18 November 2002 International Bureau Circular 414 Dear Sir/Madam The postal administration of MOROCCO asks me to inform you of the following: The postal administration of Morocco deplores the fact that illegal postage stamp issues inscribed "République sahraoui" (Saharan Republic) or "Sahara Occidental" (Western Sahara) are still circulating on the international philatelic market, and being sold through various Internet sites and philatelic publications. We wish to stress once again that this alleged republic does not exist, and that all these postage stamps are illegal. The illegal issues of which we are aware are summa­rized below: – Three souvenir sheets commemorating various aspects of the life of the singer Elvis Presley. Each sheet contains one postage stamp with a face value of 200 ptas. – One miniature sheet of nine postage stamps commemorating various aspects of the life of the singer Elvis Presley. The face values are 20, 29, 40, 58, 105, 136, 148, 163 and 175 pesetas respectively. – Three souvenir sheets commemorating various aspects of the life of the actress Marilyn Monroe. The face values of these sheets are not known. – One miniature sheet of nine postage stamps commemorating various aspects of the life of the actress Marilyn Monroe. The face values are 20, 29, 40, 58, 105, 136, 148, 163 and 175 pesetas respectively. – One souvenir sheet (with a face value of 200 ptas) and six individual stamps (with face values of 28, 29, 40, 68, 105 and 136 ptas) depicting various breeds of dog. – One souvenir sheet (with a face value of 200 ptas) and six individual stamps (with face values of 28, 29, 40, 68, 105 and 136 ptas) depicting various types of fire-fighting vehicles. – One souvenir sheet (with a face value of 200 ptas) and six individual stamps (with face values of 28, 29, 40, 68, 105 and 136 ptas) depicting various types of old cars. – One series of five postage stamps on the theme of Galileo and space. – One miniature sheet and a series of five postage stamps on the theme of the 1996 Olympics. – Another series of five postage stamps depicting various athletes from the 1990 Olympics. – One series of five postage stamps depicting various desert cacti. – One miniature sheet depicting camels. – One miniature sheet depicting a football world cup. – One miniature sheet depicting scenes from Ancient Egypt. These stamps have been issued in contravention of the Universal Postal Conven­tion and the Letter Post Regulations and are prejudicial to the integrity and sover­eignty of our country. Consequently, we regard these illegal issues as null and void and worthless whether for postal prepayment or as philatelic or collector's items. The postal administration of Morocco would be grateful for any information leading to the identification of those responsible for these illegal issues so that appropriate action may be taken. We also take this opportunity to confirm that the official postage stamps of Morocco are to be found on our site www.bam.net.ma . Yours faithfully, K J S McKEOWN Director of Markets More information about the illegal issues can be obtained directly from the UPU, Mrs. Maria Libera . Published: 09/15/2001. Revised: 12/07/02 . title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Myanmar | PWO
text: ← UPU Circulars by Country Version française → Illegal Stamp Issues from Myanmar Myanmar - Illegal Issues of Postage Stamps UNIVERSAL POSTAL UNION Berne, 25 November 2002 International Bureau Circular 428 Dear Sir/Madam The postal administration of MYANMAR asks me to inform you of the following: "Our administration would like to draw your attention to the presence on the philatelic market of illegal stamps bearing the inscription 'Union of Myanmar'. "These stamps, with a face value indicated in Myanmar kyats, have not been issued by the Ministry of Communications, Posts and Telegraphs, the sole body entitled to issue stamps in the name of the Union of Myanmar. They must therefore be regarded as illegal stamps." The list of illegal postage stamps appears in the annex. title: Illegal Stamp Issues at Philakorea
text: Illegal stamps (labels purporting to be real stamps) remained in the news in 2004. The International Bureau of the Universal Postal Union continued its announcements of labels that UPU member countries deem to be not their issues. In February, for the African nation Benin, the UPU issued a 30-page list. In January, dealer Algiras Satas of Lithuania (Conquest Trading Co.), seller in 2002 of the witty Island of Freedom labels picturing the South Korean soccer team, was booted out of a stamp show in Hong Kong for offering items the show organizers deemed to be illegal stamps. In July, the editors at Scott Publishing Co. announced they still would not be listing new issues of Liberia, even though in spring a Liberian minister mailed a flurry of stamp-bearing envelopes to Scott and to Linn's . The 2000 edition of the Scott Standard Postage Stamp Catalogue , published in 1999, was the last edition to list any new Liberian stamps. Source: http://www.linns.com/features/openalbum/openalbum.asp?uID= Something begins to move in the domain of illegal stamps. Please see below the e-mail that the PWO received from Mr. Knud Mohr, the President of the FIP, answering our inquiry of July 13, 2002. Dear Mr Victor Manta, Thanks for your mail and for your information about PWO and your activities against illegal stamps. For your information, I enclose the letter which the UPU on behalf of WADP and its partners have sent to the Organising Committee of PHILAKOREA 2002. I believe you find it talks for itself and that whatever action needed in the fight against illegal issues will be used. With my best regards Knud Mohr (July 14, 2002) NO Illegal Issues of Postage Stamps at Philakorea 2002 UNIVERSAL POSTAL UNION Berne, 12 July 2002 International Bureau, Fax PHILAKOREA 2002 Organizing Committee 154-1, Serin-dong, Jongno-gu SEOUL 110-110 KOREA (REP) Fax : +82 2 2195 1485 Subject: Presence of standholders selling illegal stamps at PHILAKOREA 2002 Dear Mr. Oh: I am writing to you on behalf of the World Association for the Development of Philately (WADP)*. It has been brought to the attention of the WADP that certain standholders may be planning to sell illegal stamps at PhilaKorea 2002. The WADP wishes to reiterate its conviction that the production, distribution and sale of illegal stamps have a serious negative impact on Posts and the philatelic market as a whole. That is why the WADP calls on all industry participants to do everything possible to curb this illegal practice. To this end, the WADP urges the PhilaKorea Organising Committee to deny exhibition access to any standholder found offering illegal stamp issues for sale.. Furthermore, at the request of the International Federation of Philately (FIP) and the International Federation of Stamp Dealers Associations (IFSDA) the WADP wishes to advise that dealers who offer for sale illegal stamp issues at philatelic exhibitions will be barred from participating in future FIP exhibitions and IFSDA-sponsored philatelic events. The WADP is in contact with other philatelic exhibition organisers who have had negative experiences with certain standholders. We will be pleased to bring to your attention any information we receive on this subject, should you so wish. We wish PhilaKorea 2002 every success. Yours sincerely (Signed) K.J.S. McKeown WADP Secretary More information about the illegal issues can be obtained directly from the UPU, Mrs. Maria Libera . Published: 07/14/2002. Revised: 12/19/04 . title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Russian Federation | PWO
text: ← Circulaires UPU par pays English original → Illegal Stamp Issues from Russian Federation Russie (Fédération de) Emissions illicites de timbres-poste UNION POSTALE UNIVERSELLE Berne, le 14 janvier 2002 Circulaire du Bureau international 15 Madame, Monsieur, L'administration postale de la FÉDÉRATION DE RUSSIE me prie de vous communiquer ce qui suit (traduction de l'anglais): «En sa qualité de membre de l’Union postale universelle, l’administration postale de la Fédération de Russie émet des timbres-poste dans le respect des dispositions de la Convention postale universelle et du Règlement de la poste aux lettres. Toutefois, récemment, on a constaté l’apparition sur les marchés philatéliques mondiaux d’un grand nombre d’émissions illicites diffusées au nom d’entités territoriales officielles de la Fédération de Russie. Ces émissions couvrent des thèmes «populaires», tels les personnalités politiques, les grands sportifs, les vedettes de Hollywood, etc. L’administration postale de la Fédération de Russie attire votre attention sur le fait que les régions au nom desquelles les émissions concernées ont été faites font partie intégrante de la Fédération de Russie et que, selon les dispositions des Règlements de l’UPU et de la législation de la Fédération de Russie, elles ne sont pas habilitées à effectuer des émissions de timbres-poste indépendantes (la liste de ces régions figure en annexe). Compte tenu de ce qui précède, toutes les émissions faites au nom d’entités territoriales officielles de la Fédération de Russie doivent être considérées comme illicites. Elles n’ont aucun rapport avec la poste et ne sauraient être utilisées comme moyen officiel d’affranchissement confirmant le paiement pour le service postal. L’émission de ces contrefaçons est effectuée par des sociétés privées anonymes opérant hors de la Russie et n’a pas de lien direct avec les entités territoriales officielles de la Fédération de Russie. La diffusion de timbres-poste illicites porte un grave préjudice moral et économique à la Fédération de Russie, discrédite le service postal russe aux yeux de la communauté philatélique mondiale et incite les collectionneurs à éviter d’acheter non seulement les émissions illicites, mais aussi celles qui sont parfaitement légales.» Veuillez agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'assurance de ma haute considération. Le Directeur de la communication et des marchés postaux, K.J.S. McKEOWN Annexe Liste des régions de la Fédération de Russie au nom desquelles des timbres illicites ont été émis Région de l'Altaï Province de l'Amour Régions antarctiques de la Fédération de Russie République autonome juive Archipel François-Joseph District autonome d'Evenkie République de Kabardino-Balkarie Région du Kamchatka République des Karachaïs-Tcherkesses District autonome de Koryak Iles Kouriles Iles Novossibirsk Ile de Kolguev Ile de Kunashir Nouvelle-Zemble Ile de Spitzberg République d'Adygha République du Bachkortostan République de Bouriatie République du Daghestan République d'Ingouchie République d'Ichkérie République de Kalmoukie République de Carélie République des Komis République des Maris République de Mordovie République Sakha (Yakoutie) République d'Ossétie du Nord République du Tatarstan République de Touva République de Khakassie Région de Sakhaline République d'Oudmourtie République de Tchétchénie République de Tchouvachie Published: 09/15/2001. title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Russian Federation | PWO
text: ← UPU Circulars by Country Version française → Illegal Stamp Issues from Russian Federation Russian Federation Illegal Issues of Postage Stamps UNIVERSAL POSTAL UNION Berne, 10 July 2000 International Bureau Circular 214 Dear Sir/Madam The postal administration of the RUSSIAN FEDERATION asks me to inform you of the following: "I would like to draw your attention to our postal administration's grave concern about the illegal production and distribution of postage stamps ostensibly issued by various regions of the Russian Federation. Attached is a list of the regions in whose name illegal stamps have been issued. We were grateful to see participants attending the pilot course for Central and Eastern European countries on the promotion and development of philately, recently held in Riga (Latvia), made aware of this ever-growing proliferation of illegal stamps. We have also learned that such stamps have been openly offered for sale on the Internet for some time now. "Not only does such a proliferation of illicit stamps do harm to philately and the Russian Federation's reputation, it also contributes to the decline of the entire philatelic market. We are therefore counting on the Universal Postal Union and the World Association for the Development of Philately (WADP) to help us find a solution to this problem immediately." Yours faithfully, M S RAMAN Assistant Director-General Annex 1 List of regions of the Russian Federation in whose name illegal stamps are being issued: Altai Region Amurskaya Province Jewish Autonomous Region Franz Josef Land Autonomous Region of Evenkia Republic of Kabard-Balkaria Kamchatka Region Karachay-Cherkessia Autonomous Region of Koriakia Kuril islands Novosibirsk islands Kolguev Island Kunashir Island New Land Island Spitsbergen Island Republic of Adygea Republic of Bashkortostan Republic of Buriatia Republic of Daghestan Republic of Ingushetia Republic of Ichkeria Republic of Kalmykia Republic of Karelia Komi Republic Mari-El Republic Republic of Mordovia Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) Republic of North Ossetia Republic of Tatarstan Republic of Tuva Republic of Khakasia Russian Antarctica Sakhalin Region Republic of Udmurtia Republic of Chuvashia UNIVERSAL POSTAL UNION Berne, 14 January 2002 International Bureau Circular 15 Dear Sir/Madam The postal administration of the RUSSIAN FEDERATION asks me to inform you of the following: ''As a member of the Universal Postal Union, the postal administration of the Russian Federation issues postage stamps in accordance with the provisions of the Universal Postal Convention and the Letter Post Regulations. "However, there has recently appeared on world philatelic markets a large number of illicit stamp issues distributed on behalf of official territorial entities of the Russian Federation. These issues feature 'fashionable' subjects such as political figures, sports celebrities, Hollywood movie stars, etc. "The postal administration of the Russian Federation draws your attention to the fact that the regions on whose behalf these stamps have been issued form an integral part of the Russian Federation and that, according to the provisions of the UPU Regulations and Russian Federation legislation, they are not authorized to issue postage stamps independently (the list of these regions appears in the annex). All stamps issued on behalf of official territorial entities of the Russian Federation must therefore be regarded as illegal. They have no connection with the Post and cannot be used as an official means of indicating prepayment of postage. "These forged stamps are being issued by anonymous private companies operating outside Russia and have no direct connection with the official territorial entities of the Russian Federation. "The distribution of illegal postage stamps does serious moral and economic harm to the Russian Federation, discredits the Russian postal service in the eyes of the world philatelic community and encourages collectors to avoid buying not only illegal but also perfectly legal stamp issues." Yours faithfully, K J S McKEOWN Director of Communications and Postal Markets Annex List of regions of the Russian Federation on whose behalf illegal stamps have been issued Altai Region Amurskaya Province Antarctic Regions of the Russian Federation Jewish Autonomous Region Franz Josef Land Autonomous Region of Evenkia Republic of Kabard-Balkaria Kamchatka Region Republic of Karachay-Cherkessia Autonomous Region of Koriakia Kuril islands Novosibirsk islands Kolguev Island Kunashir Island Novaya Zemla Spitsbergen Island Republic of Adygea Republic of Bashkortostan Republic of Buryatia Republic of Dagestan Republic of Ingushetia Republic of Ishkeria Republic of Kalmykia Republic of Karelia Komi Republic Mari-El Republic Republic of Mordovia Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) Republic of North Ossetia Republic of Tatarstan Republic of Tuva Khakass Republic Sakhalin Region Republic of Udmurtia Chechen Republic Republic of Chuvashia More information about the illegal issues can be obtained directly from the UPU, Mrs. Maria Libera . title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Rwanda | PWO
text: ← Circulaires UPU par pays English original → Illegal Stamp Issues from Rwanda Rwanda - Emissions illicites de timbres-poste UNION POSTALE UNIVERSELLE Berne, le 10 décembre 2001 Circulaire du Bureau International 504 Madame, Monsieur, L’administration postale du RWANDA me prie de vous informer que son pays continue à faire l’objet de dénigrement et d’avilissement par la dissémination de timbres-poste illégaux. Elle me prie, par conséquent, d’attirer l’attention de tous les Pays-membres de l’Union et de tous ses partenaires philatéliques sur le fait que de nombreux timbres-poste continuent à être produits et disséminés au nom du Rwanda. En fait, l’administration postale du Rwanda informe qu’elle vient de découvrir l’exis­tence sur le marché philatélique d’autres séries de feuillets de timbres-poste aux divers motifs et qui portent l’inscription «RWANDA» (v. ci-joint la liste qu’elle a pu établir). Ces derniers continuent à porter un grave préjudice moral et économique à son pays, à son service postal et à l’Union tout entière. Elle maintient que ces timbres-poste sont illégaux et qu’ils ont été émis à son insu et en violation des dispositions des articles 6 et 25 de la Convention postale uni­verselle et de son Règlement de la poste aux lettres et de la législation nationale de la République rwandaise. Lesdits timbres-postes n’ont ni valeur de collection ni valeur d’affranchissement. Elle a des preuves que, parmi les distributeurs, il y a des sociétés situées en Grande-Bretagne et en Belgique et au moins deux sites Internet aux Etats-Unis. Elle peut dès lors penser que lesdites sociétés sont complices de la production desdits timbres-poste illégaux. Elle continuera à rechercher les faussaires afin de les traduire devant les tribunaux. Elle en appelle à la collaboration de tous les collègues postiers dans les pays concernés pour enrayer ce problème, surtout que le service postal semble être le moyen d’envoi préféré pour commander et recevoir les timbres-poste illégaux. Elle demande également que la communauté philatélique et tous les collectionneurs soient mis en garde contre l’achat de ces feuillets illégaux qui discréditent son service postal aux yeux des philatélistes du monde entier. Enfin, l’administration postale du Rwanda renouvelle sa requête auprès de toutes les administrations postales d’accroître leur propre vigilance et de ne pas accepter les correspondances affranchies au moyen de ces timbres-poste illégaux, de ne pas manquer d’en informer leurs partenaires philatéliques et de l’informer, ainsi que le Bureau international, si elles disposent de renseignements concernant la distri­bution de tels timbres-poste dans leur pays. Veuillez agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l’assurance de ma haute considération. Le Directeur des communications et des marchés, K.J.S. McKEOWN Annexe Timbres-poste illégaux émis en feuillets au nom de la République du Rwanda Note. - Les valeurs indiquées sur les timbres-poste constituant les feuillets décrits ci-après représentent des valeurs élevées par rapport aux tarifs de base en vigueur au Rwanda pour l’affranchissement. Les tarifs élevés indiqués sont destinés à tromper l’acheteur. En outre, la monnaie du Rwanda est le FRW, et non le F, comme indiqué. 1. Un feuillet composé de trois timbres-poste, dont deux pareils illustrent les prési­dents Kennedy et Lincoln, et celui du milieu le lancement d’un missile. Le feuillet est intitulé «SPACE KENNEDY» et comprend dans son pourtour des images de l’espace. Les valeurs sont de 300 F disposées horizontalement. 2. Un feuillet composé de trois timbres-poste illustrant diverses scènes d’une histoire pour les enfants intitulée «Winnie the Pooh». Le feuillet est intitulé «POOH» et comprend dans son pourtour d’autres images de l’histoire. Les valeurs sont de 300 F et sont disposées horizontalement. 3. Un feuillet composé de trois timbres-poste illustrant trois modèles de voitures de sport. Le feuillet est intitulé «MODERN SPORT CARS» et comprend dans son arrière-fond une plus grande voiture. Les valeurs sont de 300 F et sont disposées horizontalement. 4. Un feuillet composé de trois timbres-poste, dont deux pareils illustrent la défunte princesse Diana, et celui du milieu représente le pape Jean-Paul II. Le feuillet est intitulé «xx OF THE CENTURY» et comprend dans son pourtour des têtes de diffé­rentes personnalités. Les valeurs sont de 300 F disposées horizontalement. 5. Un feuillet composé de trois timbres-poste illustrant des scènes du bateau «Titanic». Le feuillet est intitulé «TITANIC» et comprend dans son pourtour d’autres scènes du bateau. Les valeurs sont de 300 F et sont disposées horizontalement. 6. Un feuillet composé de trois timbres-poste, dont deux pareils qui illustrent le conte de fées «Blanche-Neige et les sept nains». Le timbre-poste du milieu repré­sente un personnage. Le feuillet est intitulé «xx OF THE CENTURY» et comprend dans son pourtour des têtes de différentes personnalités qui n’ont pas de rapport avec le conte de fées. Les valeurs sont de 300 F et sont disposées horizonta­lement. 7. Un feuillet composé de sept timbres-poste illustrant diverses scènes de cow-boys jouant au golf. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. La colonne de 200 F contient en fait un seul timbre-poste tout en bas; les deux autres forment un timbre-poste se tenant à deux sans aucun texte ni chiffre. Le feuillet est intitulé «COWBOY GOLFERS» et comprend dans son pour­tour différentes scènes. 8. Un feuillet composé de neuf timbres-poste illustrant différentes espèces de poissons tropicaux. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. Le feuillet comprend dans son pourtour différents aspects da la vie sous-marine. 9. Un feuillet composé de neuf timbres-poste illustrant différentes espèces d’orchi­dées. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. Le feuillet comprend dans son pourtour différentes plantes. 10. Un feuillet composé de neuf timbres-poste illustrant différents types d’avions. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. 11. Un feuillet composé de six timbres-poste illustrant différentes poses de l’actrice américaine Marilyn Monroe. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. Le feuillet comprend dans son pourtour d’autres poses de l’actrice. En haut et au milieu du feuillet figure l’indication «Marilyn Monroe». 12. Un deuxième feuillet composé de six timbres-poste illustrant différentes poses de l’actrice américaine Marilyn Monroe. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. Le feuillet comprend dans son pourtour d’autres poses de l’actrice. En haut et au milieu du feuillet figure l’indication «Marilyn Monroe». 13. Un feuillet composé de neuf timbres-poste illustrant différents types de trains. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. Le feuillet comprend dans son pourtour différentes autres prises des trains. En haut et au milieu du feuillet figure l’indication «Steam Trains». 14. Un feuillet composé de neuf timbres-poste illustrant différents tableaux du peintre Renoir. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. Le feuillet comprend dans son pourtour différentes autres vues des tableaux. En haut et au milieu du feuillet figure l’inscription «RENOIR». 15. Un feuillet composé de neuf timbres-poste illustrant différents félins sauvages, notamment le léopard et le lion. Chaque timbre-poste porte sur son côté droit la lettre «L» dans un cercle. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. Le feuillet comprend dans son pourtour différentes autres prises des mêmes animaux sauvages. En haut et au milieu du feuillet figure une inscrip­tion illisible, peut-être «Cats». 16. Un feuillet composé de neuf timbres-poste illustrant différentes personnalités sportives mondialement connues (golf, tennis, boxe, basket-ball, football et base-ball). Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. En haut et au milieu du feuillet figure l’inscription «MILLENIUM». 17. Un feuillet composé de neuf timbres-poste illustrant différentes races de chiens domestiques, plus précisément les chiots de chacune des races illustrées. Les valeurs sont disposées verticalement par colonne de 100, 200 et 300 F. Le feuillet comprend dans son pourtour différentes autres prises des mêmes chiots. En haut et au milieu du feuillet figure l’inscription «Pedigree Puppies» et en bas l'inscription «RWANDA». A noter que les feuillets 1 à 6 sont vendus comme feuillets perforés et sont accom­pagnés de l’indication que la version non perforée peut s’obtenir au double du coût du feuillet perforé! title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Rwanda | PWO
text: ← UPU Circulars by Country Version française → Illegal Stamp Issues from Rwanda Rwanda - Illegal Issues of Postage Stamps UNIVERSAL POSTAL UNION Berne, 10 December 2001 International Bureau Circular 504 Dear Sir/Madam The postal administration of RWANDA asks me to inform you that its country continues to be denigrated and debased by the circulation of illegal postage stamps. It therefore asks me to draw the attention of all Union member countries and all philatelic partners to the fact that numerous postage stamps purporting to come from Rwanda continue to be produced and distributed. The Rwandan postal administration has learned of the existence on the philatelic market of further sets of miniature sheets of postage stamps with various designs, bearing the inscription "RWANDA" (a list of those it has been able to identify is annexed). These stamps continue to do serious moral and economic harm to the country, its postal service and the Union as a whole. It maintains that these postage stamps are illegal and were issued without its knowledge in contravention of articles 6 and 25 of the Universal Postal Convention, its Letter Post Regulations and the legislation of the Republic of Rwanda. These postage stamps have no value as collector's items or for postal prepayment. The administration has proof that the distributors include companies based in Great Britain and Belgium and at least two Internet sites in the United States. This leads it to believe that the companies in question may be involved in producing the illegal stamps. Its efforts to track down the counterfeiters will continue, so that they can be brought to justice. It calls for the cooperation of all postal colleagues in the countries in question to check this problem, particularly since the postal service appears to be the chosen method for ordering and receiving the illegal postage stamps. It also asks that the philatelic community and all collectors be warned not to buy these illegal miniature sheets, which discredit its postal service in the eyes of philatelists the world over. Finally, the postal administration of Rwanda reiterates its request to all postal administrations to exercise increased vigilance and refuse mail items bearing these illegal stamps. It also asks them to inform their philatelic partners accordingly and to notify the Rwandan administration and the International Bureau of any information they may have concerning the distribution of such postage stamps in their country. Yours faithfully, K.J.S. McKEOWN Director of Communications and Markets Annex Illegal postage stamps issued in miniature sheets, purportedly by the Republic of Rwanda NB - The values shown on the postage stamps that make up the miniature sheets described below are high in comparison with the basic postage rates in use in Rwanda. The high rates indicated are designed to deceive purchasers. Furthermore, the currency of Rwanda is the FRW, not the F as indicated. 1 A miniature sheet made up of three postage stamps, two of them identical, illustrating President Kennedy and President Lincoln, with the middle stamp showing a missile launch. The miniature sheet is entitled "SPACE KENNEDY" and includes images of space in the margins. The stamps have face values of 300 F and are arranged horizontally. 2 A miniature sheet comprising three postage stamps illustrating various scenes from the "Winnie the Pooh" children's stories. The miniature sheet is entitled "POOH" and includes other illustrations from the stories in the margins. The stamps have face values of 300 F and are arranged horizontally. 3 A miniature sheet comprising three postage stamps illustrating three sports car models. The miniature sheet is entitled "MODERN SPORT CARS" and includes an image of a larger car in the background. The stamps have face values of 300 F and are arranged horizontally. 4 A miniature sheet made up of three postage stamps, two of them identical, illustrating the late Diana, Princess of Wales, with the middle stamp showing Pope John Paul II. The miniature sheet is entitled "xx OF THE CENTURY" and includes the heads of various personalities in the margins. The stamps have face values of 300 F and are arranged horizontally. 5 A miniature sheet comprising three postage stamps illustrating pictures of the RMS TITANIC. The miniature sheet is entitled "TITANIC" and includes other pictures of the ship in the margins. The stamps have face values of 300 F and are arranged horizontally. 6 A miniature sheet made up of three postage stamps, two of them identical, illustrating the fairy story "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs". The middle postage stamp shows a character. The miniature sheet is entitled "xx OF THE CENTURY" and includes the heads of various personalities unrelated to the fairy tale in the margins. The stamps have face values of 300 F and are arranged horizontally. 7 A miniature sheet comprising seven postage stamps illustrating various scenes of cowboys playing golf. The values are arranged vertically in columns of 100 F, 200 F and 300 F. The 200 F column contains a single postage stamp at the bottom, the two others forming a double se-tenant stamp without any text or numbers. The miniature sheet is entitled "COWBOY GOLFERS" and includes various scenes in the margins. 8 A miniature sheet comprising nine postage stamps illustrating various species of tropical fish. The values are arranged vertically in columns of 100 F, 200 F and 300 F. The miniature sheet features various aspects of underwater life in the margins. 9 A miniature sheet comprising nine postage stamps illustrating various species of orchids. The values are arranged vertically in columns of 100 F, 200 F and 300 F. The miniature sheet features various plants in the margins. 10 A miniature sheet comprising nine postage stamps illustrating various types of aircraft. The values are in vertical columns of 100F, 200F and 300F. 11 A miniature sheet comprising six postage stamps with various pictures of the American actress, Marilyn Monroe. The values are arranged vertically in columns of 100 F, 200 F and 300 F. The miniature sheet features other pictures of the actress. At the top of the sheet, in the middle, there is the inscription "Marilyn Monroe". 12 A second miniature sheet comprising six postage stamps with various pictures of Marilyn Monroe. The values are arranged vertically in columns of 100 F, 200 F and 300 F. The miniature sheet features other pictures of the actress. At the top of the sheet, in the middle, there is the inscription "Marilyn Monroe". 13 A miniature sheet comprising nine postage stamps illustrating various types of trains. The values are arranged vertically in columns of 100 F, 200 F and 300 F. The miniature sheet features various other pictures of trains in the margins. At the top of the sheet, in the middle, there is the inscription "Steam Trains". 14 A miniature sheet comprising nine postage stamps illustrating various paintings by Renoir. The values are arranged vertically in columns of 100 F, 200 F and 300 F. The miniature sheet features in the margins various other scenes from paintings. At the top of the sheet, in the middle, there is the inscription "RENOIR". 15 A miniature sheet comprising nine postage stamps illustrating various types of wild cat, in particular the leopard and lion. Each postage stamp has the letter "L" in a circle on the right-hand side. The values are arranged vertically in columns of 100 F, 200 F and 300 F. The miniature sheet features in the margins various other pictures of the same wild animals. At the top of the sheet, in the middle, there is an illegible inscription, which may be "Cats". 16 A miniature sheet comprising nine postage stamps illustrating various internationally known sporting personalities (golf, tennis, boxing, basketball, football and baseball). The values are in vertical columns of 100F, 200F and 300F. At the top of the sheet, in the middle, there is the inscription "MILLENIUM". 17 A miniature sheet comprising nine postage stamps illustrating various breeds of domestic dog, and more especially puppies of each breed. The values are arranged vertically in columns of 100 F, 200 F and 300 F. The miniature sheet features various other pictures of the same puppies in the margins. At the top of the sheet, in the middle, there is the inscription "Pedigree Puppies", and at the bottom there is the inscription "RWANDA". NB - Miniature sheets Nos 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are sold as perforate sheets, and are accompanied by the information that an imperforate version is available for twice the price of the perforate version! More information about the illegal issues can be obtained directly from the UPU, Mrs. Maria Libera . Published: 01.02/2001. Revised: 01/02/02 . title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Tajikistan | PWO
text: ← Circulaires UPU par pays English original → Illegal Stamp Issues from Tajikistan Tadjikistan - Emissions illicites de timbres-poste UNION POSTALE UNIVERSELLE Berne, le 17 June 2002 Circulaire du Bureau International 229 Madame, Monsieur, L'administration postale du TADJIKistan me prie de bien vouloir vous informer de ce qui suit (traduction de l'anglais): «L'administration postale de la République du Tadjikistan, en sa qualité de membre de l'Union postale universelle, émet des timbres-poste dans le respect des disposi­tions de la Convention postale universelle et du Règlement de la poste aux lettres. Toutefois, un nombre croissant d'émissions illicites, produites au nom de l'admi­nistration postale du Tadjikistan, sont proposées sur les marchés philatéliques du monde entier. Les thèmes choisis pour ces émissions sont des sujets appréciés du public: personnages politiques, athlètes célèbres, «stars» d'Hollywood, etc. Toutes ces émissions produites au nom de la République du Tadjikistan doivent être considérées comme illicites. Elles n'ont aucun rapport avec la poste et il est impossible d'utiliser les timbres en question comme moyen d'affranchissement. Ces contrefaçons sont réalisées par des compagnies privées situées en dehors du Tadjikistan. La diffusion de ces émissions illicites cause un préjudice moral et économique con­sidérable à la République du Tadjikistan. Cela discrédite le service postal du Tadji­kistan aux yeux du monde philatélique. Il en résulte que les collectionneurs évitent d'acheter des timbres illicites, mais aussi des timbres tout à fait légaux.» Voir en annexe une liste des émissions illicites produites au nom du Tadjikistan. Veuillez agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'assurance de ma haute considération. Le Directeur de la communication et des marchés postaux, K.J.S. title: Why no images of illegals on sites | PWO
text: Why no images of illegals on sites ← General Articles THE FIGHT AGAINST ILLEGAL STAMPS The PWO, following the recommendation of the UPU, opposes to the publication of images of illegal stamps on sites. Please find below some arguments for this position. "Shell" wrote (on RCSD): > So, how do I know which issues are illegal? A picture of the illegal stamp > with say a watermark or disclaimer stating it was illegal would certainly > help me. I do not understand why you don't want pictures of illegal > stamps shown. > Shell > > (Just another newbie question from Planet 10) Yes, in a way you are right. If we use catalogues in identifying the usual stamps, why shouldn't we use the same method for illegals? Unfortunately, it's not so simple, and the devil is hidden, as so often, in many significant details. I'll take some arguments from an earlier posting of mine and I'll complete them with knowledge from the further evolution of the topic. 1. A (smaller) problem is that such a site won't be complete, because: - there are so many illegals - they aren't already listed somewhere, so it's practically impossible to identify and to find them all (this being the job of the UPU and of PAs. - of course anybody can help them, and is invited to do so) - there are many potential illegals, about which the PAs haven't complained at the UPU, so that officially at least their status is still unclear. So the question will be: Which is the status of suspected stamps that aren't shown on that site? I repeat it, it's not the big problem, because if the idea should be good, the fact of presenting less were anyway better than of showing nothing. 2. Another problem is that there is a high risk that some (more or less collectors, rather all kind of fans), who love Madonna, Britney etc., will see these illegals on the proposed sites and that they will buy them anyway. So why facilitate the access to such information and this way facilitate the activity of illegals dealers and producers? They could even link to such a site, and say that the problem is just controversial. Consider also that after a time these illegals, proposed by ex-fans, enter the philatelic circuit. Just take a look at eBay, where many unsuspecting persons try selling their illegals (I know it directly from many of them). This is, BTW, the argument invoked by the UPU. 3. There are some pornographic stamps. Challenged by me, a participant wrote on this subject "Lady or not, I will publish what is illegal", which shows a certain logic and determination, but less common sense. I think that this is also a bad idea, and that this would classify such a site as a X-rated one. The afflux of visitors from sex sites (who will surely link to a such "related" one) is guaranteed, but is this in the interest of philately? You know my answer. The contradiction between offering a full view of illegals and staying moral comes from the evil nature of illegals, of course, and not from those who wish fighting against them. 4. Because illegals are (obviously for quite anybody) immoral, why show more of them than necessary??? Why not take example from the editors of the renown Stanley Gibbons catalogues, who write following on the subject of stamps with a controversial validity (which, btw, aren't considered illegals): "From June 1967 very many stamp issues were made by a succession of agencies which had been awarded contracts by the Ruler, sometimes two agencies operating at the same time. Several contradictory statements were made as to the validity of some of these issues which appeared 1967-1972 and for this reason they are only listed in abbreviated form." It's for Ajman, SG edition 1997. If the editors decided to only list, in an abbreviated form, the stamps of a controversial validity, and _without_ showing their images, then why should be done much _more_ than that for stamps of _no_ validity at all? 5. The fight against illegals is taken very easy by some. I can affirm it, because at PWO we have some experience and we made many things in fighting illegals, possibly more than all others together on the Internet (see the links below, please). For example, we have published (together with AskPhil) the UPU Circulars referring to illegal stamps. We find that these circulars provide sufficient information in order to identify the already denounced illegals. Coming back to the big numbers of different illegals and the difficulty to obtain all of them for a catalogue of images, may I mention that the (cheap) idea of taking just a very limited number of images from eBay and to put them of sites is simply absurd (I couldn't find a milder word, sorry). Just think how have the authors identified these illegals. My answer is (and it's obvious): by comparing them with the descriptions from UPU circulars!!! That's exactly what I made too when I wrote to dealers on eBay, explaining them what are they actually selling (most didn't know) and asking them to take back their offers (what worked in 80% of cases). So may I ask, why put such images of illegals on sites, when anybody (yes, anybody who can read) can identify them by using the circulars? Isn't this just a method to demonstrate its own superiority, or something like that? 6. Some have written here that the Circulars are unintelligible and difficult to understand, but I have never seen an example... I would agree that they could be more complete (I'm sure that UPU welcomes any good suggestions), but not that they are hard to understand. IMO, they aren't more difficult than the stamp catalogues. I hope that my arguments will help in better clarifying the situation of illegals, of means to fight them, and of taking the most appropriate and responsible position. I support the idea that any person is responsible for what they buys, sells or collects, and that it's not the right of others to dictate them what should they collect or not. But, in the same time, it is necessary to fight against those who abuse the unsuspecting stamp collectors and the poor postal administrations, who infringe the property rights of those PAs, and sometimes infringe intellectual property too. Regards, Victor Manta (published on the Usenet newsgroup rec.collecting.stamps.discuss, on July 19, 2002 Published: 07/19//2002. Revised: 07/19/02 . title: Illegal Stamps — Introduction | PWO
text: Illegal Stamps — Introduction Fight Against Illegal Issues of Postal Stamps The Philatelic Webmasters Organization ( PWO ), a non-profit organization located in Switzerland, that counts at time over 350 members from all continents, was created in order to promote, support and develop philately through philatelic webmastering. The World Association for the Development of Philately (WADP) started in 1996 an action against the producing and the selling of the Illegal Stamps. The Illegal Stamps were defined by the General Assembly of the WADP, in its second meeting (6 th of Oct. 2000), as: Illegal issues for territories which are not entitled to issue stamps and false stamps produced by fraudsters in the name of an issuing authority with the intent to defraud collectors. The Universal Postal Union, a member of the UN and of the WADP, is the organization that coordinates the fight against the illegal stamps. Consequently, it has published since 1996 an growing number of Circulars in which the postal administrations members of the UPU have denounced stamps that were illegally issued in their name or in the name of their territorial units. In the last years the philatelic business has considerably grown throughout the Internet. Some unethical sites and dealers, and sometimes uninformed sellers use the Internet to defraud the stamp collectors, by proposing for sale illegal stamps. The first victims are mostly the beginners in our nice hobby. Being mostly active on the Web, we created this subsite to allow for a better understanding of illegal stamps and to inform how to recognize and to avoid them. We can be easily reached by e-mail (please click here to send us a message - take out spaam from the e-mail address please). Developed by the Universal Postal Union (UPU) and the World Association for the Development of Philately (WADP), a WADP Numbering System (WNS) was introduced on 1 January 2002 with the aim of creating a database of all authentic postage stamps issued by UPU member countries and territories on or after that date. The PWO tightly collaborated from its very beginnings with the Universal Postal Union in the fight against illegal stamps. For this reason as well information about illegal issues as the UPU Circulars were published on a regular basis on the PWO site. The PWO, in direct concern with the International Bureau of the UPU in Bern, has dedicated the present subsite to the fight of illegal stamps. Because In the middle of the year 2003 the UPU started by publishing the UPU Circulars referring to illegal stamps on its own site, we didn't publish them on this site anymore, and we limited ourselves to provide (in the menu) links to the pages where they could be found. Unfortunately, these links got broken in the middle of the year 2009, this after the UPU site redesign ended they reappeared. Update . Since 2016, the older Illegals Circulars cannot be accessed on the UPU site without a user name and pasword, that are generally unknown. Fortunately, for the years 2010 - 2017 links to them were published on the FIP site of Fight Against Fakes and Forgeries by Richard Gratton (Secretary & treasurer). Good job, Richard! title: Emissions illicites de Madagascar | PWO
text: ← Circulaires UPU par pays English original → Emissions illicites de Madagascar Madagascar - Emissions illicites de timbres-poste UNION POSTALE UNIVERSELLE Berne, le 24 septembre 2001 Circulaire du Bureau International 393 Madame, Monsieur, L'administration postale de MADAGASCAR me prie de vous informer qu'elle est en possession d'informations concernant la circulation sur le marché international d'une émission illicite de timbres-poste émise au nom de PAOSITRA MALAGASY. Les caractéristiques de cette émission sont les suivantes: Un feuillet perforé et un feuillet non perforé, portant en bas l’indication «Millenium – Concorde 2000 – 30e anniversaire» et contenant 9 timbres-poste, dont chacun est d'une valeur de 2000 Fmg, 400 ARIARY. Chaque timbre-poste reproduit des prises de vue différentes de l'avion «Concorde» ainsi que les mentions «REPOBLIKAN’I MADAGASIKARA» et «Paositra 1999». Ces deux dernières mentions ne sont pas positionnées de la même façon sur chaque timbre-poste. En outre, le timbre-poste en haut à droite porte également la mention «MILLENIUM» en lettres majuscules. Ces timbres-poste n'ayant pas reçu l'approbation de l'administration postale de Madagascar, ils ont donc été émis en violation des dispositions de la Convention postale universelle et du Règlement de la poste aux lettres. Par conséquent, ils sont considérés comme nuls et non avenus et ne peuvent être acceptés comme moyen d’affranchissement postal. L'administration postale de Madagascar serait reconnaissante pour tout renseignement qui permettrait d’identifier l’auteur de ces émissions illégales. Veuillez agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'assurance de ma haute considération. Le Directeur de la communication et des marchés postaux, K.J.S. McKEOWN Des informations complémentaires au sujet des émissions illégales peuvent être obtenues directement de l'UPU, auprès de Madame Maria Libera . Publié le 16-08-01. Modifié le 29-09-01 . title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Madagascar | PWO
text: ← UPU Circulars by Country Version française → Illegal Stamp Issues from Madagascar Madagascar - Illegal Issues of Postage Stamps UNIVERSAL POSTAL UNION Berne, 24 September 2001 International Bureau Circular 393 Dear Sir/Madam The postal administration of MADAGASCAR asks me to inform you that it has information about the circulation on the international market of an illegal issue of postage stamps purporting to be issued by the PAOSITRA MALAGASY. The characteristics of this issue are as follows: A perforated miniature sheet and an imperforate miniature sheet, bearing at the bottom of the sheet the inscription "Millenium – Concorde 2000 – 30e anniversaire" and consisting of nine postage stamps, each with a value of 2000 Fmg, 400 ARIARY. Each postage stamp shows different views of the "Concorde" aircraft and the inscriptions "REPOBLIKAN’I MADAGASIKARA" and "Paositra 1999". These two inscriptions are not positioned in the same way on all the postage stamps. In addition, the postage stamp on top at the right also has the word "MILLENIUM" in capital letters. As these postage stamps have not received the approval of the postal administration of Madagascar, they have been issued in violation of the provisions of the Universal Postal Convention and its Letter Post Regulations. Consequently, they are regarded as null and void and may not be accepted as a means of postal prepayment. The postal administration of Madagascar would be grateful for any information which would lead to identifying the person responsible for these illegal issues. Yours faithfully, K J S McKEOWN Director of Communication and Postal Markets More information about the illegal issues can be obtained directly from the UPU, Mrs. Maria Libera . title: UPU Circulars 1996–2003 — Historical Summary | PWO
text: UPU Circulars concerning illegal / illicit / problem stamp issues (1996–2003) Historical chronological summary — updated 8 December 2003. Transcribed from the eight-page document supplied for the PWO archive; this is a summary list, not a substitute for the original individual UPU circulars. Source note: This list does not cover all illegal stamps on the market. Postal administrations may still have had investigations in progress at the time of compilation. View the original eight-page PDF ← Back to UPU Circulars by Country 2003 — 8 circulars Guinea (Rep) 8 December 2003 – n° 421 · Entry 8 Guinea Post Office condemns a considerable number of illegal postage stamps which have been produced and freely disseminated on the philatelic market by private companies and dealers on the following subjects : - "Celebrities/famous figures" - Immoral scenes, sexually explicit and completely unethical (five miniature sheets in the same vertical format, each containing four postage stamps with the inscription "Pin-Up" in English (various half clad women) as well as the actress Marilyn. The "Scouts" logo is also included. - "Fairy tales, fantastic tales, cartoons" - Ten miniature sheets, each depicting a scene from a different fairy tale in the background, with a series of five postage stamps. At the top of each miniature sheet, in the middle, there is the inscription "Les contes populaires du monde" ("Folk tales of the world"). - "Paintings" - Fifteen miniature sheets with the inscription "American Impressionists" in English, each depicting a painting by the artist con- cerned in the background, with a series of four postage stamps. The "Rotary International" logo is also included. - "Vehicles (Transport)" - Trains and locomotives - Nineteen miniature sheets, each with a series of four postage stamps with the inscription "Les trains legendaries du monde" ("Legendary trains of the world"). The "Rotary International" logo is also included. Rwanda 13 October 2003 – n° 354 · Entry 7 Continued piracy against Rwanda Post through the issue and sale of illegal postage stamps bearing the word 'Rwanda'. - Beatification of Mother Teresa of Calcutta (Souvenir sheet includes image of Pope Jean-Paul II ) - Fauna (snake - One miniature sheet with one stamp as well as a souvenir sheet of 6 stamps - both feature the words "THE WILDLIFE TRUSTS" and a matching logo. Eritrea 25 August – n°294 · Entry 6 Illegal postage stamp issues produced mostly as sheetlets and miniature sheets in the name of Eritrea on the following thematics. Many stamps carry the emblem/logo of the Rotary and Scouts organisations. Animals: different species of bears, bison or buffalo, crocodiles, dinosaurs, dogs, elephants, frogs, horses, monkeys, pandas, snakes, tigers, turtles, wild jungle cats - Birds: different species of birds, birds of prey, fowl, parrots, penguins - Cartoons: "The Beatles Yellow Submarine") - Events: "Tribute to 11th Sept. Firefighters" - Fish species/Marine creatures - Flora: flowers (orchid), mushrooms - Insects: bees, butterflies, spiders – Lighthouses - Paintings: "The Impressionists" (Camille Corot, Camille Pissarro, Pierre Auguste Renoir), "Vincent van Gogh", “Edward Hopper”, “Jack Vettriano” - People/Personalities (including actors, actresses, singers, etc.): Brigitte Bardot, Elvis Presley, Grace Kelly, Marilyn Monroe, Sophia Loren - Immoral and Provocative Scenes (sexually explicit in some cases): sheetlet of nine depicting young women together on a golf course, sheetlets of nine each inscribed "SEXY ACTRESSES", "SEXY MODELS", "PIN UP" ("The Art of Elvgren"), "BORIS VALLEJO", "DORIAN CLEAVENGER", "Michael Möbius", "OLIVIA" and "Ricky Carralero". - Teddy Bears: sheetlets and miniature sheets depicting “Mole Island Bears" - Vehicles – Transportation: cars, Concorde, motorcycles/motor racing, trains/locomotives The Rotary emblem and the Scouts logo appear on many of the illegal stamps. Different websites carry different prices. Côte d’Ivoire 28 July – n°269 · Entry 5 Illegal postage stamp issues produced mostly as sheetlets and miniature sheets in the name of the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire on the following thematics: groups of shells, different dog breeds, species of butterfly, orchids, the actor Elvis Presley, the actress Marilyn Monroe, motorbike races, table tennis players, vintage fire engines and different trains. Many stamps carry the emblem of a specific organization. A certain number of miniature sheets are listed in dollars on one website at a very high price (19.95 USD) for the perforated format for the two sheets and at double the price (39.80 USD) for the imperforated format. The same miniature sheets are listed on another website at a much cheaper price (e.g. 3.00 USD each). Kyrgyzstan 5 May - n°172 · Entry 4 Illegal issues of postage stamps: sheetlets issued in 2002, comprising nine (3x3) stamps with face values of 10 KGS, 20 KGS and 30 KGS depicting "HARRY POTTER", "MERRY CHRISTMAS" (cartoon heroes) stamps, "JOHN PAUL II" and "SHAHMATY" (chess) stamps ; a sheet of stamps issued in 2001 depicting "JOHN PAUL II". Mauritania 28 April – n° 161 · Entry 3 Illegal postage stamp issues produced in the name of the Islamic Republic of Mauritania which include numerous souvenir sheets and sheetlets, sold in both the imperforate and perforate format portraying different type of bird (including birds of prey, ducks, pheasants, field birds and sea birds), different species of owl, various penguin scenes, various cats playing together, various elephant and polar bear scenes, different lighthouses, various types of firearm, various sports of the Sydney Olympics, various other sports (tennis, horse- riding, swimming, volleyball, table tennis, fencing, judo and cycling), different trains, different portraits of Pope John Paul II, the singer Elvis Presley, the actress Marilyn Monroe, The Beatles, Walt Disney, classic actresses, different scenes from the Harry Potter films, the group Queen, different scenes from the television series "The Simpsons", "TEDDY BEARS", "Scooby Doo". The value shown on each stamp is in UM and each stamp is inscribed with the year 2002. A number of the stamps feature the International Rotary emblem, while on others there is the Scout emblem. Uzbekistan 3 March – n° 70 · Entry 2 Illegal postage stamp issues produced in the name of the Republic of Uzbekistan: numerous souvenir sheets and sheetlets portraying chess, trains and fauna (various animals, lizards, snakes, species of "chiroptera" and "perissodactyla". Afghanistan 13 Jan – n° 02 · Entry 1 Many illegal issues of postage stamps appearing mostly on miniature sheets as well as on horizontal and vertical 9-stamp sheets on the following thematics: - various types of boats, chess positions, footballers and the logo of the Korea/Japan World Cup - Sports – Famous people – in "FORMULA 2000" - Vehicles – old types of vehicles, "ENGLISH TRAINS", other trains - Fauna – different breeds of cat, dog, horse, different species of birds of prey and members of the eagle and owl families, other creatures, various types of dinosaur, insects (the beetle), different species of fish - Flora: different plants, orchids - Paintings – (vertical miniature sheets) entitled "The impressionists" (Henri Matisse, Toulouse Lautrec, Vincent van Gogh) - Paintings – Posters – One vertical miniature sheet of nine postage stamps entitled "INTERNATIONAL CLASSIC POSTERS". - Famous persons depicting Bin Laden, "Diana, Princess of Wales , "ELVIS PRESLEY, Marilyn Monroe, "Mother Teresa" and "Jean Paul II", various people on sheets entitled "THE GREAT PEOPLE OF THE 20TH CENTURY". 2002 — 6 circulars Myanmar 25 Nov – n° 428 · Entry 6 Illegal issues of postage stamps in the name of the Union of Myanmar on the following themes Illegal stamps produced in the name of the Union of Myanmar and covering themes such as “FORMULA 1” and “GOLF ICONS” sports stars,“CLASSIC CARS”, “KINGS OF CHESS” and different aspects of chess games, Impressionist paintings, “PERSONALITIES OF THE 20TH CENTURY” , “BRUCE LEE”, Tiger Woods, orchids, mushrooms and the Rotary logo, breeds of cats and dogs and the Scouts logo, , different breeds of fish and owls, different types of trains, the “Dutch Royal Wedding” different shots from the films of the actress Marilyn Monroe, different shots of the actor Elvis Presley; “THE ILLUSTRATED PORTRAITS” of “MUSIC STARS”, different shots taken from horror films. Morocco 18 Nov – n°414 · Entry 5 Illegal postage stamp issues inscribed "République sahraoui" (Saharan Republic) or "Sahara Occidental" (Western Sahara) still circulating on the international philatelic market on the following thematics: the life of the singer Elvis Presley; the life of the actress Marilyn Monroe, various breeds of dog, various types of fire-fighting vehicles, various types of old cars; various desert cacti; camels; stamps on the theme of Galileo and space, various athletes from the 1990 and 1996 Olympics; a football world cup and scenes from Ancient Egypt. Tadjikistan 17 June - n° 229 · Entry 4 Illegal issues of postage stamps in the name of Tadjikistan (11 sheetlets representing «John Paul II», «Bruce Lee», «100th Anniversary of the Queen Mother», «Formula 1», «Michael Jordan», «Captain America», «Fantastic Four», «Harry Potter», «Ousama ben Laden», «Motorbike Sports» and «Dutch Royal Wedding»). Kyrgyzstan 3 June - n° 208 · Entry 3 Illegal issues of postage stamps bearing the symbol of the Republic of Kyrgyzstan (19 sheetlets representing "Shrek", "Defenders of Peace and Freedom", "Tiger", "Harry Potter", "Ironman", "Formula 1", "Superman", "Mother Teresa", "Flash", "The Beatles", "Legends of Baseball", "Dogs", "Green Lantern", "Concorde", "Harley Davidson", "Princess Diana", "Elvis" and "Penguins") Burundi 15 Apr – n° 143 · Entry 2 Illegal issues of postage stamps: six varieties of butterfly with the following face values: 100 F, 150 F, 200 F, 250 F, 300 F and 400 F. Russian Federation 14 Jan.- n° 15 · Entry 1 Illegal issues of postage stamps featuring 'fashionable' subjects such as political figures, sports celebrities, Hollywood movie stars, etc. ostensibly issued in the name of the various regions of the Russian Federation which are not stamp issuing authorities (Altai Region, Amurskaya Province, Chechen Republic, Jewish Autonomous Region, Franz Josef Land, Autonomous Region of Evenkia, Republic of Kabard-Balkaria, Kamchatka Region, Karachay- Cherkessia, Autonomous Region of Koriakia, Kuril islands, Novosibirsk islands, Kolguev Island, Kunashir Island, New Land Island (Novaya Zemla), Spitsbergen Island, Republic of Adygea, Republic of Bashkortostan, Republic of Buriatia, Republic of Daghestan, Republic of Ingushetia, Republic of Ichkeria, Republic of Kalmykia, Republic of Karelia, Komi Republic, Mari-El Republic, Republic of Mordovia, Republic of Sakha (Yakutia), Republic of North Ossetia, Republic of Tatarstan, Republic of Tuva, Republic of Khakasia, Russian Antarctica, Sakhalin Region, Republic of Udmurtia. Republic of Chuvashia. 2001 — 15 circulars Comoros 17 December - n° 514 · Entry 15 Illegal issues of postage stamps – Titanic, Babe Ruth, Mohammad Ali Rwanda 10 December - n° 504 · Entry 14 Illegal issues of postage stamps – 17 sheets denounced on various themes such as "SPACE KENNEDY", various scenes from the "Winnie the Pooh", sports car models, a miniature sheet entitled "xx OF THE CENTURY" illustrating the late Diana, Princess of Wales and Pope John Paul II, fairy story "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs", various scenes of cowboys playing golf ("COWBOY GOLFERS"), various species of tropical fish, various species of orchids, various types of aircraft, various illustrations of the American actress, Marilyn Monroe, various types of trains ("Steam Trains"), various paintings by Renoir, various types of wild cat, in particular the leopard and lion, illustrating various internationally known sporting personalities (in golf, tennis, boxing, basketball, football and baseball), various breeds of domestic dog, and their puppies ("Pedigree Puppies"), and at the bottom there is the inscription "RWANDA". Some miniature sheets are sold as perforate and some as imperforate versions ! Saudi Arabia 15 October – n° 421 · Entry 13 Counterfeit of the first postage stamps issued in 1934 Madagascar 24 September - n°393 · Entry 12 Illegal issues of postage stamps – a perforated and imperforated sheet depicting various shots of the «Concord» Rwanda 3 September – n° 363 · Entry 11 Illegal issues of postage stamps – 23 sheets denounced on various themes such as pornographic and erotic scenes, models of double-decker buses, varieties of roses, models of hot air balloons (including a dragon, a dinosaur, an elephant, a house and faces), various cars (old models), different views of a motorcycle in action during a race, trains (various models and views), "Millennium" and "Leaders of XI – XIXth Century", "Architecture of XI – XIXth Century", "Art of XI – XIXth Century", "Famous people of XI – XIXth Century", "Music stars of XXth Century", "Movie stars of XXth Century", "Engines of XXth Century, different positions in chess, various varieties of fungi, various breeds of cat, different butterflies. Kyrgyzstan 30 July - n° 308 · Entry 10 Illegal issues of postage stamps continue to be advertised on an Internet site on stamp series such as "Backstreet Boys", "Jennifer Aniston", "Tennis", "Beverly Hills 90210", "Minerals", "Penguins", "Tom and Jerry", "Prince William", "Babylon 5", "End of Mir". Mali 11 June – n° 238 · Entry 9 Illegal issues of postage stamps distributed by an American company and others on various themes such as International Red Cross (Jane Dalano, Henri Dunant, etc), Great composers (Haydn, Chopin, Beethoven, etc), Wild animals: (tiger, lion, eagle, etc), Horses Comoros 7 May – n° 201 · Entry 8 Illegal postage stamps (in more than 17 sheets) some bearing the inscription REPUBLIQUE FEDERALE DES COMORES, and others the inscription REPUBLIQUE FEDERALE ISLAMIQUE DES COMORES, with various designs such as "OCEAN LIFE" , "HORSES", "PANDAS" the boxer Muhammad Ali, the American baseball player Babe Ruth, other various personalities such as airplane pilots, a scientist, a racing car driver, Pope John Paul II, a man walking on the moon, various explorers, the man behind the Zeppelin airships a Fauna and flora set: United Arab Emirates 9 Apr – n° 168 · Entry 7 Illegal issues - postage stamps supposedly issued by the Emirates of Ajman, Sharjah and Fujeira depicting animals (dogs, cats, birds, reptiles) Centrafrique (République) 2 Apr – n° 156 · Entry 6 Illegal issues of postage stamps of various animals (tigers, penguins, wolves, horses) Laos 19 Mar.- n° 135 · Entry 5 Illegal issues of postage stamps on the Internet site « www.marlen- stamps.com »" on the subject of «Three of the Great of the Golf World: Tiger Woods, Payne Stewart and Arnold Palmer" and "Great People of the 20th Century, part III", with pictures of famous people, namely Elvis Presley, Marilyn Monroe, John Lennon and the Beatles». Georgia 29 Jan.- n° 50 · Entry 4 Illegal stamps issued in the name of the Republic of Abkhasia, the Republic of South Osetia, Adjara and Batumi - over 200 series of stamps denounced on a multitude of subjects. Chad 2 Jan.- n° 8 · Entry 3 Illegal issues of postage stamps issued by three companies located in Belgium, Lithuania, United States of Amerca, on the themes of Butterflies, Cats, Elephants, Birth of Gandhi. Senegal 2 Jan.- n° 7 · Entry 2 Illegal issues on theme « Greenpeace » Kyrgyzstan 2 Jan.- n° 6 · Entry 1 Illegal issues of postage stamps on the Internet site « www.marlen- stamps.com »". 2000 — 12 circulars Angola 25 Sept.- n° 406 · Entry 12 Illegal issues of postage stamps issued by three companies located in Belgium, Great Britain and Lithuania. 53 Sheetlets on the themes of Flora (roses, bonzai, flowers, mushrooms), Animals (bees , birds, butterflies, cats, dinosaurs, dogs, eagles, fish, gorillas, lions, owls, panda, swans, turtles), Trains of Angola, Millennium 2000, Papal visit, Personalities of the 20th century, Cardinal John O'Connor Afghanistan 21 Aug. - n° 345 · Entry 11 The postal administration of Afghanistan confirms that no new postage stamps since 1989 have been issued. Consequently, any postage stamps issued since 1989 are illegal issues. Kyrgyzstan 10 July - n° 285 · Entry 10 Illegal issues of postage stamps, miniature sheets representing Western show business personalities such as the “Beatles” and “Madonna”. Russian Federation 19 June - n°214 · Entry 9 Illegal production and distribution of postage stamps ostensibly issued by various regions of the Russian Federation (Altai Region, Amurskaya Province, Jewish Autonomous Region, Franz Josef Land, Autonomous Region of Evenkia, Republic of Kabard-Balkaria, Kamchatka Region, Karachay-Cherkessia, Autonomous Region of Koriakia, Kuril islands, Novosibirsk islands, Kolguev Island, Kunashir Island, New Land Island, Spitsbergen Island, Republic of Adygea, Republic of Bashkortostan, Republic of Buriatia, Republic of Daghestan, Republic of Ingushetia, Republic of Ichkeria, Republic of Kalmykia, Republic of Karelia, Komi Republic, Mari-El Republic, Republic of Mordovia, Republic of Sakha (Yakutia), Republic of North Ossetia, Republic of Tatarstan, Republic of Tuva, Republic of Khakasia, Russian Antarctica, Sakhalin Region, Republic of Udmurtia. title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Uzbekistan | PWO
text: ← Circulaires UPU par pays English original → Illegal Stamp Issues from Uzbekistan Ouzbékistan Emissions illicites de timbres-poste UNION POSTALE UNIVERSELLE Berne, le 3 mars 2003 Circulaire du Bureau international 70 Madame, Monsieur, L'Agence des communications et de l'information de l’ OUZBÉKISTAN me prie de vous communiquer ce qui suit: «Des personnes non identifiées s’efforcent de discréditer notre pays en mettant en circulation des émissions illégales de timbres-poste. Nous avons été informés de l’apparition sur le marché philatélique de timbres-poste contrefaits avec la mention ‹O’ZBEKISTON›. Ces timbres, dont la valeur est indiquée en soms, n’ont pas été émis par l’administration postale de l’Ouzbékistan. Notre administration postale attire l’attention des administrations postales des Pays-membres de l’Union, de la communauté philatélique et des collectionneurs sur l’apparition de ces timbres-poste contrefaits et demande instamment de ne pas les accepter comme moyen d’affranchissement et de ne pas les acheter. Outre cela, l’administration postale de la République d’Ouzbékistan prie les admi­nistrations postales des Pays-membres de l’Union d’informer leurs partenaires phi­latéliques de la présence et de la mise en circulation de ces timbres-poste contre­faits et de manifester de la vigilance. Ci-joint en annexe se trouve la liste des timbres-poste contrefaits mentionnés ci-dessus.» Veuillez agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'assurance de ma haute considération. Le Directeur des marchés, K.J.S. McKEOWN Annexe Emissions illégales de timbres-poste produites au nom de la République d’Ouzbékistan – Quatorze feuillets-souvenirs intitulés «A HISTORY OF THE STEAM TRAIN» contenant chacun un timbre-poste. Les valeurs indiquées sont de 36 UZS pour huit feuillets, 56 UZS pour quatre feuillets et 75 UZS pour deux feuillets. Sur les timbres sont reproduites l’année «2001», les armoiries de la République d’Ouz­békistan et différentes sortes de trains avec leurs noms. Lesdits feuillets ont été répertoriés sous les numéros UZB0201 à UZB0214. – Un feuillet de six timbres-poste où sont reproduits diverses créatures de la faune, leurs noms et l’inscription «POCHTA 2000». Les valeurs sont de 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS et 2 x 75 UZS, sous le numéro UZB0215. – Un feuillet de six timbres-poste intitulés «YEARS OF SNAKE» reproduisant différents serpents, leurs noms et l’inscription «POCHTA 2000». Les valeurs indiquées sont de 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS et 2 x 75 UZS, sous le numéro UZB0216. – Un feuillet de six timbres-poste illustrant différentes espèces de chiroptères, leurs noms et l’inscription «POCHTA 2000». Les valeurs indiquées sont de 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS et 2 x 75 UZS, sous le numéro UZB0217. – Un feuillet de cinq timbres-poste incorporant à la place du sixième un coupon. Sur ces timbres sont reproduits différentes espèces de périssodactyles, leurs noms et l’inscription «POCHTA 2000». Le coupon reproduit l’image incor- recte du drapeau de l’Etat de la République d’Ouzbékistan et l’inscription «O ZBEKISTON». Les valeurs sont de 2 x 36 UZS, 1 x 56 UZS et 2 x 75 UZS, sous le numéro UZB0218. – Un feuillet de six timbres-poste représentant des lézards, leurs noms et l’ins­cription «POCHTA 2000». Les valeurs sont de 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS et 2 x 75 UZS, sous le numéro UZB0219. – Deux feuillets de format vertical de six timbres-poste chacun où sont repro- duits des oiseaux, leurs noms et l’inscription «POCHTA 2000». Les valeurs sont de 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS et 2 x 75 UZS, sous les numéros UZB0220 et UZB0221. – Quatre feuillets intitulés «THE O’ZBEKISTON TRAINS» de huit timbres-poste chacun, portant l’année «2001», les armoiries de la République d’Ouzbékistan et différentes sortes de trains avec leurs noms. – Concernant ces feuillets, sous le numéro UZB0222, la valeur des timbres est de 75 UZS, sous le numéro UZB0223, la valeur des timbres est de 125 UZS, sous le numéro UZB0224, la valeur des timbres est de 95 UZS et, enfin, sous le numéro UZB0225, la valeur des timbres est de 56 UZS. – Un feuillet de format vertical de six timbres-poste illustrant des pièces d’échecs sur l’échiquier et portant l’inscription «O ZBEKISTON» et l’année «2001». Les valeurs des timbres sont de 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS et 2 x 75 UZS, sous le numéro UZB0226. Des informations complémentaires au sujet des émissions illégales peuvent être obtenues directement de l'UPU, auprès de Madame Maria Libera . Publié le 09-03-02. Modifié le 09-03-03 . title: Illegal Stamp Issues from Uzbekistan | PWO
text: ← UPU Circulars by Country Version française → Illegal Stamp Issues from Uzbekistan Uzbekistan Illegal Issues of Postage Stamps UNIVERSAL POSTAL UNION Berne, 3 March 2003 International Bureau Circular 70 Dear Sir/Madam The Communications and Information Agency of UZBEKISTAN asks me to inform you of the following: "Unidentified individuals have been seeking to discredit our country through the circulation of illegal postage stamp issues. We have been informed of the appear­ance on the philatelic market of counterfeit postage stamps marked "O’ZBEKISTON". These stamps, whose value is marked in Uzbekistan sums, have not been issued by the postal administration of Uzbekistan. "Our administration wishes to make the postal administrations of Union member countries, the philatelic community and collectors aware of the emergence of these counterfeit postage stamps, and urges them not to accept these stamps as postal prepayment or purchase them. "The postal administration of the Republic of Uzbekistan also asks the postal administrations of Union member countries to inform their philatelic partners of the existence and circulation of these counterfeit stamps and exercise vigilance. "A list of the counterfeit postage stamps is annexed." Yours faithfully, K J S McKEOWN Director of Markets Annex Illegal postage stamp issues produced in the name of the Republic of Uzbekistan – Fourteen souvenir sheets entitled "A HISTORY OF THE STEAM TRAIN", each containing one postage stamp. The face values are 36 UZS (sums) for eight of the sheets, 56 UZS for four of the sheets and 75 UZS for two of the sheets. The stamps feature the year "2001", the arms of the Republic of Uzbekistan and various types of trains with their names. The sheets have been assigned the reference numbers UZB0201 to UZB0214. – One miniature sheet of six postage stamps featuring various animals, their names and the inscription "POCHTA 2000". The face values are 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS and 2 x 75 UZS, and the reference number is UZB0215. – One miniature sheet of six postage stamps entitled "YEARS OF SNAKE", featuring various snakes, their names and the inscription "POCHTA 2000". The face values are 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS and 2 x 75 UZS, and the refer­ence number is UZB0216. – One miniature sheet of six postage stamps featuring various species of "chiroptera", their names and the inscription "POCHTA 2000". The face values are 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS and 2 x 75 UZS, and the reference number is UZB0217. – One miniature sheet of five postage stamps featuring a label in place of the sixth stamp. These stamps feature various species of "perissodactyla", their names and the inscription "POCHTA 2000". The label contains an incorrect depiction of the national flag of the Republic of Uzbekistan and is inscribed "O ZBEKISTON". The face values are 2 x 36 UZS, 1 x 56 UZS and 2 x 75 UZS, and the reference number is UZB0218. – One miniature sheet of six postage stamps featuring lizards, their names and the inscription "POCHTA 2000". The face values are 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS and 2 x 75 UZS, and the reference number is UZB0219. – Two vertical miniature sheets of six postage stamps each, featuring birds, their names and the inscription "POCHTA 2000". The face values are 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS and 2 x 75 UZS, and the reference numbers are UZB0220 and UZB0221. – Four miniature sheets of eight stamps each, entitled "THE O’ZBEKISTON TRAINS", inscribed with the year "2001", the arms of the Republic of Uzbekistan and various types of trains with their names. – Sheet number UZB0222 contains stamps with a face value of 75 UZS; sheet number UZB0223 contains stamps with a face value of 125 UZS; sheet number UZB0224 contains stamps with a face value of 95 UZS, and sheet number UZB0225 contains stamps with a face value of 56 UZS. – One vertical miniature sheet of six postage stamps, featuring chess pieces on a chess board, the inscription "O ZBEKISTON" and the year "2001". The face values are 2 x 36 UZS, 2 x 56 UZS and 2 x 75 UZS, and the reference number is UZB0226. More information about the illegal issues can be obtained directly from the UPU, Mrs. Maria Libera . title: Illegal Stamp Issues as Defined by the WADP
text: Fight Against the Illegal Stamp Issues WORLD ASSOCIATION FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF PHILATELY (WADP) General Assembly - Second meeting – 6 October 2000 II A Classification of Fraudulent Issues 5 Fraudulent issues are produced to defraud the post office, the collector and sometimes both. It must be said that very occasionally they are produced for amusement and in such cases are marked False or Faux in the reverse. The list below delineates the major groups of fraudulent issues and some of the details are discussed later. A Forgeries of legitimately issued stamps to defraud the post office. B Forgeries of legitimately issued stamps to defraud the collector (and occasionally the post office). C Phantom stamps from non-existent territories. D Illegal issues for territories which are not entitled to issue stamps. E Unauthorised issues produced under a lapsed contract or a disputed contract. F Unauthorised issues produced in the name of a region not under the control of the central government and of no postal validity even in a local sense. G False stamps produced by fraudsters in the name of an issuing authority with the intent to defraud collectors (and incidentally the postal administration). H Varieties of legally issued stamps, stolen or leaked from archives, printers designers, etc. (note: these can come on the market legitimately eg if a printer ceases business the printers archive is commonly sold on the philatelic market). I "Unethical" issues legally produced by postal administrations, but clearly an abuse of good philatelic practice. III Detailed Comments on the Classes of Fraudulent Issues D Illegal issues for territories which are not entitled to issue stamps 16 This is the current scourge of the philatelic industry. It has prospered on the ignorance of ‘collectors’ who are aware of a territory bearing a certain name but which is just the name of a region of a larger country (which supplies the postal service). These issues are particularly prevalent in respect of regions of the Russian Federation, the CIS states and parts of former Yugoslavia. The so-called "stamps" being issued are equivalent to ‘postage stamps’ being issued for an English county or an American state! 19 The problem requires concerted action by all in the philatelic industry. Postal administrations should be able to prosecute at every opportunity. Organised philately should ensure that such material is not sold at their events. The trade should be able to expel members who deliberately deal in such material where laws are being broken. The philatelic journalists must keep collectors informed that such issues are rubbish and not worth the paper they are printed on. G False stamps produced by fraudsters in the name of an issuing authority with the intent to defraud collectors (and incidentally the postal administration) 24 There are more and more instances of stamps coming onto the market bearing the name of a UPU member country without the knowledge or approval of the country concerned. These are often produced under a legitimate production agreement, but without the express approval or knowledge of the issuing authority. Annex 1 contains a list of postal administrations which have denounced such issues through the UPU circular distribution system over the past three years. At the request of the philatelic partners, such circulars are being regularly sent to the philatelic press, stamp catalogue editors and other interested parties in the philatelic industry. The above excerpts were published with the approval of the WADP. More information about the illegal issues can be obtained from the IB of the UPU, Mrs. Maria Libera . Published: 10/05/2001.
