title: Italia2018 - Websites Competition | PWO
text: Italia2018 - Websites Competition ← Back to Websites Competitions Francaise Websites Competition at the Exhibition of Philatelic Literature in Italy Twenty years after the first FIP evaluation of philatelic websites Victor Manta, PWO Introduction - Websites Competitions Reminder (1999 - 2014) The author of this article participated in almost all mentioned competitions, this being the reason why their unique, largely forgotten history and fate is preserved on the Philatelic Webmasters Organization's (PWO) website. The four FIP Evaluations (1999 - 2003). Here is the place to remember two decisive conclusions of the organizers of the first website competitions, offered by the International Philatelic Federation (FIP): -  It would be a mistake to attempt to evaluate Internet literature against exactly the same benchmarks as printed literature.  Charles J. Peterson, the regrettable President of the FIP philatelic literature commission, who started in 1999 what was announced as an annual evaluation of philatelic sites. -  With regards to websites, I made the ruling that they could not be judged at an international exhibition. This decision comes from the later celebrated Mr. Francis Kiddle, the former Chairman of the FIP Literature Commission. Source . This decision put a sad end, for the ten following years, to the international website competitions! Source . IPHLA 2012 was the first major website competition after the defunct FIP ones. It had the commendable intention to bring a new breath to the long-awaited competitions but succeeded only partially. The reason is that it tried again to evaluate the websites by using the same criteria as for the printed literature and by the same judges. See a PWO analysis of IPHLA 2012 here . ROSSICA 2014 , carried out under the patronage of AIJP (International Philatelic Journalists Association), is remembered as using a weird mixture of incompatible and inadequate rules, and a jury of its own. The results were the ones to be expected. Source . WEBSITES COMPETITION AT ITALIA 2018 Presentation The Philatelic Literature Exhibition Italia 2018 was a specialized national exhibition with international participation, organized by the Federazione fra le Società Filateliche Italiane (FSFI) under the patronage of the Federation of the European Philatelic Associations (FEPA). The First Shock - a long DELAY The exhibition took place between 23 - 25 November 2018 in Verona , one year after it was initially planned. It should have taken place in Milan but was moved to Verona for reasons that were never disclosed. There were no excuses presented by the organizers for the unusually large delay, and NO intention, announced on the website, to refund the many participants who paid much too early for their finally delayed participation. This can be considered as a lack of respect of organizers for the numerous participants. Meanwhile, on the exhibition site, even if 2017 copyrights appear very often on it, the delay became invisible, being thoroughly swept under the rug. Participation Fees and Required Affiliations The participation fee of Euro 40.00 (about US$ 49) was the highest so far for the website competitions. I can only hope that this is not a future trend. On the positive side, the payment of participation fees by via PayPal was an obvious advantage for the participants, as well as the acceptance by the organizers of philatelic websites from all webmasters worldwide, independently of their affiliations (if any). This idea was started by IPHLA 2012 and it should be continued. The Philatelic Literature Exhibition's Website The exhibition's website was the main (or rather the only) communication method used by the organizers, and for this reason it is worth considering. The address of the Italia 2018 website is here . For a website that hosted, among others, an international websites competition, it is a rather Spartan one (an understatement). For example on the page called Images one can read, even now in 2019, that: First pictures will be online on 20 July 2018. It is not obvious to what images this page refers, the page itself being anyway empty! Also regarding the images on this site, following the link "Websites" on the page that lists the websites competition participants and their sites, of 34 sites listed only for 3 (!) of them the images of their entry pages are shown, all others displaying instead the deceptive message : Picture temporarily unavailable. By the way, on this Participants page the site Cif  Unificato srl , that characterizes itself as an E-commerce website, should not be overlooked The Special Regulations Article 1: Competitive Exhibits In accordance with art. 1.4 of the General Regulations of the FIP for the Evaluation of Competitive Exhibits at FIP Exhibitions (GREV), these Special Regulations have been developed to supplement those principles with regard to Philatelic Literature . Source . The application of these General Regulations to the evaluation of the philatelic websites was one of the main problems, ones that were often addressed in the past on the PWO's website. A first remark is that the indiscriminate usage of these Regulations contradicts the old findings of Mr. Peterson (see above reference):  It would be a mistake to attempt to evaluate Internet literature against exactly the same benchmarks as printed literature.  He came to this conclusion after having studied hundreds of philatelic websites, but his warning was largely forgotten by all organizers of websites competitions that followed, including by those of Italia 2018. An excerpt from the Regulations illustrates this: 5.2 For Literature exhibits, the following relative terms are presented to lead the Jury to a balanced evaluation (ref. GREV. art. 5.2): (Relative evaluation terms) Printed Digital Treatment of contents 40 40 Originality, significance and depth of content 40 40 Technical matters 15 15 Presentation 5 5 Total 100 100 Please note that the columns Printed and Digital are identical, which is an early indication of the same approach, considering also that in fact the same judges evaluated all philatelic literature categories. To better understand how the above points were allotted, I asked by e-mail the President of the jury, Mr. Giancarlo Morolli (Italy) and the member of the jury Mr. Bruno Crevato-Selvaggi how was it possible that webmasters who treat for 15 - 20 years the same subject on their multipage websites, and who are presumably among the best connoisseurs of the subjects they deal with, have lost about 15 - 20 points at the Treatment of context and in Originality, significance, and depth of contents . I'm convinced that these webmasters know much more about the subject that they treated than any possible members of the jury, an attitude can be interpreted as a sign of arrogance on their part. Neither of the jury members mentioned above felt compelled to answer my question, this being the reason why I finally gave up the idea of an interview with Mr. Crevato-Selvaggi, after being rejected by Mr. Morolli (see below). Please note in passing the notion of relative terms used in art. 5.2, instead of one that should give a precise indication to the jurors I also asked both jury members about how was implemented the new criterion from the Regulations that refers to the evaluation of the exhibits: "4.4 The criterion "technical matters" requires an evaluation of such aspects as: For digital publications: user interface, search / navigation speed, usability, frequency of update (where pertinent)" . Source . Mr. Morolli addressed this question by following comments: ( ) I was the author of the sentence you quote ( ). Personally I visited most sites different times using both my PC and my tablet, with three different browsers (Opera, Chrome, and Firefox). Other jurors used Safari or Explorer. These are less relevant judging attempts because the browsers' compatibility is not mentioned among the new Regulation criteria, being one that with today's tools is easily achieved and is relatively rarely embarrassing for the users I am really committed to supplement the FEPA Regulations, which resulted out of my effort as leader of a team of experts, with clear and effective guidelines, In this respect I hope that, when I will have reached a satisfactory draft for the FEPA guidelines concerning websites, I could rely on your remarks on the same. As I understand the self-boasting Mr. Morolli, the Regulations are a work in progress under his guidance, and he will rely on my remarks, the ones that I wasn't given the opportunity to express. My intention was to ask him some obvious questions, but the jury's president explained to me that he is too busy to answer them (see also below). I finally mention that neither FIP earlier, nor FEPA or AIJP later ever asked the PWO members to share with them their observations, wishes or complaints, even since we offered to share our experience from the very beginning of philatelic websites competitions. Later we gave up and the result is that we speak about the same things now, we talked about already in the years 1999 - 2003 THE JURY Qualification Excerpt from the Regulations: 9. Composition of the Jury Literature jurors must have a reading ability in at least two languages, one of which must be any of the four official FIP languages (art. 29.3 of the Statutes). Furthermore, at least one of the jurors should have a high level of IT skills. Looking at the list of jurors I could not identify some of them who had participated in earlier websites competition. Of course, I could be wrong but publishing information about their qualification for judging the philatelic websites would have been helpful and reassuring. Because these competitions are so rare, I doubt that the Italia 2018 websites competition jurors accumulated enough significant experience in the field. The high level of IT skills required by Regulations is not relevant in our context of the deep knowledge of the subjects and the necessity of having a true philatelic webmaster heart. For this reason, their unexplained and uncommented awards deserve to be treated with a considerable dose of skepticism and doubt. Communication By the end of November 2018, after the exhibition, I asked Mr. Morolli (the President of the Jury) for an interview, for publication on the PWO site. I was especially interested to learn how can the jury of Italia 2018 help the participating webmasters to improve their sites. Here is his answer (Nov. 27, by e-mail), quoted almost in full: As far as your request are concerned I regret not being available to correspond, at least in the next months. From one side my workload as organizer and jury president (we started judging well in advance) compelled me to put aside a number of personal and professional tasks and now I must take care of them. For instance, yesterday morning I had a medical check-up that should have taken place early September. Furthermore, in Verona I committed with the FEPA President to put promptly on paper what we learnt while judging, so I will be dealing with the preparation of the new guidelines for the evaluation of philatelic literature with particular focus on the digital entries and the websites. In my almost 50 years as FIP juror I have always worked on the feedback to the exhibitors, but at present I must concentrate on regaining control of my priorities. Mr. Morolli, the Jury's President who couldn't find time for an interview with the PWO, an organization that represents so many philatelic webmasters, deserves anyway to be largely known, this being the reason why we publish his allegations and his portrait. Picture's open source - the Jury page of Italy 2018 . It is also instructive to learn that he/they learnt while judging, when an opposite approach seems to be the appropriate one (first learn, then judge, otherwise it confirms the old joke that says that who knows is the one who does the things, and who doesn't know is teaching others - by judging them!). My results Because I know a bit more about the results of my own site and because I'm authorized to freely talk about them, please see below the results of my site Romania as Shown by Its Stamps", with which I participated in the Italia 2018 websites competition. Just to mention that many of its newer articles were also published in printed philatelic magazines from Romania and USA. Due to a calculation error (that I immediately reported to the jury after I received - late, late! - the breakdown of my evaluation), I received successively from the organizers two digital certificates, the first as a Gold medal and the second as a Vermeil medal . Such a misplaced error could be easily avoided if a commonplace Excel-type spreadsheet, with automatic calculations was used, instead of a dumb table, prone to evaluator's calculation errors. Considerations and conclusions after 20 years of websites Evaluations Fortunately, the philatelic webmastering appeared and developed by itself thanks to the desire of worldwide stamp collectors to share their knowledge, and this totally independently of the philatelic organizations (FIP, FEPA, AIJP, etc.). The latter tried, unsuccessfully, to catch up with this spontaneous development, by using a kind of top down methodology and blindly following the guiding idea of we know better what means better. Almost 20 years after its first attempts, and of its failures that quickly followed, organized philately is still struggling to catch up with the stormy increase in the number and popularity of philatelic websites, that took place without its knowledge and approval, while organized philately itself is largely regressing, and thus staying traditional by getting smaller, older and obsolete. At the actual level of philatelic websites, their development is largely achieved, irrespective of the so far misguided efforts of organized philately to judge them. It is up to these organizations to attract the philatelic webmasters into something that is better thought out, thoroughly prepared, entertaining and meaningful, in a world dominated by a web that offers a lot to its users and especially to the younger generations. To achieve these goals, it would be useful for the jurors to descend from the pedestals on which they have installed themselves, by providing the necessary communication tools with the participants and by allowing the latter traceability of their own work. The creation of the PWO has been a first attempt to represent philatelic webmasters and it will continue to carefully watch and comment on future developments, in the interest off all those who are concerned and interested in the future of stamp collecting. title: Czech and Slovak Tradition of Stamp Producing
text: Gerhard Batz, Germany I'm a German stamp collector, born in 1950, married and father of a daughter and two sons. I studied social sciences and worked as market research director in a great German mail order company for many years. At this time, I'm managing director of a small direct marketing company. I started stamp collecting already in my childhood, of course without any clear direction and I only found my specialized philatelic area not before having met my wife. Her parents are so-called "Sudentendeutsche", citizens of the former Czechoslovakia of German origin who had to leave their home in the Czech lands after the war. While visiting our relatives there, one day I found a small album with Czechoslovak pre war stamps and so I started collecting Czechoslovak stamps. And in so doing, I learned a lot about the special philosophy of stamp producing in Czechoslovakia coming from the close relationship between the Czech and Slovak graphic artists and the postal authorities. This again caused in me a deep interest in Czech and Slovak graphic art and it's position within the Czech and Slovak art in general. A stamp gallery with many pictures and information about the Czech and Slovak graphic and stamp art shows my high interest in this topic (unfortunately the complete version only in German, but some parts also in English and Czech). I'm member of the Bund deutscher Philatelisten (BdPh). Since 1998 I maintain a resources site for all collectors of Czech/Slovak stamps. You can find there now the greatest number of links to philatelic websites dealing with Czech and Slovak stamps and philately on the web. My other interests are playing chess, collecting graphic art, rock music particularly from the sixties and soccer/football. When I was younger, I played soccer, but now there is no time enough for sports anymore. I often visit the Czech Republic and of course particularly the capital Prague which can be reached from our residence in less than 4 hours. More about me and my interests can be found on my Things I Like Page . STAMP ART AND ART ON STAMPS - NO DIFFERENCE A short overview to the Czech and Slovak tradition of creating stamps "Naše poštovní známka měla to štěstí, že u jejího zrodu stáli před šedesátí lety takovi umělci jako Alfons Mucha, Jakub Obrovský či V. H. Brunner. V té době ještě nikdo netušil, že tato tvorba stane součastí výtvarného umění a že účinným posláním známky bude umělecké hodnoty šířit." (Our postage stamp had the fortune that 60 years ago such artists like Alfons Mucha, Jakub Obrovský or V. H. Brunner stood at its cradle. At this time no one could foresee, that this art would become part of the fine arts and that artistic values will be spread by sending stamps. Miroslav Nýdl (1978) Leden (January) picture by Josef Mánes (1820-1871) part of the Apostle Clock from the Town Hall in Prague engraved by Bohumil Heinz (1936) Among the great number of stamps which are annually issued in the whole world and on which pictures of great artists are depicted, there are too many, which don't meet the high demands of contemporary graphic art. The interest of collectors in such motifs is leading to an overproduction of stamps which only reproduce the pictures, paintings, drawings or graphics in a photo-mechanical way, e.g. by typography or offset printing. The results mostly are size reduced, profusely colored small pictures whose disproportionally diminuation to the format of a stamp falsifies and unnaturally reproduces the original work of art. There has never been such a way of transforming and showing art on stamps in Czechoslovakia. Nevertheless, there are of course also examples of a very passive "taking over" of or a simply "sketching" from the originals, particularly during the times, when the technical means only allowed unicolored stamps. The gradual development of the print technique to four, five and multicolored stamp graphics lead to the consequence that the artistic standard and challenge changed. Above all, there was a turning away from the linear compactness and from the homogeneous surface of the stamp. This again required a more detailed and dense drawing and engraving of the lines in order to make possible an optimal coloring of the stamp engraved. Therefore the craft of the engraver changed, too. It wasn't anymore a simple and experienced work of his hands, but more it was necessary for him to develop an own understanding of the work to be engraved and to exhaust by his own artistic instinct all possibilities and chances which the work of art is offering. The originality of the so-called "Czechoslovak school of stamp engraving" lies in the fact, that stamp designing is not only an indifferent reproduction of a pattern into steel, but more a particular and special style of stamp creating, moreover an independent artistic and creative world which is recognized as an special kind of art in Czechoslovakia. During the 80 year history of Czech and Slovak stamp creating and producing, not much more than 20 engravers gave this art its face which is admired in the whole world. Therefore the stamp art of Czechoslovak stamps can not be separated from works of art on those stamps. Because of the special kind of creating Czechoslovak stamps, every issue has to be considered as a work of art by its own and stamp art is seen as a special kind of the fine arts in general. Among others, this can also be seen for example in the fact that probably the only university institut,e which is exclusivly dealing with postal graphic, exists at the Academy of Fine Arts in Bratislava. It is ruled by Slovakia's leading stamp engraver Martin Činovský who is educating there a new generation of postal graphic artists. Toaleta mladé ženy (Toilet of a young woman) picture by Tiziano Vecellio (1487-1576) first work of art on a Czechoslovak stamp which was printed multi-colored engraved by Jiří Švengsbír (1965) Bruneta (Brunette) picture by Alfons Mucha (1860-1839) one of many works of art by Mucha on Czechoslovak/Czech stamps engraved by Bedřich Housa (2000) The tradition of Czechoslovak stamp art was founded in 1918, when Alfons Mucha , one of the greatest artists of the Art Nouveau, designed the first Czechoslovak stamp - the so-called "hradčany" issue. Already soon after, other artists continued this tradition. In the years before WWII particularly Max Švabinský , surely the greatest Czech artist after Mucha, has to be mentioned. By his ideas he forced the artistic development of the designing of Czechoslovak stamps (and also banknotes). He was responsible for choosing the best artists of the country for stamp designing, e.g. sculptors like Jakub Obrovský , designers like Jaroslav Benda , graphic artists like Vratislav Hugo Brunner or painters like himself. Besides this, he also had much influence on choosing works of art for depicting on stamps. So you find pictures of well-known Czech artists like Mikoláš Aleš , Josef Mánes , Václav Brožík and many more already among the first stamps of Czechoslovakia in the 20ies and 30ies. Švabinský also forced the use of steel engraving for the stamps. Together with the graphic artist Eduard Karel and with the help of Austria's greatest engraver Ferdinand Schirnböck he himself created the first Czechoslovak stamp in this technique already in 1920. Later he promoted and patronized the two great engravers of the Czechoslovak pre-war time - first the German Karl Seizinger and later Bohumil Heinz who became a national idol for many Czech graphic artists. During their more than 80 year history, Czech and Slovak stamps always have been determined by the high quality level of their engravers. Great milestones in the development of Czechoslovak stamps were set by those craftsmen of stamp art. Jindra Schmidt in cooperation with Max Švabinský was responsible for the first multi-colored stamps in Czechoslovakia - a 9-value series of butterflies in 1961 (MiNr. 1301-1309). Jiří Švengsbír transferred the first work of art into a multicolored Czechoslovak stamp in 1965 - Tizian's "Toilet of a Young Woman" (MiNr. 1560) - and started with this stamp the annual row "umění" (=art), in which every year great works of art are depicted, engraved in the individual style of the engraver. In 1966, Josef Herčík gained international reputation by his transposition of Picasso's over-dimensioned picture "Guernica" into the tiny from of a stamp (MiNr. 1637). Other engravers like for example Miloš Ondráček or Bedřich Housa and other ones transfer great works of art onto stamps of the "umění" series every year. Splynutí duší (High Time of Feelings) picture by Max Švabinský (1873-1962) issue to Švabinský's 100th birthday engraved by Jindra Schmidt (1973) Guernica picture by Pablo Picasso (1881-1973) commemorating the 30th anniversary of the beginning of the Spanish Civil War engraved by Josef Herčík (1966) Detail from "Rosenkranzfest" (Rosary Celebration) picture by Albrecht Dürer (1471-1528) Top highlight of works of arts on Czechoslovak stamps engraved by Miloš Ondráček (1989) This "umění" series and also all other stamps of Czechoslovakia and the modern Czech Republic have mostly been created by members of the HOLLAR association of the Czech print artists in which the top 150 graphic artists are united. Therefore the list of the Czech and Slovak stamp designers can be read as a "Who's who" of the whole graphic art in both of the countries. The modern Czech Republic and Slovakia are continuing with this tradition of stamp creating and engraving and also with the series "umění". While in the formerCzechoslovakia usually five works of art were issued, mainly by Czech and Slovak artists, the successor states issue two or three works every year. As a rule, Czech and Slovak artists are honored by a stamp, but often also international ones like Picasso , Rubens or El Greco or some from the German language countries like Albrecht Dürer , Lucas Cranach or modern painters like Max Ernst . Although there is a discussion about using more "modern" print technologies in stamp producing and not more such "old-fashioned" ones like today, we should hope that the Czech Republic as well as Slovakia will still maintain their tradition and high quality level in designing and engraving stamps for a long time. title: PWO - Le but de la Page de membre
text: Le but de la Page de membre L'objectif général de l'Organisation des Webmasters Philatéliques (PWO) et de ses membres est de promouvoir la philatélie dans le monde entier. C'est pourquoi il est de l'intérêt de la PWO de faire la meilleure promotion possible du travail créatif de ses membres, c'est-à-dire leurs propres sites. Un des meilleurs moyens pour atteindre cet objectif est de présenter les pages attrayantes et intéressantes de nos membres avec des liens vers leurs sites personnels. Dans ces pages figurent également de brèves informations relatives au Webmaster qui les a réalisées. C'est la raison pour laquelle nous avons l'intention de publier sur le site de la PWO une page de liens donnant accès aux pages les plus représentatives de nos membres. Ensuite, lorsque nous serons plus nombreux, nous mettrons ces liens dans la base de données des membres, et mentionnerons principalement sur la page de liens ceux relatifs à des pages qui auront été primées lors de concours (voir ci-dessous à propos des futurs concours). Vos pages doivent être publiées sur votre propre site ; nous vous demandons de nous communiquer les liens pour les atteindre. Vous êtes libres d'inclure ou non ces pages dans votre site. En les faisant connaître par l'intermédiaire de la PWO, il est implicite que la PWO détient également un droit de copie sur les pages publiées, et peut utiliser ces dernières dans le cadre de ce qui est décrit ci-après. La PWO n'utilisera ce droit que pour faire de la publicité à la création philatélique sur le Web et à ses membres. Cette publicité sera faite sur le Web, par l'intermédiaire du site de la PWO, et éventuellement ultérieurement par des CD-Rom, réalisés par la PWO, qui pourraient être présentés lors d'événements philatéliques à titre promotionnel pour la POW et pour ses membres. Les titulaires des pages concernées seront informés en temps voulu, et pourront faire part de leurs objections éventuelles. Toute utilisation commerciale des Pages de Membre par la PWO, ou par quiconque, est expressément interdite. Un concours primé des pages de membre PWO sera annoncé ultérieurement. Pour simplifier les choses, nous commencerons avec des pages et non avec des sites complets. Cela permettra aux membres intéressés d'acquérir une expérience pratique dans l'appréciation du travail de leurs collègues en création philatélique sur le Web. Le texte du règlement sera proposé sur ce site et discuté dans le forum PWO. Les jurés seront tous les membres de la PWO qui auront exprimé le désir de participer à cet intéressant challenge. Instructions relatives à la présentation des Pages de Membre Pour atteindre nos objectifs, nous souhaitons que les Pages de Membre aient une structure uniforme, comme expliqué ci-dessous. Cela signifie : Faire figurer en premier le sigle de notre Organisation, en utilisant le fichier www.pwmo.org/ttl-pwo.gif . Mettre votre nom en titre. Écrire un texte court, mais pertinent, vous concernant. Insérer des liens vers celles de vos pages que vous voulez présenter (5 pages maximum). En bas de page, merci de faire figurer : (mm = mois, jj = jour, aa = année) Créé le mm/jj/01. Modifié le mm/jj/aa. Copyright © 2001 Prénom Nom , Pays. Tous droits réservés dans le monde entier. Votre nom peut comporter un lien soit vers votre site, si vous n'avez pas de bannière, soit vers votre adresse électronique. La bannière (si vous en avez une) de votre site avec lien vers celui-ci. Le logo de PWO, ici à droite, que vous trouverez également à http://pwmo.org/images/pwo-logo.gif . Veuillez y ajouter un lien vers http://pwmo.org . Comme dit par ailleurs, vous pouvez utiliser ma page personnelle, publiée dans ce but sur le site PWO, comme base de mise en page. Elle sera déplacée ultérieurement vers mon site personnel. Veuillez cliquer ici pour l'ouvrir dans une nouvelle fenêtre. Nos membres sont cordialement invités à nous soumettre par e-mail leurs liens vers les pages qu'ils auront choisi. Créé le 02/03/01. Modifié le 06/30/02 . Copyright © 2001 - 2002 PWO et Victor Manta , Suisse. Tous droits réservés dans le monde entier. Language

title: PWO Members Pages - Goals
text: The Goal of Members Pages The general goal of the Philatelic Webmasters Organization and of its members is to promote philately worldwide. That's why it is in the interest of the PWO to promote at best the creative work of its members, i.e. their own sites. One of the best means to attain this goal is to promote attractive, interesting pages of our members, connected through links to their own sites. These pages publish also a short information about the webmasters who developed them. That's why we intend to publish on the PWO site a page of links toward the representative pages of our members. Later, after the number of our members has grown, we will include these links into the database of our members and we will probably publish on this page of links mainly links to pages awarded through contests (please read below about future contests). Your pages will be published on your own sites; you are asked to provide us only functioning links to them. It is up to you to include or not these pages into your own sites. By advertising them through the PWO, it is implicit that also the PWO has copyright to the published pages, and can use them for the purposes mentioned immediately hereafter. The PWO will use that right only for making publicity for the philatelic webmastering and for its members. This publicity will be made on the Web, through the PWO site, and maybe later through CD-ROMs made by the PWO, that could be presented at philatelic events as publicity for the PWO and for its members. The owners of such pages will in time be asked if they object to such publication. Any commercial use of Members Pages by the PWO or by others is explicitly prohibited. A contest of PWO Members Pages will be announced at a later time, with awards to be won. We will start with pages and not with sites simply because it is easier. This will bring to our interested members a practical experience in judging the work of their colleagues in philatelic webmastering. The awarding rules will be proposed on this site and will be discussed in the PWO Forum. The judges will be all PWO members who will express their wish to participate in this interesting challenge. Indications for the presentation of Members Pages In order to attain our objectives, we ask the webmasters to maintain an uniform structure of Members Pages, as explained below. That means: Start with the name of our organization. File to be used: www.pwmo.org/ttl-pwo.gif Your name, as title A short, but relevant presentation of yourself Link(s) to my PWO member's page(s): (Note. Limited to max. 5 pages) At the bottom of the page please include (mm = month, dd = day, yy = year): Created: mm/dd/01. Revised: mm/dd/yy. Copyright © 2001 by YOUR NAME , Your Country. All rights reserved worldwide. You can link YOUR NAME either to your site (if you haven't a banner) or to your e-mail address. The banner of your site (if you have one), linked to your site. The PWO logo, found on the right and also callable from: www.pwmo.org/images/pwo-logo.gif . Please link it to: www.pwmo.org As already mentioned, you can use as an example of formatting my own page, published for this purpose on the PWO site. It will be moved later to my own site. Please click here to load it in a separate window. The PWO members are kindly invited to submit by e-mail links to their pages to the PWO. Created: 02/03/01. Revised: 09/16/01 . Copyright © 2001 by PWO and by Victor Manta, Switzerland All rights reserved worldwide. Language

title: PWO - Galerie de membres
text: Galerie des Membres À l'Organisation des Webmasters Philatéliques nous avons pensé qu'un moyen intéressant d'aide à la promotion de la philatélie sur le Web était de donner à nos membres la possibilité d'utiliser le site PWO afin de montrer quelques-unes de leurs pages les plus attractives ou représentatives. De plus les membres de la PWO peuvent se faire mieux connaître au travers d'une fiche personnelle. Nous espérons que vous apprécierez ce que nos membres vous présentent. Victor Manta , Suisse. Liens vers des pages concernant "l'art sur les timbres" : la première relative à "l'amour", et la seconde aux "récents événements dans les Balkans tourmenté". Oblitérations des Nations Unies sont présenté sur la troisième page. Frank Daems, Belgique. Liens vers un page sur les combinaisons des timbres canadiens se tenant, une sur les impressions dans les marges des timbres des îles anglo-normandes et de l'île de Man, et une sur les émissions européennes relatives au transport par rail. André Hurtré , France. Liens vers : une page du site de l'Académie de Philatélie ("tous les articles publiés depuis 1959"), une autre relative aux coupons-réponse ("coupons-réponse internationaux"), et une dernière sur les entiers postaux français ("les aérogrammes"). Gerhard Batz, Allemagne. Liens vers des pages relatives à l'art et aux artistes tchèques et slovaques. Toon Oomens, Hollande . Liens vers des pages relatives à la province de Zeeland, aux prix Nobel et à un club de jeunes. Daniel Roudeillac, France. Liens vers quelques pages représentatives de la démarche du site "Timbres et Défense", sous ses approches thématiques et géopolitiques. Lars Engelbrecht , Danemark. Des cartes postales bicolores danoises et leur s identification. Les membres de la PWO sont cordialement invités à nous soumettre par e-mail le lien vers la page qu'ils ont créée. Ils obtiendront des détails complémentaires en cliquant ici . Quant aux visiteurs, nous leur demandons d'avoir l'obligeance de nous faire savoir, également par email , ce qu'ils pensent des pages présentées, ainsi que de notre Organisation. Les commentaires les plus pertinents seront publiés (sous forme anonyme) sur ce site. Merci d'avance ! Créé le 24 juillet 2001. Mis à jour le 26.08.04 . title: PWO - Members Pages
text: Members Gallery We at the Philatelic Webmasters Organization have found that an interesting mean to promote philately on the Web is to give our members the possibility to use their PWO site in order to show some of their most attractive and most representative pages. In the same time the PWO members get the opportunity to present themselves, through an introductory page. We hope that you will like that what our members have to show. Please visit the PWO Gallery of pages. Victor Manta , Switzerland. Links to Arts on Stamp pages, related the first one to Love and the second one to recent events in the tormented Balkans. title: Damaged Paintings from Romanian Museums, on Stamps
text: SHOT PAINTINGS The Romanian people, sick and tired of 45 years of an oppressive regime, of the dictatorship of the unique Communist party and of the person who represented it during the last 25 years, the dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, upraised against and deposed the regime in December 1989. During the revolt, some mysterious forces, that weren't identified till now, have shot on mainly disarmed citizens who manifested for freedom on the streets of Bucharest, the capital of Romania. The army, who quickly rejoined the demonstrators, has retorted the unseen killers with guns and sometimes with artillery. During these street battles many objects were damaged, traces of bullets and of fire being seen during many years on the buildings of Bucharest. Unfortunately the paintings found in the National Art Museum have also suffered severe damages. These damages have profoundly impressed the amateurs of art and the population alike and for this reason on October 25, 1990, only 10 months after the described events, the Romania postal administration has issued a quite unusual set of six stamps, showing damaged masterpieces of Romanian and foreign masters. All stamps of the set mention on the top Tablouri împuscate, with the meaning Shot Paintings. On the paintings displayed on the right you can see the impacts of bullets. The stamps of a rather inferior quality, as compared with the stamp on the left side, This stamp on the right was issued by the same country 22 years earlier, in 1968. This masterpiece of Romanian art was painted by Stefan Luchian and represents Old Nicholas, the Cobza (Zither) player. Scott numbers: 2000 and 3620. In the meantime the painting was restored and is exhibited at the National Museum of Arts in Bucharest, Romania. This page displays all other stamps of the set, as follows: 1.50 L. Woman in Blue, by Ion Andreescu . Scott 3621. 4 L. Spring Time, by Peter Brueghel, the Elder. Scott 3624. 2 L. The Gardener (Safta, the Florist), by Stefan Luchian . Scott 3622. 3 L. Vase of Flowers, by Jan Brueghel, the Elder. Scott 3623. 5. L. Madonna and Child, by B. Paggi. Scott 3625. Please notice that not much was left of it, so it looks rather like a modern painting. I'm sure that one day, eventually with the help of international specialists, all these wonderful works of art will be restored and that I'll have the pleasure to show you them in their original state. All in all an impressive set, acting as a memory flash and revealing a short piece of recent history that has shaken one more country in the tormented Balkan Peninsula. This wasn't for the first time that Romanian masterpieces or their legal holders suffered. In the year 1956, after 39 years, the government of the former USSR returned to Romania works of art that were evacuated in 1917 during the WW I by the Romanian government. Among these works were also paintings of the renown Romanian artist Ion Andreescu. Big was the surprise when it was discovered that many of these paintings were replaced by fakes (the Andreescu's painting on the left is an original one). Of course nothing could be done under the political circumstances of that time. Today is too late. Source: Ioan Andreescu, p.9. Alcor Edimpex, June 1997, ISBN 973-97901-4-3. SHOT - THEN SURCHARGED ! Roughly 10 years after their issue, the first five values of the set were overprinted and surcharged with a new value of Lei 1700. This value corresponded in the year 2000 to the fee for a domestic letter. The old face value was covered by a black image of an easel, in the "tradition" of all recent overprints of the Romanian post. To cheer up the things, during a trip to Romania I let cancelling a whole set on a letter. I have chosen a date that tells something to me, that of September 19, 2000, the day of my birth anniversary. The clerk at the postal office No. 45, on the Brezoianu Street in Bucharest has done it with a lot of professionalism, and even with an obvious enthusiasm when I have told her why have I chosen that very day to cancel the stamps. Please notice that the value of Lei 5 wasn't surcharged because it was for a longer time out of stock, due to its limited printed quantity of only 250,000, as compared with 800,000 to 3,000,000 pieces for the other stamps of the set. The image above shows only the upper part of the cover, that has on its bottom part other two stamps, in order to attain the franking value of Lei 12,300, the price of an air mail letter sent from Romania to Switzerland. Actually quite expensive, compared with the year 2000's income of most Romanians. Created 08/04/00. Revised: 09/16/01 . Copyright © 2001 by Victor Manta, Switzerland. All rights reserved worldwide. title: PWO Page de membre du Victor Manta
text: Victor Manta, Suisse Je suis un collectionneur suisse de timbres-poste, né en 1944, marié et père d'une fille. Je suis spécialisé en management technique et en communication inter-culturelle , et suis titulaire d'une maîtrise de physique. Depuis environ 35 ans j'ai choisi l'art sur les timbres comme principal centre d'intérêt philatélique, mais d'autres thèmes m'intéressent également. Parmi eux, l'histoire vue au travers des timbres. En février 2001 j'ai fondé la Philatelic Webmasters Organization (PWO), en en devenant son Président et un de ses principaux animateurs. Je suis membre de l'Union des associations philatéliques suisses. En 1996 j'ai fondé le "Paintings and Arts on Stamps Internet Club" ( PASIC - Club Internet dédié à la peinture et aux arts sur timbres-poste), une association qui a été rejointe par plus de 300 membres originaires de plus de 55 pays différents. PASIC est affilié à la plus importante association thématique mondiale , ATA (American Topical Association). Mes autres domaines d'intérêt sont la publication sur le Web, l'informatique, les arts visuels, la musique et la philosophie. Je suis également particulièrement intéressé par la Roumanie, tant en ce qui concerne son art et son histoire, que ses timbres. Comme autres passe-temps, je devrais mentionner le tennis et le tennis de table, aussi bien en tant que joueur que spectateur. Liens vers mes pages PWO : L'amour dans l'art Tableux roumains fusillés Nations Unies Genève : Une administration postale amicale avec les philatélistes. Créé le 24 juillet 2001. Mis à jour le 16.09.01 . Copyright © 2001 par PWO et par Victor Manta, Suisse Tous droits réservés mondialement. Language

title: PWO Member Page of Victor Manta
text: Victor Manta, Switzerland I'm a Swiss stamp collector, born 1944, married and father to a daughter. Specialized in management, computer programming and electronics, I hold a MS degree in physics. A long time ago ago I have chosen the Arts on Stamps as my main philatelic area of interest, but other topics interest me as well. One of these is the history as seen through the stamps of issuing countries. In February 2001, after a quite long and sustained activity as a Web philatelist, I have founded the Philatelic Webmasters Organization ( PWO ). I'm its current President and one of its principal animators. I'm member of the Union of Swiss Philatelic Associations. In 1996 I have founded the Paintings and Arts on Stamps Internet Club ( PASIC ), an association that was joined by over 500 members from over 60 countries. PASIC is affiliated with the biggest topical association worldwide, the ATA (American Topical Association). In 1998 I have founded the Topicals Stamps Club on Yahoo, joined so far by over 300 stamp collector. My other domains of interests are Web publishing, computers, visual arts, music and philosophy. I'm also specially interested in Romania, as much in its art and history as in its stamps . As other hobbies I would mention tennis and table tennis, playing as much as watching. Links to my PWO member's pages: Venus, by Rubens Romanian Shot Paintings United Nations Geneva : A Philatelic Friendly Postal Administration Created 08/04/00. Revised: 01/15/06 . title: New PWO Member, New Site Entry Form
text: DEMANDE D'ADHESION ET/OU D'AJOUT D'UN SITE PWO est une organisation pour les Webmasters Philatéliques, une organisation faite pour les webmasters qui créent des sites philatéliques. Nous souhaitons admettre uniquement ceux qui créent des sites dont le contenu a un intérêt philatélique. Veuillez vous abstenir si vos pages sont purement commerciales ou une collection de liens, c'est à dire ne pas demander d'admission de sites ou le visiteur philatéliste n'a rien à apprendre, à aimer ou à admirer. Nous ne nous attendons pas à ce que vous soyez un expert en philatélie, mais tout webmaster dont le site a un quelconque intérêt philatélique, tout amateur qui veut montrer ou dire quelque chose au sujet des timbres et qui présente un site philatélique (mais pas un de ces sites vite faits avec seulement deux à trois pages) est le bienvenu parmi nous. Veuillez entrer ci-dessous les informations relatives au nom de site et l'URL principale et non pas des pages individuelles, même traîtant de sujets différents !!! Votre nom apparaîtra sur notre liste autant de fois que vous, en tant que Webmaster, avez créé ou maintenez des sites philatéliques différents. Notez que votre adresse email est affichée uniquement dans la page des membres, voilà pourquoi seuls les membres de PWO y ont accès. Pour adhérer à la Philatelic Webmasters Organization, veuillez utiliser le formulaire ci-dessous. Lisez les Statuts avant d'envoyer votre demande pour devenir membre de la PWO et ne soumettez votre site que si vous acceptez ceux-ci. Si vous serez admis, vous pouvez demander votre nom d'utilisateur et mot de passe par e-mail. Vous pouvez vous considérer comme admis si l'enregistrement de votre nom et site figure avec persistance dans notre liste des membres. Nous attendons de vous de publier un lien sur votre première page de votre site vers la PWO, en utilisant le logo ci dessous, afin de faire connaitre notre organisation aux autres collectionneurs et webmasters. Si pour une quelconque raison vous ne pouvez afficher notre logo en première page, alors affichez-le dans votre page de liens ou sur une page ou vous écrivez sur vous-même. Par le fait que il y a tant des liens vers la liste des membres de la PWO, vous beneficiez d'une très grande visibilité sur le Web. Il vous est demandé de placer le lien http://www.pwmo.org sur cette image ( http://www.pwmo.org/images/pwo-logo.gif - vous pouvez la télécharger ou utiliser le lien vers elle) pour augumenter cette visibilité . N'oubliez pas svp de signaler les changements de votre URL ou de votre adresse email. Périodiquement nous enlèverons les liens de sites dont les liens n'ont pas été mis à jour. Demande d'adhésion à la PWO Merci d'avoir postulé ! Created: Jan. 16, 2019. Revised: Feb. 5, 2019 . Copyright © 2019 by PWO and by Victor Manta, Switzerland. All rights reserved worldwide. After having joined us, the members should use the PWO banner on the first page of their sites or on the links page and to link it to the PWO site at: http://www.pwmo.org

title: Join PWO | Philatelic Webmasters Organization
text: Join PWO and/or Add New Sites This is a Philatelic Webmasters Organization, an organization thought for webmasters who create philatelic sites. We expect that only those webmasters join, who can propose sites showing some philatelic contents of interest. Please abstain if your pages are purely commercial, trade, just collection of links, etc., i.e. where a stamp collectors cannot learn/admire/love something. We don't expect that you are an expert in your philatelic field or that you have a degree in computing, that's why any stamps fan who wishes to show or to say something about stamps, and who presents a philatelic site (but not his quickly and dirty made 2-3 pages!) is kindly invited. Please enter below information referring to sites names and URLs and not to individual pages (even if the pages treat different subjects)!!! Your name should appear several times on the list only if you, as a webmaster, have created and/or maintain several different philatelic sites . title: PWO Forum
text: PWO MEMBERS FORUM VISITING PWO FORUM FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND REGISTRATION. The easiest way for entering in our PWO Forum is by clicking (once) on "Forum" ... Choose a user name and a password (and write them somewhere, if you've to many other passwords to remember). Your user name will be shown on all your forum messages, so please try to let it be understandable for other members (for example Victor Manta is "manvic", and André Hurtré is "Andre"). Your password should remain confidential. Overwrite "Gast" with your user name, and enter your password. You may also select "Save my login info for next time" (you will see later how much will be saved - normally only the password). As far as we know software makes not difference between caps and lower cases letters. Both your user name and password are working either from an English page or from a French one. But they are valid only in the Forum zone. A new window ("Please Register") will be opened, after having clicked on "REGISTER". Please add the required information ("Username" and "Password" must be the same ones that those you've entered in the previous window). Clicking on "REGISTER" will register you as a life time member of our Forum. Please select (from left menu) "APWP" for the PWO Forum. You're welcomed on board ! VISITING AGAIN If you want visit again your PWO Forum, you will have to enter your Username and your Password (the ones you've written somewhere ... you know where) and to click on "EINLOGGEN". In the new window, don't forget to select "APWP". Other buttons seems to be fully understandable for our English speaking members Use "PRIVATE MESSAGE" only when you are sure that your addressee expects to get private post. And the most important, participate actively to your Forum! For this please click on the button shown below: Created: 08/06/01, by André Hurtré, France. Revised: 09/16/01 . title: Forum de la PWO
text: FORUM DES MEMBRES DE LA PWO PREMIER ACCÈS AU FORUM ET INSCRIPTION Un clic sur "Forum" vous donne accès à la "barrière d'entrée". Choisissez un nom d'utilisateur. C'est ce nom qui figurera comme identifiant sur tous vos messages (merci donc d'en choisir un relativement explicite ; par exemple, Victor Manta est "manvic" et André Hurtré est "Andre") et inscrivez-le à la place de "Gast" dans le cadre "Username" ( notez-le ... et souvenez-vous de l'endroit où vous l'avez noté). Choisissez un mot de passe (qui restera votre secret), inscrivez-le dans le cadre "Password" ( et notez-le aussi, avec l'autre ...). Nom d'utilisateur et mot de passe fonctionnent aussi bien à partir de la zone anglaise que de la zone française du site PWO. Mais ces deux éléments ne concernent que le forum. Le logiciel ne fait, semble-t-il, aucune différence entre majuscules et minuscules. Vous pouvez cocher la case figurant devant "Save my login info for next time". C'est sans risque, mais pas forcément efficace ... Après un clic sur "REGISTER", une nouvelle fenêtre ("Please Register") s'ouvre pour confirmer et compléter votre inscription. Mettez : dans "Username", votre nom d'utilisateur (celui indiqué dans la fenêtre précédente) ; dans "Password", votre mot de passe (le même que dans la fenêtre précédente) ; de nouveau ce mot de passe dans le cadre suivant pour confirmation ; dans "First name", votre prénom ; dans 'Last name", votre nom ; dans "E-mail" ... trouvez vous-même et, même remarque que plus haut pour "Save my login info for next time". Un clic sur "REGISTER" confirme définitivement votre inscription comme membre permanent du Forum. Vous pouvez alors y accéder (choisir "APWP" pour le Forum PWO). Bienvenue à bord ! Y RETOURNER ET S'EN SERVIR Pour y retourner, inscrivez vos nom d'utilisateur et mot de passe (ceux que vous avez précédemment notés, mais où ?), puis faire un clic sur "EINLOGGEN" pour entrer (puis sur "APWP"). Quelques autres explications : après avoir consulté un message, utiliser "REPLY" (en bas) pour y répondre, puis "SEND" pour l'envoyer ; "POST" pour créer un nouveau message, puis "SEND" pour l'envoyer ; "SEARCH" vous permet(tra) de rechercher dans les (très nombreux futurs) messages le mot qui vous intéresse ; "MY PROFILE" vous remémore les informations vous concernant (inscrites lors que votre inscription), et peut vous permettre de les modifier ; "PRIVATE MESSAGES" est une BAL pour correspondre confidentiellement avec un membre du Forum (message à adresser à son nom d'utilisateur ). Nous vous suggérons de ne pas l'utiliser (préférez les e-mails directs) ... si vous espérez avoir une réponse. "LOGOUT" pour retourner à la barrière d'entrée du Forum. Et surtout, n'hésitez pas à participer activement au Forum PWO (cliquer sur le bouton s.v.p)! Publié le 16-08-01-01 par André Hurtré. Modifié le 16-09-01 . title: Italy 2018. Competition des sites philatéliques
text: English Considérations et conclusions après 20 ans d'évaluations de sites Web Victor Manta, PWO Cet article est un extrait de l'analyse de l'exposition Italia 2018, qui est publié en anglaise ici . Heureusement, le webmastering philatélique est apparu et s'est développé de lui-même grâce à la volonté des collectionneurs de timbres du monde entier de partager leurs connaissances, et ceci totalement indépendante des organisations philatéliques (FIP, FEPA, AIJP, etc.). Ces derniers ont tentés, sans succès, de rattraper ce développement spontané, en utilisant une sorte de méthodologie top-down et en suivant aveuglément l'idée directrice «nous savons mieux ce qui signifie mieux». Près de 20 ans après ses premiers essais et ses échecs qui ont suivi rapidement, la philatélie organisée a toujours du mal à rattraper la progression rapide en nombre et popularité des sites Web philatéliques, qui se sont développés indépendamment et sans sa approbation, tandis que la philatélie organisée est en grande partie en régression et reste donc "traditionnel", en devenant plus petit, plus vieux et obsolète. Au niveau actuel des sites Web philatéliques, leur développement est largement réalisé, quels que soient les efforts jusqu'ici mal orientés de la philatélie organisée pour les juger. Il appartient à ces organisations d'attirer les webmasters philatéliques vers quelque chose de mieux réfléchi et bien préparé, dans un monde dominé par un Web qui offre beaucoup à ses utilisateurs et en particulier aux jeunes générations. Pour atteindre ces objectifs, il serait utile que les jurés descendent des socles sur lesquels ils se sont installés, en fournissant les outils nécessaires de communication avec les participants et en permettant à ceux-ci de suivre leur travail. La création de la PWO a été une première tentative de représentation de webmasters philatéliques. Elle continuera à surveiller de près et à commenter les développements futurs, dans l'intérêt de tous ceux qui sont concernés et intéressés par l'avenir de la philatélie. Created: Jan. 13, 2019. Revised: Jan. 13, 2019 . Copyright © 2019 by PWO and by Victor Manta, Switzerland All rights reserved worldwide. Language

title: APWP - Reasons
text: Our Reasons and Goals The Association of Philatelic Web Publishers (APWP) has been created in order to promote, support and develop philately through publishing activity on the Web. There are many national and international organizations that group the stamp collectors or the philatelic professionals representing their interests. At the moment there is no organization grouping the recently appeared category of stamp collectors who combine their philatelic hobby with the Web publishing activity. On these pages such stamp collectors are called the "Web Publishers" (WP). The WP are quite different from the philatelic journalists, meaning here those who work for philatelic journals and who are grouped in the International Association of Philatelic Journalists (AIJP). The main difference is that most of WP are amateurs. They bring to the Net what they love so much: their stamps and information about them and their knowledge about Web publishing. All of them started by themselves, being pushed by the impulse to share with others what they like, and by their interest to explore a new dimension of the human communication, made possible by the technological (r)evolution. For many of WP the newsgroup rec.collecting.stamps.discuss was till now the only place where they could discuss their problems, or where they could announce their new pages. But they had and still have to take in consideration the interests of the majority of participants, interests that aren't focused on Web publishing. Some of us, the most advanced and/or the most brave, have participated at Web competitions proposed by organizations representing the traditional philately (like FIP, MIDAPHIL). We were often disappointed by the juries' lack of knowledge and/or lack of understanding of the specificity of Web publishing. The noting criteria were not clear or absent, the qualification of judges in Web publishing was unknown and the promised score sheets never arrived. In the last years the number of young stamp collectors has continually diminished. New possibilities, like exciting games, computers and Internet became more attractive than stamp collecting. Through the Web publishing activity in the philatelic domain, we have a new chance to regain the young generations' interest for stamp collecting. For all these reasons the time has come that we, the Web Publishers, take our destiny in our own hands! The best mean to solve our own problems and to attain our goals is to act together, as members of a structured organization. These are the reasons why we have established the Association of Philatelic Web Publishers (APWP). Our big advantage is that we have the means and the knowledge to efficiently communicate worldwide, with a matchless efficiency and at minimal costs. What can an APWP member expect from his organization and from his colleagues: He (and she) is listed on the Members List, together with many others who share his interests. This not only makes his site and himself better visible, but also presents him in the proper context of sites that have many characteristics in common . As member he will get listed the name of his site, the topic (or the specialization for commercial sites), the kind of site (Homepage, Commercial, Postal Authority, Organization), the URL of his site, his name as the author of his site, the language, the country where he lives and his e-mail address. The membership facilitates the relationship and the exchange of experience between him and other members, thus encouraging direct contacts. The APWP organizes on-line study groups, meetings, forums, common exhibitions and other activities. Periodically the APWP proposes different kinds of Web sites competitions (worldwide, regional, thematic, etc.), for different levels, judged by juries who are competent in their field. The judges use clearly established and widely known criteria. A member has the possibility to announce the results of his work (new sites or pages) on a specialized Forum and to publish pages of general interest on the APWP site. Through the interaction with many other members who share his interests, he can take profit as much from the technical expertise as from the artistic and philatelic experience of all members. Member's privacy is protected by the APWP Statutes . Some of the proposed facilities, like the on-line joining of the APWP and the free listing of all members on a Web site, are offered from the very beginning. The totality of the stated objectives will be attained gradually, just in time when a certain critical mass of members has been reached. And last, but not least, the success of the APWP depends of the activity of us, its members. The results depend of our imagination, initiative and spirit of collaboration. Together we will succeed! The APWP members are entitled to use the APWP members logo, shown below. Please link this image to the APWP site: http://www.values.ch/apwp.htm Victor Manta Founder, Feb. 2001 Arts on Stamps APWP Statutes APWP Members List Click here to send us an e-mail Click here to join the APWP. It's free . Created: 02/03/01. Revised: 11/27/05 . Copyright � 2001 by APWP & by Victor Manta, Switzerland All rights reserved worldwide. Language

title: Site Awarded in Pakistan | PWO
text: Site Awarded in Pakistan A website was awarded at the National Stamps Exhibition "Lahore 2009" The Pakistan Philatelic Association with the collaboration of Pakistan post, Philatelic Federation of Pakistan and Lahore Museum Lahore organized a National Stamps Exhibition “Lahore 2009” from 21-23 March, 2009 at Lahore City Heritage Museum (Tolinton Market) Lahore. The Classes in the Exhibition were Traditional, Postal History, Postal Stationary, Aero philately, Thematic, Revenue, Youth and Literature. Collectors from all over the country participated in that exhibition. Rana Shamshad Ahmad, Post Master General, Pakistan Post, awarding a Vermeil Medal to Akhtar ul Islam Siddiqui on his website Pakistan Philately For the first time in the history of Pakistan a website, Pakistan Philately, was submitted in the literature section of a national philatelic exhibition. The website was presented on a CD. The jury examined the website, that consisted of a Catalogue of Pakistan Postage Stamps from 1947 to March 2009, News & Articles on Pakistan Philately, a List of Philatelic Literature & Associations, a Philatelists Directory and more. The website was accepted by the organizers and it was awarded a Vermeil Medal. The jury who decided the awards consisted of Mr. Salman Qureshi, a prominent philatelist and Ex. President of the Philatelic Federation of Pakistan, Chairman Col. Nasir Hussain and Imtiaz Hussain Rizvi, General Secretary of the Philatelic Federation of Pakistan. The collectors at exhibition hall commented that it was a rather a magazine then a simple webpage. A beautiful envelope & exhibition brochure were issued by Pakistan Philatelic Association. title: 25 Years of PWO (2001–2026) | Philatelic Webmasters Organization
text: 2001 — 2026 25 Years of PWO A Quarter-Century of Philately on the Internet From the first generation of philatelic websites to international virtual exhibitions, PWO has encouraged collectors to share knowledge, defend philatelic integrity and give digital publishing a voice. In 2001, creating a philatelic website was still a pioneering undertaking. Collectors were discovering that the Internet could do much more than advertise collections: it could preserve research, connect specialists across continents and make philatelic information available to anyone with a connection. The Philatelic Webmasters Organization (PWO) was established to encourage precisely that development. In 2026, it celebrates twenty-five years of work on behalf of philatelic webmasters and their readers. A Quarter-Century at a Glance 2001 PWO is founded to promote philately through philatelic webmastering. 2008 PWO and AIJP present a joint philatelic webmastering initiative at EFIRO, Bucharest. 2022 PWO-EXPO brings together 72 exhibits from 50 participants in 22 countries. 2026 PWO marks its 25th anniversary and looks toward the next generation of philatelic publishing. 2001 · The founding idea 1. A Voice for Philatelic Webmasters PWO was founded in 2001 by Victor Manta, a Swiss-based philatelist and webmaster. Its original statement of aims defined the mission plainly: to promote, support and develop philately through philatelic webmastering. At a time when philatelic associations represented collectors, journalists and traditional publishers, a new kind of contributor was emerging: the collector who researched, wrote, illustrated, programmed and maintained a philatelic website. Such work combined philatelic knowledge with technical skills and often depended entirely on voluntary effort. PWO sought to give those webmasters a common identity and to encourage cooperation rather than isolation. The underlying conviction was that publishing good philatelic information online benefits the entire hobby. The founding text, Our Reasons and Goals , drew a careful distinction between philatelic webmasters and established professional groups. Journalists were represented by the International Association of Philatelic Journalists (AIJP), while publishers had their own associations. Philatelic webmasters formed a different community: collectors who combined knowledge of stamps and postal history with the skills needed to build and maintain a website. The document emphasized that most such webmasters were amateurs, working from personal enthusiasm and a desire to share what they knew. PWO therefore began with a practical question: how could this emerging community cooperate, improve its publications and gain recognition within organized philately? Read the original PWO reasons and goals The original PWO emblem, a familiar sign of international philatelic webmastering. International membership 2. A Worldwide Community The Internet offered philatelists something that printed publications could not always provide: the possibility of reaching readers around the world without waiting for the next issue of a journal or the next meeting of a society. PWO brought together the people who used that possibility to publish their research, collections and observations. The organization grew into a network of hundreds of philatelic authors and website creators. A PWO–AIJP announcement in 2008 referred to more than 350 members . By 2022, a PWO account of the planned virtual exhibition reported more than 400 members representing over 415 sites . These figures document different moments in PWO's history; they should not be read as a statement of present-day membership. There was never just one model of a PWO member's website. Some focused on the stamps or postal history of a particular country; others specialized in thematic collecting, exhibition material, research, illustrations or information for beginners. What united their authors was the belief that a carefully maintained website could make a genuine contribution to philatelic knowledge. Such websites also crossed boundaries between collectors, editors and researchers. An article published by one webmaster could be discovered by a reader in another country, cited by a specialist or used as a starting point for new research. This international exchange was among the lasting promises of philatelic webmastering. The members directory remains a visible record of that collective effort. Inevitably, the online world has changed: websites have moved, technologies have become obsolete and some early projects have disappeared. The historical value of the surviving links and documents has therefore grown with time. Explore the PWO Members List 350+ members documented in 2008 400+ members reported in 2022 Historical milestones from PWO publications Philatelic integrity 3. Against Illegal Stamps: The UPU Circulars One of PWO's most sustained activities has concerned illegal and abusive postage-stamp issues . These are not merely questions of taste or collecting fashion. Unauthorized products bearing the name of a country can be offered as genuine postal issues, confusing collectors and damaging confidence in the philatelic market. PWO's work has therefore combined documentation, public warning and critical discussion. A particularly valuable resource is the archive of Universal Postal Union (UPU) circulars concerning illegal issues. Rather than leave the reader to search through scattered notices, PWO has organized the material by country . This makes it possible to trace warnings associated with a particular postal administration and to consult historical evidence alongside newer information. The archive also preserves a chronological summary for 1996–2003 , based on an eight-page historical document. Its own introduction warns that the list was never exhaustive: an absence from the summary cannot establish that a disputed item was legitimate. Such qualifications are essential to responsible philatelic research. PWO's role has never been limited to reproducing official notices. Its articles have examined the strengths and weaknesses of tools intended to help collectors, including the WADP Numbering System (WNS) . A 2017 analysis by Victor Manta questioned whether an incomplete registration database could reliably be used to infer that every unlisted stamp was illegal. The argument illustrates an important principle of the organization's work: official information should be made accessible, but it must also be examined critically . For the collector, this distinction is practical. An official UPU circular is evidence of a communication from a postal administration; PWO's articles provide analysis and context. Neither should be confused with a blanket judgment about every item that resembles a stamp. The objective is better-informed collecting, not simply longer lists of prohibited material. UPU Circulars — country index · Historical circulars, 1996–2003 · The WNS & UPU Circulars in 2017 · PWO articles on illegal stamps An original illustration from PWO's archive of UPU circulars concerning illegal issues. Recognition and fair judging 4. International Website Competitions From the early years of online philately, PWO followed competitions in which philatelic websites were presented alongside more established forms of literature. The organization recorded results and experiences, including recognition received by PWO and its members. At the same time, PWO argued that a website cannot be judged simply as if it were a printed book. Its usefulness also depends on navigation, links, updating, accessibility and the ways in which readers can explore information. These features are not secondary technical details; they are part of the publication itself. The organization's historical competition reports discuss the practical consequences of exhibition rules, participation fees and judging arrangements. Such criticism has a constructive purpose: to make digital competition more transparent, more welcoming and more relevant to the medium. A revealing example appears in PWO's discussion of the FIP Literature Commission's 2005 article, The Role of Websites in Philatelic Literature Competitions . The debate was not merely about medals. It concerned the basic definition of a philatelic website as an exhibit: how should a jury evaluate navigation, links, continuous revision and the combination of research with presentation? PWO argued that digital publications deserved criteria appropriate to their medium. Its published responses are also a record of the sometimes difficult dialogue between pioneering web authors and established exhibition institutions. They should be read as PWO's documented position in that debate, not as a neutral account of every participant's view. Historical website competition reports · PWO on competitions Historical PWO award illustration preserved in the site's 2002 archive. Bucharest · 2008 5. EFIRO 2008: Philatelic Websites Enter the Exhibition Hall The international philatelic exhibition EFIRO 2008 in Bucharest offered PWO a particularly meaningful opportunity to demonstrate the value of philatelic publishing on the Internet. The exhibition commemorated the 150th anniversary of Romania’s first postage stamps , the celebrated Moldavian Bull Heads . The idea was to present selected web pages devoted to Romanian philately to visitors of a major international exhibition. PWO proposed and coordinated the initiative in cooperation with the Association Internationale des Journalistes Philatéliques (AIJP) and the exhibition organizers. It connected the work of online authors with the established world of philatelic exhibitions and journalism. According to the original PWO–AIJP announcement, the EFIRO organizing committee approved the project in April 2007 . In May 2007, representatives of the organizing committee and PWO met in Bern, at the International Bureau of the Universal Postal Union , to discuss the project's objectives and practical arrangements. The resulting presentation featured philatelic material from 11 webmasters representing several countries: Claude Wainstein, Dan Dobrescu, Dan Grecu, Fery Ambrus, Horst Scherer, Jay Carrigan, Laszlo Kallai, Mats Blückert, Paul Hirsch, Valentin Robu and Victor Manta. Their pages illustrated how the Internet could bring together diverse approaches to Romanian stamps and postal history. EFIRO 2008 was therefore more than an occasion to display websites. It was an early example of cooperation between a community of philatelic webmasters, an international association of philatelic journalists and the organizers of a major exhibition. It made visible an idea central to PWO since its foundation: online philatelic research deserves a place within the wider philatelic culture. Original PWO–AIJP press release · Introduction to the exhibition pages · The 11 participating webmasters The EFIRO 2008 poster, preserved in the PWO archive. 2022 · From principles to practice 6. PWO-EXPO 2022: An Exhibition Designed for the Web The original PWO-EXPO 2022 logo. After years of discussing the place of websites in international philatelic competitions, PWO helped put its ideas into practice through PWO-EXPO 2022 , an open virtual exhibition for philatelic websites and social media, organized in cooperation with Virtuafil. According to the organizers’ closing message, registration closed on 9 July 2022 and the exhibition concluded on 19 September 2022 . The original closing report records these figures and the jury’s award decisions; it remains available in the modernized PWO archive. The organizers sought to remove some of the barriers associated with conventional exhibitions and to recognize online publishing on its own terms. The competition brought together websites and social-media exhibits from across the world, with jury evaluation and public participation. 72 exhibits 50 participants 22 countries These figures are recorded in PWO's contemporary reports. The exhibition also received a special commemorative cancellation issued by Moldova Post. Its closing report recorded 12 Gold, 12 Silver and 21 Bronze medals , and acknowledged the volunteer international jury. Special Moldova Post cancellation dedicated to PWO-EXPO 2022. An original award illustration from the PWO-EXPO 2022 archive. PWO-EXPO was significant not only for its results but for what it demonstrated: an international philatelic exhibition could be organized around the actual characteristics of digital publications, rather than forcing them into a format inherited from print. Founding statement and participation rules · Exhibition report · Closing message and results (modernized test page) 2001–2026 7. Twenty-Five Years Later: The Mission Continues In 2001, a philatelic webmaster needed patience, curiosity and a willingness to learn new technical skills. In 2026, publishing tools are far more accessible, readers increasingly use mobile devices and automatic translation helps overcome language barriers. But technology alone does not make a valuable philatelic publication. Good philatelic work still rests on the same foundations: reliable evidence, accurate identification, clear illustrations, responsible interpretation and the readiness to correct mistakes. These are the qualities that make a website worth returning to, and worth preserving. PWO's own archive tells a second story, about the history of the Internet itself. Early websites were often personal initiatives sustained for years by unpaid effort. Some have disappeared; others survive only because their creators continued to care for them. Preserving competition records, official documents, reports and the debates surrounding online publishing is consequently a form of historical stewardship. Looking ahead, PWO's founding questions remain relevant. How can trustworthy philatelic information be found amid a growing volume of online material? How should digital publications be evaluated fairly? And how can collectors of different generations and languages continue to learn from one another? The answers will evolve, but the need for an independent, internationally minded philatelic community remains. The first quarter-century of PWO is an occasion to thank the philatelic webmasters who have contributed their time, knowledge and enthusiasm. It is also an invitation to a new generation to continue publishing, questioning, sharing and exploring. Twenty-five years of PWO celebrate not only an organization, but the philatelists who believed that the Internet could open new horizons for stamp collecting. title: PWO Awards
text: The PWO Award The Philatelic Webmasters Organization ( PWO ) proposes an Annual PWO Award to philatelic sites that distinguished themselves by something special, unique or very attractive. For this award there weren't elaborated precise criteria or rules. Even if it's an annual award, it won't necessarily be attributed during a given year, and a site can be also awarded retroactively. Any philatelic webmaster, PWO member or not, may apply for it. PWO can also award sites that haven't applied for it, and this at its full discretion. The very few sites and webmasters that could be awarded, will have the right to display the image shown below: and will link it to this page. This page will in the future list the sites and the webmasters that were awarded. The attribution of this award will be decided by the PWO Executive Council, who will freely consult philatelic webmasters specialized in philatelic domains close to that of candidate's site. In order to apply, send us an e-mail , in which please specify : the name of your site the URL of your site your full name the country where you live something about your person and your philatelic interests (optional).
